results.name: AI providers: accept a ready-made sprite sheet from the remote (animated)
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · built at 1287dc5; 101 unit pass + verified live end to end

Why this exists

SOMET-327 made the local side refuse frames > 1. That reasoning was about the wrong machine. This side prepares the request, waits, receives and stores; the other machine draws the image or sprite.

Delivered

  • services/spriteSheet.js — PNG size from the IHDR chunk, grid resolution, manifest arithmetic. No image library.
  • Migration 1714440380000 — sheet_layout / sheet_columns / sheet_rows / sheet_directions, all nullable so an unconfigured provider behaves exactly as before.
  • {{frames}} placeholder so the template tells the remote how many frames to draw.
  • Stores atlas.png + atlas.json in sprite-gen's layout, returning {atlas_key, manifest_key, frames} — the admin UI's animated path works unchanged.
  • Settings UI: layout selector + grid fields. The stale "remote cannot animate" warning is replaced by one that fires only when a provider has no grid configured.

Verified live

Real 512×1280 PNG through the real routes → done, 32/32 frames, atlas and manifest both served by the asset route, cell [128,160], all 8 facings, every rect 128×160, and the remote received batch_size: 4.

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ Animated entity sprite via a remote provider.
  • ✅ Manifest satisfies spriteAtlas.js — tests resolve it through the renderer's own lookup logic.
  • ✅ Uneven grid rejected with the actual pixel size; nothing stored.
  • ✅ Non-PNG rejected.
  • ✅ Static frames = 1 unchanged.
  • ✅ Full round trip documented in docs/ai-providers.md, linked from README.md.

Not verified

Browser rendering of the new grid fields, and an animated sprite actually moving in game — still blocked on the same environment issue as SOMET-333.

results.name: The per-file test timeout is too tight for bcrypt, so the suite reports a spurious failure under load
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-15 · merged 7b7952a, pushed; 2286 tests / 0 failures under 12-core saturation

Symptom

npm test intermittently reported tests/auth_routes.test.js timing out after 20000ms — only on a busy machine, three times this session (load 9.7, 12.7, 26), passing in isolation every time. The real cost was that each occurrence had to be explained away, which trains people to ignore red.

Root cause — no defect, a mis-set budget

Measured: bcryptjs at COST_FACTOR = 12 takes ~547ms per hash (3ms at cost 4), and auth_routes.test.js makes 17 register/login calls — so bcrypt is essentially 100% of its runtime, 6.1–7.0s idle across three runs. bcrypt at cost 12 is deliberately slow; node --test runs 218 files in parallel, so per-file wall time moves with machine load. Nothing was broken except the budget.

Resolution

--test-timeout 20000 → 60000. tests/helpers/advisoryLock.js's comment, which justified LOCK_WAIT_MS = 6000 by arithmetic against the old 20000, corrected so it cannot mislead — and 6000 deliberately not re-derived, since nine sequential 6s waits would fill even the larger budget and its job is to bound one acquisition.

Rejected: lowering the cost factor under test

A 60× speedup was available and refused. auth_passwords.test.js pins cost 12 by reading the digits out of a real hash, so a test-only cost would have disarmed that guard — the same failure mode SOMET-344 had just been spent repairing. It would also have introduced the codebase's first NODE_ENV-dependent behaviour into its one security-critical path. src/auth/passwords.js has a zero-line diff.

Verification

A load-dependent failure cannot be proven fixed by an idle run, so both arms ran under deliberate 12-core saturation: the new budget at load 31 produced no bcrypt timeout; the old budget at load 21 timed out both auth_passwords.test.js and auth_routes.test.js — two files, not the one that had been showing up. Final run: 2286 tests, 0 failures, load 23.4.

Reported, not folded in

Both saturated runs also tripped a shared-database race — the entry-world is_entry window on one, the village-crossing write floor on the other. Different races on each arm, present with and without this change; live data verified correct afterwards. Load makes them likelier; this change does not.

results.name: Three backend collision tests were left behind by the feet-footprint change and now assert nothing
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-15 · merged 48c5a33, pushed; backend suite 2280 tests / 0 failures

Symptom

Three backend tests failed on main from the moment SOMET-337 landed: the player wall-clamp test in authority_world.test.js, the cornered-creature test in creature_skittish.test.js, and the fresh-stall-window test in guardChaseGiveUp.test.js.

Root cause — not a gameplay bug

SOMET-337 introduced FOOTPRINT_SCALE = 0.5: movement resolves against a half-size feet box instead of the full sprite box, so every actor stands 16px closer to a wall (12px for a 48px creature). All three fixtures had placed their actor flush against a wall under the OLD geometry, so under the new footprint the scenarios no longer set up. Two failed on assertions labelled "precondition"; the third reported x = 40, the correct answer for an ordinary unobstructed step, while still carrying "clamps" in its name.

The part that was worse than stale

guardChaseGiveUp's h2 sat 80px east of the post, meeting its own stated requirement ("blocked from its very first tick") only under the full-box footprint. With the halved footprint the guard could sidestep east, so its first tick delivered movement and the else branch zeroed _chaseStall incidentally. Probed both ways: with the reset deleted the counter read 38 at t0 and 0 at t1 and the test still passed; under scale 1.0 the same mutation gave 38 → 39 → dropped and it failed. SOMET-337 did not just break the setup — it disarmed a working regression guard, which a green suite would never have revealed.

Resolution

  1. Player start 30 → 50 (footprint east face 98), expecting 51.99. Clamp boundary mapped empirically first: 30 steps freely, 42 and 50 clamp, 60 is already inside.
  2. Creature spawn BOX → BOX − 12, so the footprint's west face is flush with the wall.
  3. Guard stall window filled by a bounded condition loop instead of a fixed tick count, and h2 moved due north so there is no free sidestep.
  4. One pin on FOOTPRINT_SCALE/WALL_EPS whose message names all three fixtures and what to re-derive. The fixtures keep hand-computed literals deliberately — a value derived from the same constant as the code agrees with a wrong constant.

Only src change: exporting those two constants for the pin. No behaviour change, so parity with the frontend's systems/movement.js is untouched.

Carry forward

Changing a shared geometry constant can silently invalidate the scenarios of tests in files that never mention it. Some of the resulting failures are stale numbers; some are disarmed guards, and they look identical. Anything touching FOOTPRINT_SCALE, tile size or actor box dimensions should re-run the mutations named in the pin, not merely the suite.

results.name: Slice D — projectile augments and explosive ammo
results.description_html:
Backlog · 2026-08-15 · filed: the half of the original request slice C deferred — "bows can carry frost", "arrows can be explosive"

Why this exists

SOMET-332 shipped augment stones for MELEE weapons only. The augment rider is resolved and carried correctly by activeWeaponType, but the four damage sites in backend/src/authority/projectiles.js never read it, so a bow would socket an augment and add nothing. Rather than half-wire it, slice C made isCompatible REFUSE the socket — an explicit rule instead of silent inertness. This ticket is what lifts that restriction.

The original request asked for both halves: "same with arrows, or bows — arrows can be explosive". Neither is delivered yet.

Part 1 — the augment packet on projectile hits

Carry weapon.augment onto the projectile at spawn() (snapshotted at launch, like damage, vfxTrail and originLift already are — the shooter can be dead before it lands), then apply the bonus as a SECOND packet at all four damage sites: the two AoE sites in _detonate (creatures ~:241, players ~:275) and the two direct-hit sites in step() (creatures ~:373, players ~:411).

The ordering hazard. Unlike the melee path, these sites do not share one loop with one hp<=0 check. damageCreatureById applies damage AND resolves the kill internally, deleting the creature. So a second packet applied afterwards either targets a deleted creature or double-counts the kill. Decide the rule explicitly — most likely apply the augment packet FIRST and let the main packet's existing kill check stay the single authority, mirroring what applyMeleeArc does.

Then delete the melee-only branch in services/stones.js's isCompatible. The test 'an augment stone is refused by a projectile weapon, not silently inert' in backend/tests/augment_stones.test.js is pinned to the current behaviour and will fail — that failure is the reminder, and updating it is part of this ticket.

Part 2 — explosive ammo

ProjectileSim.spawn reads only weapon.*. The ammo_type_id item_type contributes NOTHING to the shot it becomes, so "explosive arrows" cannot be authored at all today — it is a real change to the spawn merge, not a config flip.

Merge the ammo row's aoe_radius / impact_behavior_id (slice B) into the spawned projectile. Note: item_types_aoe_pierce_check (a detonating projectile may not also pierce > 1) is a row-level CHECK — it constrains the weapon row and the ammo row separately, but nothing validates the MERGED result. A piercing bow firing detonating arrows would slip past it.

Part 3 — make max_range real

Slice B created impact_behaviors.detonate_at accepting 'contact' and 'max_range' but seeded only 'contact', because the engine detonates an AoE shot on its FIRST contact of ANY kind — including running out of range — and so cannot tell the two apart. A guard test in backend/tests/weapon_option_catalogs.test.js fails if a 'max_range' row is seeded before the engine can honour it.

Splitting the two is what makes "magic can be explosive when the distance ends" (from the original request) authorable. Doing so means separating the range-expiry path from the contact path in step().

Acceptance criteria

  1. An augment stone sockets into a projectile weapon and its bonus lands, in its own element, on direct hits AND on AoE detonations.
  2. A creature killed by the augment portion of a projectile hit is reported killed exactly once.
  3. The melee-only restriction is removed and its pinning test updated, not deleted.
  4. Explosive ammo detonates when the AMMO row says so, with the weapon carrying no aoe of its own.
  5. A piercing weapon firing detonating ammo is rejected or resolved by an explicit documented rule — not left to slip past the row-level CHECK.
  6. detonate_at = 'max_range' behaves differently from 'contact', and slice B's guard test is updated to allow it.

Depends on

SOMET-332 (augment rider, stone_mode) and SOMET-329 (impact_behaviors). Both currently To Review on feat/weapon-option-catalogs.

results.name: AI providers follow-up: UI for pinning a type to a provider permanently
results.description_html:
Closes the gap left by SOMET-331. Filed rather than silently absorbed.

What exists already

SOMET-328 shipped the storage and the resolver: entity_types and tile_types carry ai_provider_mode (default | local | provider) and ai_provider_id, and resolveGenerationTarget honours them with full test coverage including the ON DELETE SET NULL degradation. Nothing writes those columns.

What SOMET-331 shipped instead

A per-generation selector. Choosing a provider affects that one job and is forgotten. I deliberately did not persist it on selector change, because that would make one control mean two things — "generate this one with X" and "permanently change this type's default" — with the second happening silently.

What this ticket is

A deliberate, separate control for the persistent pin. Shape is open; the obvious candidate is a field in the type's own edit form (beside prompt / render_mode), saved with the rest of the type, rather than in the generation panel.

Acceptance criteria

  • An admin can set a type's generation service to Default / Local sprite-gen / a named provider, and it persists.
  • Setting the pin is a save, not a side effect of changing a dropdown in the generation panel.
  • The generation panel's per-job selector still overrides the pin for that job only (precedence is already implemented and tested).
  • A type pinned to a provider that is later deleted shows as Default rather than as a dangling reference (the column is already ON DELETE SET NULL).
  • The PUT /api/entity-types/:id and tile-type equivalents accept and validate the two columns; an unknown mode is rejected (the DB CHECK already rejects it — the route should too, with a readable 400).
  • Round-trip test: set a pin, reload the editor, the pin is shown.

results.name: DB tests leak fixture worlds and flip is_entry, making multi-file runs order-dependent
results.description_html:
Several DB-backed suites create throwaway worlds (zzTestAlpha, zzTestBeta, respawn-test-*) and some flip the global worlds.is_entry flag onto them. Two consequences, both observed on 2026-08-14:

1. Multi-file runs fail non-deterministically

Running tests/mapService*.test.js tests/*decoration*.test.js tests/chunk*.test.js tests/village*.test.js tests/biome*.test.js tests/authority_collision.test.js tests/map_spec*.test.js tests/seed_map*.test.js tests/guard_rescue_leash.test.js produces a failure that moves between runs:

  • One run: zzTestBeta: spawn/merchant/guard posts collide -- tiles ["11,11","11,12","11,11","11,12"] (villageScreenBudget_db.test.js)
  • Another run, same file set, without any source change: the entry world "zzTestAlpha" must have exactly one village (SOMET-153's original criterion), got 0

Both files pass in isolation. node --test runs files concurrently, so these suites race each other over shared rows.

2. Leaked fixture rows accumulate

Cleanup runs after the assertions rather than in a finally, so any failed assertion leaks its world. As of 2026-08-14 the dev DB holds 9 orphaned respawn-test-* worlds from SOMET-309's suite. Harmless individually, but they accumulate and they pollute any query that scans worlds.

Why this matters beyond tidiness

A test that flips is_entry can silently redirect any OTHER test that looks up "the entry world" onto a 16×16 fixture. SOMET-339's egress guard originally did exactly that lookup and had to be rewritten mid-implementation to read the checked-in map specs instead, precisely so a concurrent suite could not make it measure the wrong world and pass while proving nothing. That is a guard that would have rotted silently — the failure mode this project already has a documented history of.

Suggested direction

  • Move fixture cleanup into finally so a failed assertion cannot leak a world.
  • Restore is_entry to its previous owner in cleanup, rather than leaving it on a fixture.
  • Consider unique per-run fixture names (the respawn-test-* suite already does this and never collides with itself), or serialising the suites that contend over is_entry.
  • One-off: delete the 9 leaked respawn-test-* worlds. Their FKs cascade.

Provenance

Found 2026-08-14 while verifying SOMET-339 had not regressed anything. Confirmed pre-existing: the same file set fails on main without that change, on a different test.

results.name: creature_respawns cascade-deletes from worlds but is missing from the clear-maps CASCADES list
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-15 · cherry-picked to main as 1c4e2d7, pushed; shared checkout never touched

Symptom

backend/tests/clear_maps.test.js — "every table with an ON DELETE CASCADE FK to worlds is named in CASCADES" failed on main. The scanner found 12 cascading tables; the pinned list named 11. The extra one was creature_respawns.

Root cause

SOMET-309 added creature_respawns with world_id ... references 'worlds', onDelete: 'CASCADE' (migration 1714440330000) and did not add it to CASCADES in backend/scripts/clear-maps.js.

That list is the text make clear-maps and make reseed-map print in their confirmation prompt, immediately before an irreversible DELETE FROM worlds. A table missing from it means the prompt understates what is about to be destroyed. Resolution

  1. creature_respawns (creatures queued to respawn into the worlds being deleted) added to CASCADES. Losing this table costs nothing — the queue only holds creatures due to return to a world that is itself being deleted — but the list's value is that it is exhaustive: the harmless entries are what make the alarming ones credible.
  2. Pinned expectation updated to 12, deliberately not relaxed into a subset check, so a future cascading table is still noticed rather than tolerated.
  3. Mutation-verified twice; the two assertions fail on different messages, so each is independently load-bearing.

Cherry-picked rather than merged. The working branch had accumulated three other sessions' commits (SOMET-326/337/338) because the shared checkout was sitting on it while they worked; merging would have published their work in a shape they had not chosen. The cherry-pick carried exactly the two intended files, and the whole operation ran in a throwaway worktree.

results.name: New players cannot leave the starting village — Vale Crossing's only gate is blocked by decorations
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-15 · merged to main at 71cd661; live-verified — a fresh character walks from the village spawn to the eastern map edge, reachable tiles 9 → 13,772

A new character spawns inside Vale Crossing (the entry world's village) and cannot walk out. The village's only gate is at row 46, col 49, E edge. GET /chunk reports blocking decorations at (46,50) and (46,51), plus (45,50) and (47,50) — i.e. the tiles immediately outside the gate and the ones flanking them.

Evidence

Flood-fill from the village spawn point reaches 9 tiles. Ignoring decorations entirely, the same flood-fill reaches 15,873 tiles. Confirmed live against the running dev stack by driving the WebSocket authority as a client: pushing east stops hard at x=4936 on every row tried, all four rows.

Root cause (confirmed 2026-08-14)

isExcludedBlockerCell (backend/src/services/mapService.js) excluded blocking decorations only inside the village footprint and within Chebyshev radius 1 of the entry spawn. The tiles outside the gate edge were unprotected, and the clump field placed a blocker at col 50 on every row 44–48. Carved paths, which are excluded for all decorations, do not reach this village at all (zero path cells in rows 40–59 × cols 40–64), so nothing else was protecting the corridor. Latent since decorations shipped; SOMET-335 moved the entry spawn inside the village and turned it fatal.

Fix

isExcludedBlockerCell now also spares a corridor running outward from every village's gate, DECO_CELL tiles long with one tile of lateral slack. New tests/entry_world_egress_db.test.js flood-fills from every spec-declared entry spawn and fails if it cannot reach the map edge — asserting the outcome rather than the cause, since this has broken three times through different causes. The generator diff is exactly 6 cells removed and none added.

Impact

This is the first thing a new player experiences. They spawn, they cannot leave, and there are no creatures inside the village — so the game is unplayable from a fresh account. It is unrelated to creature respawn (SOMET-309); it was found while validating that ticket, which is why respawn had to be verified in Old Trailhead instead of the entry world.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Register a new account and create a character (spawns in Vale Crossing).
  2. Walk east toward the gate at row 46, col 49.
  3. Expected: the player exits the village and can reach open world and creatures.
  4. Actual (before the fix): movement stops at x=4936; the reachable area is 9 tiles.

Provenance

Found 2026-08-14 by the independent validator for SOMET-309, against main at 50cc237.

results.name: Tree entity type is 777x888 px — one decoration fills half the viewport
results.description_html:
Backlog · 2026-08-14 · found while browser-verifying SOMET-319; pre-existing, not caused by it

Symptom

The Tree entity type carries display_width = 777, display_height = 888. drawEntity uses those directly as the drawn sprite size, so every Tree renders as a 777×888 px box — over half the 1280×720 viewport, from one decoration on one tile.

Compare the sane rows in the same table: Stone 48×48, IceRock 48×48, dead_tree 56×92, pine_tree 64×104. 777/888 reads as placeholder keyboard-mash typed into the Entity Types admin.

Where it bites

Tree spawns at chance 0.2 on earth, grass, leafs, dirt, and backend/seeds/data/biomes.js lists it in the flora of several biomes including Verdant Jungle. It was NOT visible during the SOMET-319 verification only because the entry world (Catacomb Threshold) is built from rocks/crypt_floor/cobblestone/sand, which spawn Stone instead. Any grass or earth world shows it.

It also renders as a flat colour rectangle rather than a sprite — render_mode = 'rect', no image, no sprite — which is expected until sprites are generated for it, but it does mean the oversized box is a solid green slab.

Fix — data, not code

The seeding migration 1714440003000_create_environment_types.js inserts Tree with no display dimensions, so 777×888 was entered later through the admin UI. The correction therefore belongs in the row, not in a migration: set it to something in line with its siblings (pine_tree's 64×104 is the closest analogue). Deliberately not applied by an agent — it is a live row in the shared dev DB and the target size is a product call.

Check while you are there

Worth scanning the whole table for other out-of-range display dimensions from the same admin flow; a numeric sanity bound on the Entity Types form would stop the next one.

results.name: Collision footprint is the actor's full body box — characters stop ~32px short of a blocking tile
results.description_html:
Backlog · 2026-08-14 · opened as the disclosed follow-up to SOMET-319; needs a feel judgement before anyone codes it

What

With the render anchor corrected (SOMET-319) the character's feet now mark its true position — which makes the remaining gap visible: you stop about 32 world px (0.32 of a tile) short of a blocking tile's edge.

Why

Not a bug — a direct consequence of the footprint model. resolveMove clamps the box's leading face to the tile boundary, and the box is the actor's whole body (player 64×64, creature 48×48) against a 100px tile. So the anchor — now drawn at the feet — comes to rest half a box-width from the boundary: 32px for a player, 24px for a creature.

The decision to make first

Whether that standoff actually reads as wrong in play. It was invisible before, because the sprite was drawn half a tile forward and the gap was hidden under the figure. Judge it in the running game before changing anything; a smaller footprint is a gameplay-feel change, not a correctness fix.

If it is changed

  • Shrinking the footprint to a feet box (e.g. 32×32 → 16px standoff) is the obvious lever, and the swept clamp's preconditions (tile-aligned walls, sub-tile steps) survive it.
  • Both mirrored copies must change identically: frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/systems/movement.js and backend/src/authority/collision.js are byte-for-byte duplicates with no shared module. Divergence = client/server rubber-banding.
  • The same function moves creatures, so any change alters mob movement and gate-threading too — a narrower footprint lets actors slip through gaps they currently cannot (the 100px gate case).
  • Golden-vector tests exist in both suites and would need new expected numbers.

results.name: migrate:up is blocked on this database by pgmigrations rows recorded out of filename order
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · applied to the shared dev DB; migrate:up works; merged 1b4f62c, pushed

Symptom

npm run migrate:up refused on the shared dev database: Not run migration 1714440171000_fix_village_spawn_inside_walls is preceding already run migration 1714440172000_fix_legacy_creature_gold. SOMET-335's migration only landed because the dev stack's bind-mount watcher applied it.

Root cause

The message misleads: every migration had run. node-pg-migrate reads the ledger with ORDER BY run_on, id and its checkOrder zips it positionally against the files sorted by filename, throwing at the first differing index — and assuming an unrun migration is the only possible cause. Two other causes were present:

  1. Out-of-order application — three inversions where a later-timestamped branch was applied before an earlier one merged.
  2. A renumbered migration — 1714440300000_creature_respawns was renamed to 1714440330000_creature_respawns in 3462095, explicitly because SOMET-335's 1714440320000 landed on main first. The ledger still held the old name, so the new one read as never-run. Not cosmetic: that migration is a bare pgm.createTable and the table already existed with both named indexes, so the first migrate:up past the ordering errors would have failed with 42P07.

The repository was never at fault — a fresh database applies all 96 in filename order. This was ledger drift, so only the ledger was repaired.

Resolution

backend/scripts/repair-migration-order.js: pure planRepair split from the I/O, dry-run by default, mandatory backup. Never runs, re-runs or reverts a migration; never inserts or deletes a row. A genuinely unrun file is reported and left for migrate:up; a recorded name with no file is reported and left alone; an ambiguous rename blocks outright. Deliberately not --no-check-order, which would silence the real condition the check exists for.

The reorder permutes ids and run_on values already present — both multisets survive exactly — but it does change which row carries which timestamp, which is why the backup is mandatory.

Applied to the shared database; migrate:up now reports "No migrations to run! Migrations complete!"

Known, not fixed here

This is a cure, not a vaccine. While branches run in parallel against one shared database, timestamps will keep colliding and migrations will keep being applied out of order. Also left open: creature_respawns is missing from the CASCADES list (SOMET-309's, failing on main today).

results.name: The entry world's entry_spawn is not its village spawn — nothing validates the invariant
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged ba0101f, pushed; self-reviewed, evidence triad in the close-out comment

Symptom

backend/tests/villageScreenBudget_db.test.js — "the entry world has a village and its entry_spawn IS that village spawn" failed against the live database. Expected { x: 4650, y: 4550 } (villages.spawn_x/spawn_y), actual { x: 6450, y: 6450 } (worlds.entry_spawn), world Vale Crossing.

Root cause

Not database drift — the checked-in spec itself was wrong. backend/seeds/maps/hub-vale.map.json, world hub (Vale Crossing, is_entry: true) declared entry_spawn (6450,6450) = tile (64,64), the geometric centre of the 128x128 map, while its village box sat at rows 44..47 / cols 44..49 with spawn (4650,4550) = tile (45,46) — ~20 tiles apart.

It was wrong before SOMET-307 too: at 96x96 it was entry_spawn (4850,4850) vs village spawn (3050,2950). SOMET-307 translated both correctly by the same +16-tile delta, so the resize was not the cause — it faithfully carried a pre-existing inconsistency forward.

Migrations 1714440175000 (SOMET-282, delivering SOMET-153's original criterion) and 1714440201000 (SOMET-296) both wrote entry_spawn from villages.spawn_x/spawn_y so the two could not disagree. Neither lasts: a migration runs once, and applyMapSpec upserts entry_spawn from the spec on every re-seed, silently undoing them.

The real defect was that validateMapSpec never checked it. It verified exactly one is_entry world and validated village geometry, but nothing related the entry world's entry_spawn to the village it declares — so a spec could be authored, resized or re-seeded with the two disagreeing and every gate passed.

Player impact

A new character's first join, and every subsequent respawn, landed ~20 tiles outside the starting village — no guards, no merchant, in open terrain with hostiles.

Resolution

  1. validateMapSpec now rejects a spec whose is_entry world declares a village its entry_spawn is not the spawn of, and requires entry_spawn once a village is declared. Only well-formed villages are compared against, so a malformed one keeps its own more accurate error instead of throwing.
  2. hub-vale's entry_spawn corrected to (4650,4550); all three checked-in specs pass the gate.
  3. map_spec_fixtures.test.js already runs the validator over the real specs, so authored data is gated, not just fixtures — reverting the spec value turns it red with the exact coordinates.
  4. Migration 1714440320000 repairs rows already written, in any environment.
  5. Six mutations of the new check, each killing a different named test.

results.name: AI providers follow-up: async queue mode (ComfyUI-style submit + poll + fetch)
results.description_html:
Todo · 2026-08-14 · queued: follow-up, do not start before the sync path works

Deliberately deferred out of the core epic. Only start this once the sync path works end to end.

Why it is separate

The core adapter assumes one POST returns the image. ComfyUI does not work that way: POST /prompt returns a prompt_id, you poll GET /history/{prompt_id} until the output appears, then fetch the file from GET /view?filename=.... Supporting both roughly doubles the adapter, so the sync path ships first and this plugs into the same module.

Scope

  • Add a mode column to ai_providers: sync (default, existing behaviour) or async.
  • For async, add the three configurable pieces the poll loop needs: submit-response id pointer, poll path template, and result-file pointer — same generic philosophy as models_pointer, no ComfyUI-specific code.
  • Poll with backoff and an overall deadline; a job that never completes fails rather than polling forever.
  • Settings tab exposes the mode switch and reveals the async fields only when selected.

Acceptance criteria

  • Against a stubbed ComfyUI-shaped service, an async provider produces the same normalized job document as a sync one.
  • A never-completing job hits the deadline and fails with a clear message; no orphaned poll timer survives.
  • Switching an existing provider from sync to async does not break it or lose its template.
  • Existing sync-provider tests stay green unchanged.

results.name: AI providers: SSRF + secret hardening, docs, end-to-end browser verification
results.description_html:
In Progress · 2026-08-15 · BLOCKED: hardening + docs done at c45bef5; browser verification cannot run in this environment

Closing slice. The feature lets an admin make the backend issue arbitrary outbound HTTP, so the SSRF work is scoped as its own task.

✅ Done

  • services/safeFetch.js — scheme allowlist enforced at call time as well as save time, embedded credentials refused, redirects capped at 3 with every hop re-validated and the auth header dropped on a cross-origin hop, streaming size cap, redacted URLs in error strings.
  • Wired into both outbound paths (discovery and generation).
  • docs/ai-providers.md — registration, placeholders, pointer syntax, worked A1111 and OpenAI-compatible templates, limitations, security.
  • AGENTS.md trust note.
  • 78/78 backend AI-provider tests pass, 10 of them new for the guard.

Deliberate deviation

Private address ranges are not blocked. The intended target is a LAN machine, so blocking RFC1918 would defeat the feature. Documented position: admin is a trusted role here by design.

🚧 Blocked — not done

results.name: Slice C — augment stones (frost swords, explosive arrows)
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · PARTIAL — 5 of 7 ACs. Melee augments shipped (0c9bdc2); projectile augments and explosive ammo deferred, see below

Goal

A sword can carry frost or fire that adds to its damage. Arrows can be explosive. Socketing was replace-only — activeWeaponType overwrote the host weapon's element, damage, cooldown and mana_cost with the stone's, so a fire stone in a long sword made the sword cast fire rather than making a flaming sword.

Built

item_types.stone_mode ('replace' | 'augment', NOT NULL DEFAULT 'replace') and bonus_damage. The augment branch of activeWeaponType is checked BEFORE the replace branch — an augment also has a non-null element and would otherwise fall straight into the overwrite it exists to avoid — and returns the host weapon untouched plus an augment rider.

Two damage packets, never blended. The weapon's own damage in its element, then the augment's bonus in the augment's element, so frost on a physical sword is resisted as frost. Applied inside applyMeleeArc's existing single loop: one hp<=0 check per target, so a creature finished off by the bonus is reported killed exactly once.

DEFERRED — read before reviewing

Augments are melee-only. The four damage sites in projectiles.js do not read the packet, so isCompatible REFUSES an augment socket into a projectile weapon rather than accepting it and doing nothing — an explicit rule beats silent inertness. A test pins the refusal and will fail when projectiles learn the packet.

"Arrows can be explosive" and "bows can carry frost" from the original request are NOT delivered. Needs a follow-up ticket covering: the four projectile damage sites, and the ammo merge in ProjectileSim.spawn (which reads only weapon.*, so an ammo_type_id row contributes nothing to the shot it becomes — note item_types_aoe_pierce_check applies to the MERGED result).

Acceptance criteria

  1. Every existing spell stone behaves exactly as before. — ✅ DEFAULT 'replace', no content migration
  2. An augment adds bonus elemental damage without changing the weapon's own damage, cooldown or mana cost. — ✅
  3. The bonus packet is mitigated by the AUGMENT's element. — ✅ proven by comparing ice- vs fire-resistant targets against a physical sword
  4. An augment stone gains XP and levels on a landed hit. — ✅ trap 1, pinned
  5. Explosive ammo detonates on impact when the ammo row says so. — ❌ DEFERRED
  6. Buff stones unaffected, still equipped-only. — ✅ stoneKind checks augment before element, so no buff stone changes class
  7. Unsocketing cleanly removes the bonus, including the destroy roll. — ⚠️ holds by construction (unsocket clears socketedStoneTypeId, so the plain weapon is returned) but is NOT covered by a test

Traps

  1. Stone XP. CONFIRMED and closed — stoneHit is gated on w.stoneItemId != null, set only by the replace branch; the augment branch now sets it too.
  2. Ammo contributes nothing to a shot. CONFIRMED, deferred with the projectile work.
  3. The stone shape constraint blocks augment stones. WRONG. The constraint is item_types_stone_kind_check and it never blocked them. It did allow an augment with NULL bonus_damage — a stone that sockets and adds nothing — so it was TIGHTENED, not relaxed. Both new constraints verified non-vacuous against the live schema.

Also open

No browser pass. Stones are not authorable in the Items admin at all (the category select offers weapon/armor/ammo only), so a new augment stone can currently only be created by migration — pre-existing, but it blocks authoring.

results.name: Slice B — bounded catalog tables for weapon options
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · built on feat/weapon-option-catalogs (161d716); element was never free text — a hidden CHECK would have made the catalog decorative

Goal

An admin authoring a weapon should pick from a constrained list, not type a string or tune a raw pixel number. Four new catalog tables, each seeded from the values already in use, each surfaced as a select in the Items admin.

Tables — all built

  1. attack_origins — name, height_fraction, label, sort_order. Slice A's CHECK dropped and replaced by an FK. attackOrigin.js now takes its fractions from this table, so editing height_fraction actually moves where attacks launch from.
  2. elements — name, color, tint_color, damage_type, on_hit_effect. Two colour columns, not one: they were two different client literals serving two different roles (body colour vs impact wash), and collapsing them would have restyled every impact burst.
  3. projectile_shapes — dart / bolt / orb / fireball, the four distinct radii already in the catalog. Supplies projectile_radius when set.
  4. impact_behaviors — single_hit / pierce / detonate_on_contact. Supplies pierce, and gates whether aoe_radius is honoured.

The hidden constraint

This ticket asserted element was free text. It was not: 1714440017000_items_inventory.js already pinned it to a hardcoded five-name CHECK. Adding the FK without dropping that CHECK left the catalog decorative — an admin could add an elements row and still be unable to use it. Caught by attempting the write against the live schema. Dropped in the migration, restored on the way down, guarded by a test.

Acceptance criteria

  1. All four tables exist, seeded from live values, every existing row migrates without behaviour change. — done, verified by psql against the dev DB
  2. element and attack_origin are FKs; an unknown value cannot be written. — done
  3. Adding a new element requires no frontend change. — proven in a rolled-back transaction: a new void element was immediately usable on a weapon, which the old CHECK would have refused. Colour comes from the catalog; both client literals now delegate to one module.
  4. The Items admin presents all four as dropdowns. — built; browser confirmation open for the reviewer
  5. Deleting a referenced catalog row fails loudly (RESTRICT). — proven: DELETE refused by item_types_element_fkey

Scope call, narrower than sketched

The ticket asked for impact vs max_range impact behaviours. The engine detonates on FIRST contact of ANY kind — including running out of range — so it cannot tell them apart. Seeding both would put a value in the catalog the engine silently ignores, which is the class of defect this epic exists to remove. The column accepts max_range for slice C; no row uses it, and a test fails if one is seeded early.

Deferred, disclosed

elements.on_hit_effect is data but the runtime still reads effects.js's own table; a guard test fails if the two disagree in either direction. Creature attack_element and ability element still reference element names without an FK.

Reviewer: the open item

No browser pass. Open the Items admin, confirm all four dropdowns populate from /api/weapon-catalogs, and confirm a projectile still draws in its element colour — the palette now arrives on joined rather than being compiled in.

results.name: AI providers: route generation through the resolved provider + per-type override
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · built at e5f4475; 15/15 pass incl. 2 DB tests

Wires the adapter into the live generation path. The existing local sprite-gen path stays intact when no provider is active.

Resolved design decisions

  • Sentinel: an ai_provider_mode enum column (default | local | provider) beside the nullable FK — not a reserved row. One nullable FK cannot distinguish "follow the active provider" from "always local", and collapsing them lets activating a provider silently take over types deliberately pinned to local.
  • JOB_ID_RE was NOT widened. It already permits underscores, so rmt_<hex> passes the SOMET-182 traversal guard unchanged.

Delivered

  • Migration 1714440370000 — ai_provider_mode + ai_provider_id (ON DELETE SET NULL) on entity_types and tile_types.
  • services/generationTarget.js — pure resolveGenerationTarget, four levels: request → type → active → local.
  • Remote branch in startGenerationJob; sprite_sets.backend records remote:<name>.
  • fetchJobDocument prefix dispatch across all three /api/*-jobs/:jobId routes.

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ No active provider + no override → unchanged sprite-gen path.
  • ✅ Active provider routes tile and entity jobs to the adapter.
  • ✅ A type pinned to local stays local while a provider is active.
  • ✅ request > type > active > local, all four levels asserted.
  • ✅ Traversal guard intact for ../ and encoded traversal, with and without the prefix.
  • ✅ Deleting a referenced provider blanks the pin and degrades to the fallback (DB test in a rolled-back transaction).

Note for the reviewer

The full backend suite has 2 pre-existing failures (clear_maps.test.js CASCADES scanner, seed_map_db.test.js waypoint/guard) unrelated to this branch and not bisected against main.

results.name: AI providers: remote image adapter (template substitution, response decode, MinIO write)
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · built at e38981a; 20/20 pass. Static-image only — see scope limit.

Sync mode: one POST, image in the response. ComfyUI-style async queue polling is SOMET-334.

⚠️ Scope limit discovered while building

A single sync call returns a single image, so a remote provider produces a static image (image_key, the shape tile and object panels consume). It cannot produce the multi-frame directional atlas animated creature sprites need. frames > 1 now fails the job with an explanatory error instead of silently returning a still. Animated generation still requires local sprite-gen. Remote-driven animation would need SOMET-334 or a new frame-stitching ticket.

Delivered

  • services/remoteImageProvider.js — substituteTemplate, decodeImage, storageKey, startGeneration/runGeneration, rmt_-prefixed job registry.
  • services/assetStore.js — putObject + ensureBucket (module was read-only).
  • Timeout AI_PROVIDER_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5 min, not the 30s control-plane budget); size cap AI_PROVIDER_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES (default 32 MB).

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ Substitution: nested objects/arrays, whole-leaf numeric coercion, unknown placeholder left intact, no-placeholder passthrough byte-identical.
  • ✅ A1111 shape (images[0]) → real PNG bytes in a fake MinIO, sprite-gen job shape returned.
  • ✅ data:image/png;base64, prefix decodes.
  • ✅ Raw image/png body stored without base64 decoding.
  • ✅ Non-2xx / unreachable / no-image-at-pointer / bad base64 → failed job with a readable error and no half-written object.
  • ✅ Response size capped.

Known limitation

The job registry is in memory, so a backend restart loses in-flight remote jobs. Parity with sprite-gen's own JobManager; accepted for v1.

results.name: Slice A — per-weapon attack origin anchor
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-14 · built on fix/attack-origin-anchor (2a6b6d0); 10 lift sites collapsed, not the 4 first scoped

Goal

Make where an attack visually launches from authorable per weapon, and derive it from the actor's own body height instead of a tile constant. This is the slice that fixes the reported symptom.

Data

item_types.attack_origin — nullable text, CHECK (attack_origin IS NULL OR attack_origin IN ('feet','middle','head')). NULL means "use the kind default". Slice B replaces this CHECK with an FK to a real catalog table, so keep the value a name, not an integer.

Kind defaults resolve server-side, mirroring the existing pattern in backend/src/authority/vfx.js (KIND_DEFAULTS): melee → middle, projectile → middle. Admins then author head for thrown weapons and whichever spells want it, feet for ground-level spells. Fraction table: feet 0.0, middle 0.5, head 0.85.

Wire — send a resolved pixel lift, not the anchor name

This is the load-bearing decision. A projectile in flight has no actor attached to it, and its shooter may be off-screen or dead by the time it lands, so the client cannot look up a sprite height to resolve a fraction against. Instead the server computes lift = round(actorHeight × fraction) ONCE, at attack/spawn time, and puts that number on the frame.

This is the same snapshot-at-spawn convention damage and vfxTrail already follow — see the comments in backend/src/authority/projectiles.js around spawn() explaining why a value is captured at launch rather than re-read later. Sprites draw at their world box size in unscaled screen pixels (drawImage(img, drawX, drawY, w, h) with h = obj.height || 64), so a server-computed pixel lift is directly usable by the client with no further scaling.

Carriers: the attacks[] event (melee arc and non-arc VFX shapes), the projectile snapshot, and detonations. A blast inherits its projectile's lift so a detonation sits where its shot was actually flying.

Client

One shared pure helper replaces the hardcoded s.y - ISO_TILE_H / 2 sites in frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/systems/RenderSystem.js. Built: there were TEN, not the four first scoped — the projectile dot, the blast ring, the melee arc, the projectile trail (both ends), the particle spray, _drawVfxShape's centre and its along() helper, and the block glyph's centre and spark origin.

Acceptance criteria

results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-15 · built at 266b737; 20/20 tests pass, none skipped

The Refresh available models button. Depends on the CRUD slice.

Why generic

Every service exposes its model list differently: A1111 GET /sdapi/v1/sd-models + $[*].model_name, Ollama GET /api/tags + models[*].name, OpenAI-compatible GET /v1/models + data[*].id. The profile row stores models_path and models_pointer, so a new service is configuration, not code.

Delivered

  • services/pointerPath.js — pure evaluator, ~60 lines, no dependency. selectAll for lists, selectOne for SOMET-327's image pointer.

  • ✅ A1111 shape returns checkpoint names and persists to models_cache.
  • ✅ Ollama shape returns names through the same code path — the genericity proof.

  • ✅ test against an unreachable URL returns ok:false at HTTP 200.

results.name: Attack origin, bounded weapon catalogs, and augment stones
results.description_html:
In Progress · 2026-08-15 · slices A/B/C built, PR #19 open and unmerged; slice D (SOMET-343) filed for the deferred half

Reported symptom

Attacks appear to launch from a point just below the actor's head, while melee swings read as coming from the middle of the figure. Different attack kinds should launch from different heights: melee and most ranged (bow, sling) from the middle, thrown weapons from the top, and spells from top, middle or bottom depending on the spell.

Root cause (verified in code, then on the wire)

Every attack visual lifted from the same hardcoded constant, s.y - ISO_TILE_H / 2 (32 px above the feet), at TEN sites in RenderSystem.js — the melee arc, the projectile dot, its trail (both ends), the blast ring, the particle spray, the non-arc VFX shapes, and the block glyph. Actors draw feet-on-tile-centre, so 32 px is exactly mid-body for a 64px player but 67% of a 48px creature's height. The lift was a TILE constant, not a fraction of the body.

Slices

  • SOMET-326 — per-weapon attack origin anchor. Built, To Review. Browser-verified: o: 32 unauthored, o: 54 for an authored head.
  • SOMET-329 — four bounded catalogs (attack_origins, elements, projectile_shapes, impact_behaviors). Built, To Review. Browser-verified: all four dropdowns populate; the element palette arrives on joined.
  • SOMET-332 — augment stones. Partial (5/7 ACs), To Review. Melee only.
  • SOMET-343 — projectile augments and explosive ammo. Backlog. Carries the deferred half of the original request.

What the original request asked for, and where it stands

  • "attacks should start from different heights per weapon" — delivered (326)
  • "edit attack types per weapon in the admin" — delivered (326 + 329)
  • "bounded tables with available options" — delivered (329)
  • "distance of attack" — already existed (item_types.range), now catalog-adjacent
  • "sword can be frost or fire" — delivered (332, melee)
  • "arrows/bows can be explosive or elemental" — NOT delivered, deferred to 343
  • "magic explosive when the distance ends" — NOT delivered; the engine cannot yet distinguish max-range from contact. Deferred to 343.

Standing design constraint

The world is 2D — projectiles carry only x,y, no Z. An attack origin is a render anchor only. It must never change collision, hit detection, or line-of-sight; a test asserts two weapons differing only in origin resolve the identical kill.

Notes for whoever reviews

All three slices were implemented by ONE session and self-review is disclosed on each — an independent reviewer is preferred. Two premises written into these tickets turned out to be wrong against the live schema (element was never free text; the stone constraint never blocked augments) and are corrected on their items; treat the remaining ticket text as claims to check, not as fact.

results.name: Epic: Admin-configurable remote AI image provider
results.description_html:
Todo · 2026-08-14 · queued: design settled, 8 children written, no code yet

Goal

Let an admin point sprite/tile/entity image generation at an AI image service running on another machine, instead of only the local sprite-gen container hardcoded to SPRITE_GEN_URL.

Shape

A new admin Settings / AI Providers tab stores named provider profiles: base URL, optional auth header + token, an editable JSON request template, and the selected model. A Refresh models button queries the service for its available models. Exactly one profile may be active. Only the prompt comes from the local entity/tile-type row and is substituted into the saved template at call time.

When a profile is active it becomes the default for generation; entity types and tile types can override per-type (including back to local sprite-gen).

Decisions taken at design time

  • Remote service is an image endpoint (A1111 / sd.cpp / ComfyUI-class), not a text LLM. Ollama/llama.cpp were the mental model for "many models behind one URL".
  • Global default + per-type override, not a hard switch.
  • Auth token is write-only in the API: reads return has_token, never the value.
  • Named profiles, one marked active (partial unique index).
  • Model discovery is generic — the row stores models_path + models_pointer so A1111 / ComfyUI / Ollama all work with no code change.
  • Sync request/response first (one POST, image in the response). ComfyUI-style async queue polling is a separate follow-up child, not part of the core slices.

Existing code this lands on

  • backend/src/services/spriteGen.js — the single hardcoded client
  • backend/src/index.js startGenerationJob (~line 1971) and the three /api/*-jobs route pairs
  • backend/src/services/assetStore.js — MinIO, currently read-only
  • frontend/src/ui/navSections.js, frontend/src/App.jsx
  • frontend/src/games/something2/TileTypesAdmin.jsx, EntityTypesAdmin.jsx, generationJobPayload.js

Build order

SOMET-324 → 325 → 327 → 328 → 330 → 331 → 333. SOMET-334 (async queue mode) only after the sync path works end to end.

Done when

Every child is Done: an admin can register a remote provider, refresh its model list, test it, mark it active, and generate a tile texture and an entity sprite through it end to end, with the image landing in MinIO and rendering in the admin UI.

results.name: Mid-death XP test counts an unrelated join-time transaction, not the kill's
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged and pushed (main at 3377f42); suite 4 → 3 failures; self-reviewed

One of the four surviving backend failures, investigated with the systematic-debugging discipline because it was the one candidate that looked like a REAL gameplay bug — a player revived by their own kill.

It is not a gameplay bug. The guard under test works: player.hp stays -5 and player.maxHp stays 100. Those assertions passed the whole time; the failure was three lines further down.

Evidence

2 !== 1 at assert.strictEqual(pool.clients.length, 1). Instrumenting the fake pool to dump every statement per checked-out client identified both transactions:

client#0  BEGIN | UPDATE characters SET starting_loadout_granted_at = now() ...
                | SELECT item_type_id, quantity FROM class_loadouts ... | COMMIT
client#1  BEGIN | DELETE FROM world_creatures ... | player_progression read/write
                | SELECT ... FROM creature_drops ... | COMMIT

client#0 is grantStartingLoadout, which runs at JOIN and is transactional by design (SOMET-79). client#1 is the kill. This is the only test in the file that boots a server and joins — the other pool.clients.length assertions are Part 1 unit tests calling commitCreatureDeath directly, which is why they were unaffected.

Fix

The assertion now finds the kill's client by the statement that makes it the kill (DELETE FROM world_creatures) and asserts THAT one was released — the question its own message already claimed to ask, and one that is indifferent to unrelated transactions.

Re-pinning the count to 2 was rejected: it goes green and breaks again the next time anything opens a transaction on join, inside a test about dying. Deleting the assertion was rejected: it goes green and drops a real connection-leak guard.

Acceptance criteria — all met

  1. ✅ The test passes, asserting on the transaction that performed the kill.
  2. ✅ The mid-death assertions are untouched.
  3. ✅ Mutation-verified — removing client.release() from commitCreatureDeath turns it red with "the kill client must still be released". loot.js restored byte-identical.
  4. ✅ No production code changed; backend 4 → 3 failures, no new ones; frontend 950 tests green.

Remaining three failures

assertJwtSecretOrExit, "the live home region matches the checked-in specs", and "the entry world has a village and its entry_spawn IS that village spawn" — the last two are live-data/seed checks rather than logic tests.

results.name: Stone DB tests cannot run against an already-migrated database: 12 of 16 suite failures, one cause
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged as 3c71f68 and pushed; suite 16 → 4 failures; self-reviewed

12 of the backend suite's 16 failures shared a single root cause, and it was not a product bug.

Three test files — stones_integration_db, migration_convert_magic_weapons_db and migration_stone_item_type_down_guard_db — apply stone migrations as SETUP to guarantee the schema they need exists. Correct against a virgin database, impossible against ours, which has carried those migrations since they landed:

column "stat_bonus_stat" of relation "item_types" already exists   (SQLSTATE 42701)

Fix: an explicit presence guard, not a scratch database and not error-swallowing

A per-run scratch database was considered and rejected — these files already roll back in finally, so they never mutate the shared database and the isolation it would buy is already there. Each SETUP apply is now skipped when an information_schema probe finds its schema present. The virgin-database path is unchanged: the guard adds a skip, it does not assume a state. The conversion migration under test still runs its real up() and down().

Errors are never caught and discarded. A blanket 42701/42P07 tolerance was one line away and would have turned twelve honest failures into twelve dishonest passes, while disarming the exact duplicate-object check these migration tests exist to perform.

Two things the original scoping got wrong

Three files, not two. The down-guard file carried the same cause and was missed, which is why the first full run landed on 6 rather than the predicted 4.

The down-guard fix introduced a deadlock, and that was fixed rather than shipped. Its "zero category=stone rows remain" test rests on a premise false on a migrated database, so the precondition is now established explicitly with a DELETE inside the never-committed transaction. That created a race: node --test runs files in parallel, all three write those rows, and two touching them in different orders produced a real deadlock detected abort in a full run while passing in isolation. All three now take one transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock, released by the ROLLBACK they already perform — the technique the entry-world guard already uses.

Acceptance criteria — all met

  1. ✅ All three files pass against the already-migrated dev database.

results.name: fix(render): actor sprites drawn half a tile in front of their collision anchor — obstacles block at the waist, not the feet
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · sprites re-anchored to the collision point; verified in-browser A/B

Symptom

Walking into a tree, stone or wall, the character stops when the middle of the figure reaches the object. Collision should read at the character's feet.

Root cause (render, not collision)

World collision is correct — it runs on the actor's world box, anchored at its centre. The renderer is what is off: RenderSystem.drawCreature / drawEntity compute drawY = s.y - h + ISO_TILE_H/2, putting the sprite's feet ISO_TILE_H/2 = 32px below the projected anchor.

With ISO_TILE_W=128 and MAP_TILE_SIZE=100 the iso scale is K=0.64, so 32 screen px is exactly worldToScreen of a (+50, +50) world offset — half a tile diagonally toward the camera. The sprite is drawn half a tile in front of where the actor actually is, so the collision anchor lands on the sprite's waist (feet at s.y+32, anchor at s.y, sprite 64px tall).

Everything else in the scene is anchored at the diamond centre — floor tiles, walls, ground items, merchant/bank markers, blast rings — so only actors and tile decorations are displaced. Knock-on effects: a dropped item renders at the player's waist instead of their feet, and VFX documented as "chest height" (s.y - ISO_TILE_H/2) actually draw at head height.

Acceptance criteria

  • An actor's feet are drawn at worldToScreen(collision anchor) — the centre of the tile diamond they occupy.
  • Walking into a blocking decoration/wall stops the character with its feet at the obstacle, not its waist.
  • Tile decorations (trees/stones) use the same anchor, so actor-vs-decoration spacing stays consistent.
  • Status-effect rings still sit under the actor's feet; ground items, merchants, banks, walls and floor tiles unchanged.
  • No change to world-space collision maths — frontend systems/movement.js and backend authority/collision.js stay byte-for-byte mirrored.
  • Browser-verified before/after with screenshots.

Files

frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/systems/RenderSystem.js — drawCreature, drawEntity, placeholder branch, and the _drawEffectRings coordinate note.

results.name: Revive two dead inventory-fixture branches still pinned to the pre-SOMET-257 user_id query
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged as d3815c0 and pushed; branch-fires assertion added and mutation-verified; self-reviewed

The last of the four fixtures found during SOMET-316, and the ones deliberately left alone at the time rather than edited on spec.

authority_openchest_integration.test.js and overview_chest_cache_invalidation.test.js both branched on:

/^\s*SELECT id, item_type_id, quantity FROM player_items WHERE user_id/i

Neither had matched anything since SOMET-257 re-keyed inventory onto character_id. The adjacent FROM player_equipment WHERE user_id branch in each file was dead for the same reason.

Behaviour-neutral, and still worth doing

Each fixture's fallthrough is return { rows: [] } — exactly what the dead branches returned — so both files passed before and after. Nothing was failing.

What was fixed is a LIE IN THE FIXTURE. The branches read as "this is how the inventory load is answered here" and were never reached, so a maintainer edits them expecting an effect. They also carried the SOMET-316 trap in dormant form: pinned to an exact column list AND a retired ownership column. Had the fallthrough ever changed to something other than an empty result, both files would have silently fed the authority that new default and failed as bogus ownership errors far from the edit.

Why a green suite could not verify this

A dead branch and a live one are indistinguishable to a passing test when the fallthrough returns the same value — which is exactly how this survived. A pool.inventoryLoads counter is incremented inside the branch and asserted > 0 after a real WS join, so the fix is falsifiable. Reverting the predicate to WHERE user_id turns that assertion red with "loadInventory was never answered by the fixture branch", proving both halves at once: unreachable before, reached now.

Acceptance criteria — all met

  1. ✅ Both branches match the query loadInventory actually issues, proven by the fired-or-not assertion rather than by the files still passing.
  2. ✅ Both files 8/8; full backend suite 2282 pass / 16 fail, diffing IDENTICAL to the post-SOMET-317 baseline — no new failures, none newly fixed.
  3. ✅ No production code touched.

Closes the SOMET-316 sweep

A repo-wide grep confirms no test still pins SELECT id, item_type_id, quantity FROM player_items, and no fixture still matches player_items/player_equipment on WHERE user_id. All four fixtures found during SOMET-316 now match the table and the ownership predicate rather than the column list.

results.name: Mark bound items in the merchant sell panel, before the click instead of after
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged to main as f6d85e5 and pushed; all 4 ACs verified in a browser; self-reviewed

The second surface deliberately scoped OUT of SOMET-316, now that the data it needs is on the wire.

trade.js sellItem refuses a soulbound instance with "starting gear cannot be sold" — but only AFTER the player clicks Sell. The shop panel's "Your items" column gave no warning, so the only way to discover that your starting sword is unsellable was to try to sell it. The account chest already marks the same item bound; the merchant, where the information actually changes what a player does, did not.

SOMET-316 put soulbound on every inventory item the client holds, so renderShop already had the value in inventory.items — a render change with no new data plumbing.

The Sell control stays live, deliberately

The marker is a LABEL, not a client-side gate. Withholding the hit area for a bound row would put an authorization decision in the client: if this flag were ever stale or wrong, a player would be locked out of selling an item they legitimately own, with no way to discover why. Leaving the control live means a stale flag degrades to a cosmetic wrong label plus the server's own clear refusal — the safe direction to fail. canEquipClient sets the precedent. A test pins this, because "helpfully" hiding the button is the obvious future edit.

Acceptance criteria — all demonstrated

  1. ✅ browser — the starting loadout shows bound in the merchant's "Your items" column.
  2. ✅ browser — a third leather-vest of the SAME item type with soulbound = false renders unmarked beside the bound one.
  3. ✅ browser — all 3 rows keep a live Sell control; clicking the bound row reached the server, which answered "starting gear cannot be sold", and nothing moved (3 items before and after, gold unchanged).
  4. ✅ browser — same amber treatment and row slot as the account chest panel.

Two traps hit during this item, both worth reusing

1. A stale vite module graph read as a broken feature. The first browser attempt showed no markers. Vite's watcher had missed host-side git checkout rewrites, so the served inventory.js contained zero occurrences of soulbound while the file on disk had three. A cache-bypassing reload did NOT fix it; make dev-stop && make dev did. Signature: a client object missing a field ENTIRELY that the client mapper sets unconditionally means old client code is running, not bad server data. curl the served module rather than trusting the browser.

2. The base moved mid-task. Local main gained 13 commits from an externally-made feat/world-scale-density merge while this session worked. The full backend suite was therefore re-run against the merged result before pushing: zero new failures, and three pre-existing baseline failures FIXED by that work. By the time the push ran, those commits had already been pushed externally, so this session's push carried only its own two.

results.name: Send soulbound to the client so bound items are marked while carried, not only while stored
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged to main as 2fcb224 and pushed; all 4 ACs demonstrated; self-reviewed

Follow-up to SOMET-310, recorded as residue in that item's Done comment.

The account chest panel marked a stored item bound, but the same item showed no marker while the character was CARRYING it. The panel was not at fault: loadInventory never selected soulbound, so the client's inventory mirror had no such field to render.

The marker therefore appeared only once the item was somewhere it could not be sold anyway, and was absent in the Carrying tab — exactly where "this will not sell" is worth knowing, since trade.js sellItem refuses only AFTER the click.

Scope: two payload paths, not every one

Only two places can hand the client a bound item, because soulbound defaults false on every fresh INSERT:

  • items.js loadInventory — the join snapshot, and the ONLY loader that can emit a true value (grantStartingLoadout is the sole writer of soulbound = true).
  • accountChest.js withdrawItem — already read the flag to carry it across the move, then dropped it from the returned wire item.

NOT touched, because they cannot produce a bound instance: trade.js buyStock, loot.js claimItem (loot.js:428 — dropping a bound item is REFUSED precisely so this cannot launder one), and the chest-open grant path.

Display only

Every rule that reads this flag — sellItem's refusal, dropItem's — runs server-side against the row, never against the client copy. A stale or forged value can mislead a player's own panel and authorize nothing. Normalized to a real boolean client-side so a frame from an older server reads as "not bound" rather than undefined.

The fixture trap this uncovered

Two integration fixtures matched loadInventory's EXACT select list. Adding one column silently switched those branches off, the fake returned no rows, the authority received an EMPTY inventory, and ten unrelated tests failed as "you do not own that item" — a fixture bug wearing an ownership bug's clothes. Both now match the table and the ownership predicate, never the column list. The mirror image of the trap items.js already documents for knockback/stat_bonus_stat: there the SELECT was wrong, here the TEST was pinned.

Acceptance criteria — all demonstrated

  1. ✅ browser — a character carrying its starting loadout sees both items marked bound in the Carrying tab.
  2. ✅ browser — deposited then withdrawn, the item is still marked bound while carried; the flag survives on the wire, not just in the database.
  3. ✅ browser — a second short sword of the SAME item type with soulbound = false renders unmarked beside the bound one.
  4. ✅ suites — no refusal changed; SOMET-310's ownership, equipped, stone and capacity guards all still pass, and the backend failing set is byte-identical to the pre-change baseline.

results.name: 13 worlds seed zero creatures — placement finds no valid tile
results.description_html:
Pre-existing, confirmed against a session-start baseline taken before SOMET-301 changed anything — every one of these had creature_count = 0 already. Filing it because SOMET-301's seeding made it visible and loud.

Affected (all from loop-catacombs and spine-descent): Ashfang Den, Catacomb Threshold, Deepvault Row, Drowned Southwing, Farrow Hall, Frostbound Shrine, Frozen Ossuary Heart, Glacier's End, Hollow Cache, Sealed Mausoleum, Shrikewind Gorge, Sunken Eastwing, The Deep Cut.

What is known

Seed log reads populateWorld: scatter under-delivered for world <name> (requested 221, placed 0). That message comes from the late warning, not an early return — so these worlds get past the allowed-types and hostile-types guards and their creature types do exist (e.g. Deepvault Row allows ["Slime","Bat"], Glacier's End allows ["Skeleton"]). Placement itself finds no valid tile and rejection sampling exhausts maxAttempts. Most likely their biome/tile mix leaves no walkable candidate tiles.

The resize scaled the request (12 → 221-301) but placed stays 0 either way, so the failure mode is unchanged by that epic.

Why it matters now: SOMET-301's headline is 48,133 creatures across 86 worlds — but 13 of those worlds are empty and would be empty at any size.

results.name: Entry world is lethal: a level-2 Slime camps the spawn and kills level-1 characters
results.description_html:
Observed repeatedly during SOMET-308's browser verification, across two separate sessions and multiple respawns.

A level-2 Slime with damage 5.5 sits at or beside the Old Trailhead spawn point and kills a fresh level-1 character within seconds of it appearing — then again on respawn. A new player's first experience of the game is dying immediately, repeatedly, before they can move.

Attribution is genuinely unclear — do not assume it is SOMET-301

Doubling density raises how many creatures sit near any given tile, so that epic plausibly made this more likely. But creature levels and damage come from level_band / creatureLevel, which SOMET-301 did not touch, and Old Trailhead's band is [1,2] — a level-2 creature there is within spec. It may well have been possible before and simply not hit.

Worth checking whichever way it lands: whether the entry world should exclude hostile spawns within some radius of the spawn point at all, independently of density.

results.name: No navigability regression test for hub-vale, spine-descent, loop-catacombs
results.description_html:
Surfaced by SOMET-301. p5-descent has backend/tests/p5_navigability.test.js, a fast database-free guard that runs the same check applyMapSpec runs at apply time. The three hand-authored specs have nothing equivalent, and seed_map_db.test.js's loop throws on the first failing spec so it proves little.

This matters because resizing worlds broke navigability for 12 worlds — 9 in p5-descent and 3 hand-authored (hub-vale/mire, loop-catacombs/eastwing, loop-catacombs/deepvault) — all fixed by seed retuning. Only the generated set has a guard against that regressing.

One trap to design around

A spec-only check is not sufficient for at least one world. hub-vale.map.json declares only hub --S--> mire, but the live database also has an E doorway on mire. Seed 2011 (from migration 1714440165000) passes at 96x96 against the spec's declared doorways and fails against the live set (doorway E at (48,95) is unreachable). A test that reads only the spec would be another 64-shaped fiction — it must read live doorways, or explicitly cover both sets.

Reuse the machinery p5_navigability.test.js already uses: buildWorldGenConfig + assertNavigable + requiredTilesFor, with catalog data from seeds/data/tileTypes.js and biomes.js. No database required for the spec-side legs.

Seed 2011 (from migration 1714440165000) passes at 96x96 against the spec's declared doorways and fails against the live set (doorway E at (48,95) is unreachable). A test that reads only the spec would be another 64-shaped fiction — it must read live doorways, or explicitly cover both sets.
Reuse the machinery p5_navigability.test.js already uses: buildWorldGenConfig + assertNavigable + requiredTilesFor, with catalog data from seeds/data/tileTypes.js and biomes.js. No database required for the spec-side legs.

results.name: seed-map silently ignores a village whose box moved; home-region migrations hold stale 64-era coords
results.description_html:
Surfaced by SOMET-301, which is the first change ever to move an existing village box in a checked-in spec.

Defect 1 — a moved village drifts with no warning

backend/scripts/seed-map.js:347-353 skips village creation entirely for any world that already has one ("all-or-nothing per world"), and :377-382 warns only when the village count differs. A village whose box moved is count 1 vs 1, so it drifts silently. The all-or-nothing skip was written for "an author added a village", not "an author moved one".

Real consequence, observed in a browser during SOMET-308: the player spawned at the resized world's centre on open grass while the village sat 16 tiles away at its old position. Worked around there by deleting the village rows and their guards and re-seeding — but the next person to move a village will hit it again.

Defect 2 — home-region content exists in two places, only one was moved

backend/migrations/1714440201000_home_region_content.js:76-131 and 1714440240000_home_region_waypoints.js:57-59 carry the home region's village boxes, roads, pens and waypoints as deliberately frozen literals at 64-era coordinates (min_row: 24, min_col: 38, spawn_x: 3950; waypoints at 3250/4050/3050). SOMET-301 moved the same content in the specs (to 56/70/7150, 4850/7250/4650) and left the migrations untouched.

A fresh make reseed-map converges from the spec and is correct — that is the path SOMET-308's browser checks exercised. An in-place make seed-map does not, per Defect 1. backend/tests/home_region_db.test.js:75-96 asserts live rows equal the checked-in specs, so it fails on any pre-existing database re-seeded in place — and is invisible without TEST_DATABASE_URL.

Suggested direction

Give a village an identity beyond its box (a stable key in the spec) so the seeder can reposition rather than skip. Failing that, make the box mismatch at least as loud as the count mismatch already is.

results.name: Measure per-player load now that size and density multiply
results.description_html:
Surfaced by the final whole-branch review of SOMET-301. The design doc's runtime argument is wrong, and nothing measured the real cost.

The mechanism

deriveSize and deriveDensity in backend/scripts/dungeon/escalation.js are both floor(hopFraction * 5) over 5-element tables, so the ramp is perfectly correlated: 96↔sparse, 128↔normal, 160↔dense, 192↔horde, 224↔swarm. Per-world population therefore swings ~86x across the ramp (28 → 2408), not the ~5x either lever gives alone.

Why that matters at runtime

The design doc argues cost is "close to free" because simulation scales with connected players, not world area. That is true of area alone and false of the combination. backend/src/authority/server.js:1019-1026 activates a radius-1 chunk neighbourhood (9 chunks = 9,216 tiles) and :1041-1052 broadcasts that same set to every socket each tick. At 64x64 with chunk_size 32 a world had only 4 chunks total, so the 9-chunk neighbourhood was clamped by the world itself — at most ~98 creatures at the old swarm rate. At 224x224 swarm it is unclamped at ~442. That is roughly 4.5x the per-tick creature simulation and per-player broadcast payload, for the 14 deepest worlds.

What to do

  • Measure tick time and per-socket payload with a player parked in a 224x224 swarm world, ideally with several players in the same neighbourhood.
  • If it is bad, the cheapest mitigation is already designed in: lower the ramp's top step(s) in SIZE_STEPS. Nothing else depends on those specific numbers.
  • Decoupling size from density (different bucket counts) is the more surgical fix if only the deepest tier is a problem.
