results.name: Account chest: shared item storage across a user's characters
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · all 7 ACs demonstrated; self-reviewed; branch feat/account-chest (1544f5c) unmerged

A per-ACCOUNT item store ("bank"), accessible from a bank marker beside the merchant in every village. Every character on the account sees the same contents; no other account can see or touch them. Items only — users.gold is already account-wide, so a gold vault would be a UI for something that already happens.

Data model

New table account_items, keyed on user_id (not character_id) — that single column choice is the whole feature.

account_items
  id           uuid pk default gen_random_uuid()
  user_id      int  notNull -> users ON DELETE CASCADE
  slot         smallint CHECK (slot BETWEEN 1 AND 40)
  item_type_id int  notNull -> item_types
  quantity     int  notNull CHECK (quantity > 0)
  soulbound    bool notNull default false
  deposited_at timestamptz notNull default now()
  UNIQUE (user_id, slot)

The 40-slot cap is a SCHEMA INVARIANT, not a COUNT(*) check — same reasoning migration 1714440092000 spells out for the 8-character cap. Two concurrent deposits into the last free slot cannot both win; the loser takes a unique-constraint violation the handler turns into "your chest is full". Count-then-insert would race.

Transfer semantics

One transaction per direction. Ownership is enforced by the SQL predicate, never by a pre-check outside the transaction (the buyStock pattern in backend/src/authority/trade.js).

  • deposit: DELETE FROM player_items WHERE id=$1 AND character_id=$2 RETURNING ... then INSERT INTO account_items. The character_id=$2 clause IS the authorization — 0 rows means not yours.
  • withdraw: exact mirror, predicate user_id=$2. No capacity check — character inventory has no cap today.

Deposit guards (rejections, not new mechanics)

  • Equipped item — player_equipment declares UNIQUE(item_id) with a cascade, so deleting an equipped player_items row would silently strip the equipment row. Explicit guard required.
  • Any stone — TIGHTENED DURING BUILD from the planned "socketed stones only". stone_instances.player_item_id CASCADEs on a player_items delete and that row holds the stone's accumulated XP, which account_items has nowhere to carry. Refusing only SOCKETED stones would have silently destroyed a loose stone's progression on deposit.
  • Weapon holding stones — refused with "unsocket the stone first". socketed_into_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so depositing would pop the stone out unasked.
  • Soulbound is ALLOWED and PRESERVED across the round trip. Moving a bound item between your own characters can never produce gold because it stays unsellable; clearing the flag, however, would launder starter gear into sellable gold and reopen the SOMET-277 faucet through a new door.

Placement & wire protocol

One bank per village, beside the existing merchant, DERIVED in fetchVillages from the STORED merchant position rather than stored in its own columns — so every existing village gets one with no backfill and there is no second source of truth. Bound to key b, not e, so it does not fight the merchant interact.

Frames mirror the shop: openbank -> bank {villageId, items[], capacity} -> deposit {itemId} / withdraw {itemId}, each re-sending a fresh bank. All routed through chainOp. EVERY frame re-resolves the bank post from the server's own copy of the player position; the opener is not the only proximity gate.

Client

renderBank + _bankHitAreas in RenderSystem.js, tabbed Chest / Carry, reusing the shop panel's existing tab and page widgets. BOTH lists are paged — the shop's "Your items" column breaks out of its draw loop when it runs out of room, and an unreachable chest row would be an unrecoverable item.

Acceptance criteria — all demonstrated

  1. ✅ browser — Character A deposited a vest; character B on the same account opened the same post, saw it, and withdrew it. Item conservation checked: 4 items before, 4 after.
  2. ✅ real DB — account B sees 0 rows while A sees 1; B's attempt to withdraw A's row is refused and A keeps it.
  3. ✅ browser — depositing an equipped vest returned "unequip it first"; it stayed both equipped and carried.
  4. ✅ service tests — a stone, and a weapon hosting one, are both refused. NOT browser-exercised; see the Done comment.
  5. ✅ real DB — the 41st deposit returned "your chest is full" and the refused item stayed with the character.
  6. ✅ browser — forged deposit/withdraw frames naming another character's or a nonexistent row were refused with no state change.
  7. ✅ browser — a "Chest" marker renders beside "Merchant"; b opens the panel in range, and every bank frame is refused from 318px away.

Testing

backend/tests/account_chest.test.js (10 tests, mutation-checked), backend/tests/villagesService.test.js (+2 geometry invariants), frontend/.../__tests__/bankPanel.test.js (10 tests).

results.name: Creature respawn — worlds drain permanently and never refill
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged to main at 50cc237; 607 tests green, respawn observed live in the running authority (kill → queue row → creature on the wire, attackable)

Killed creatures are deleted permanently: backend/src/authority/loot.js:75 issues DELETE FROM world_creatures WHERE id = $1 on death. populateWorld — the only code that ever creates hostile creatures — is called from exactly two places, backend/scripts/seed-map.js:505 and the admin re-roll route at backend/src/index.js:2630. There is no timer, no cron, and no on-join repopulation anywhere.

The world's creature population is a finite pool that only drains. Measured 2026-08-13: 3,726 creatures across 86 worlds, for 21 characters.

Why this is filed separately

SOMET-301 raises the starting pool roughly tenfold, which buys time but does not change the shape of the problem — a determined group still empties a world and it stays empty until an operator clicks re-roll. "Enough creatures for players" is not actually true until this ships.

Notes for whoever picks this up

Nothing in SOMET-301 blocks it. A respawn scheduler reads the same world_creatures table and can reuse populateWorld's placement. Note that world_creatures has no death/respawn timestamp column today.

results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-13 · 20 worlds resized, 5 feature sets re-placed, 3 seeds retuned (92aeb84)

Plan Task 6. deriveSize does not reach the three hand-authored specs — a world whose spec still says 64 stays 64. 20 worlds get explicit sizes; only 5 of them carry authored features.

Re-placement rule

Features are laid out around the centre tile of a 64-tile world (tile 32). Translation delta is new/2 - old/2 tiles (delta * 100 px), applied to every tile and pixel coordinate. Exception: a road endpoint at a map edge (1 or 62) re-anchors to the new edge — 1 stays 1, 62 becomes new - 2 — or the road dead-ends mid-map.

Acceptance criteria

  • All 20 worlds resized per the plan's table; chunk_size stays 32.
  • The 5 worlds with features (hub-vale hub/forest, spine-descent entry/pass, loop-catacombs entry) have villages, roads, pens, waypoints and spawns re-placed.
  • tests/map_spec_fixtures.test.js and tests/authored_roads.test.js pass.

results.name: World scale and creature density
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-14 · merged to main in 711c183; 48,131 creatures across 96–224 worlds

Every world was 64x64 tiles (~18 screens) and the whole game held 3,726 creatures across 86 worlds. Both were too small for multiple concurrent players.

Result

86 worlds now spread 96(28) / 128(13) / 160(17) / 192(12) / 224(16) tiles, holding 48,131 creatures. Size is derived from progression depth by deriveSize(hopFraction), beside the existing level-band and density derivations; density tier rates doubled with no migration.

results.name: Merge portals and waypoints into one travel network — one portal per map, popup on arrival
results.description_html:
Reported from testing SOMET-296: "there should be one portal per map, you have added multiple". Correct — and the deeper problem is that the game now has two mechanics for one idea. The waypoint system (SOMET-292/293) already implements exactly the requested behaviour: must be standing on one, undiscovered ones are not selectable, server re-derives every rule. It just opens with T and is called something else. The risk was flagged during the SOMET-296 brainstorm and accepted; testing showed the cost.

Decisions confirmed during grilling:

  1. Merge into one network. One travel landmark per map. It IS the waypoint; the separate concept is retired. Dungeon doors stay a different thing and never appear in the travel list.
  2. Keep the waypoints implementation. waypoints + character_waypoints + joinPolicy's waypoint-travel leg + the popup are built and tested — reuse them. Delete the 8 home-region portal rows added by SOMET-299 (migration 1714440250000) and the spine-descent.map.json portal entry.
  3. Coverage: every safe map, none in dungeons — but authored explicitly per map spec, NOT derived from a column. Reason below.
  4. Trigger: auto-open once per arrival on the tile, latched so it does not reopen until the player steps off and back on. T still opens it manually.
  5. Let the two non-duplicate links go. Thornbriar↔Windwatch and Old Trailhead↔Catacombs Entry disappear with the rest. Catacombs Entry reverts to being reached on foot via Highlands Reach.

Why the selector must be authored, not queried — two findings from the live data:

  • allows_fast_travel does not mean "safe". 30 worlds carry it, including Sealed Mausoleum, Drowned Southwing, Deepvault Row, Sunken Eastwing and Frozen Ossuary Heart — the loop-catacombs chain. It cannot be the selector for "none in dungeons".
  • Blackfen Sinks is flagged and ships sealed (SOMET-273: 0.1% of its interior reachable). Any automatic placement rule puts a portal in a map nobody can walk in.

Load-bearing constraint: 7 of the 14 existing dungeon portals are guarded via blocks_portal_id. A guarded portal must never become travel-selectable — that drops a traveller past the guard and defeats the level-band gating joinPolicy protects. The rule already exists (guardedWaypointViolations) and must keep holding after the merge.

Scope:

  • Enforce at most one travel landmark per world — map-spec validator AND a DB unique index, so it cannot be violated by a hand-written row.
  • Auto-open on arrival, latched; T retained.
  • Empty-list state when nothing is reachable yet.
  • Rename user-facing text to "Portal".
  • Migration: delete the 8 SOMET-299 portal rows + the spec entry. down() restores them.
  • SOMET-297/298 landmark markers keep working and now show one portal per map.

Open — needs a decision before implementation: exact empty-list copy; whether the rename reaches the DB/table names or stays user-facing only; whether walk-through dungeon doors keep their marker; which additional safe maps get a portal and where (content pass, can follow).

results.name: Slice 3 — author eight home-region portals (spec pair + migration for six cross-spec rows)
results.description_html:
Spec §4. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-landmark-visibility-design.md — independent of Slices 1-2, ordered after them only so no portal ships invisible.

Eight PORTAL rows. Each direction is its own row — that is how all 14 existing portals are built, and map_links_portal_coords_check requires from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y all non-null on every one.

Spec route (spine-descent.map.json): Old Trailhead → Windwatch Pass, Windwatch Pass → Old Trailhead.

Migration route: Old Trailhead ↔ Thornbriar Reach, Thornbriar Reach ↔ Windwatch Pass, Old Trailhead ↔ The Catacombs: Entry.

Why there must be two routes: the home region spans two map specs. Old Trailhead and Windwatch Pass are spine-descent worlds; Thornbriar Reach is a hub-vale world. A spec link resolves from/to against world keys within that spec (seeds/mapSpec.js:170-171), so a cross-spec portal cannot be expressed there at all. This is not new — 1714440201000_home_region_content.js:20-22 records that the Old Trailhead ↔ Thornbriar compass link "exists only in the live database and is in no checked-in spec." The migration must use LITERALS, not a read of the spec files, with worlds matched by name via worlds_name_unique: a migration must do the same thing forever, and a later spec edit must not silently rewrite what it already applied.

Placement: a small pad immediately outside each village's gate edge. All three home villages gate south (villages.gate_edge = 'S'). Inside the walls would put a teleport pad where the merchant and the two gate guards already stand.

Thornbriar ↔ Windwatch is the genuinely new connection — today those two are linked only through Old Trailhead; the compass graph has no direct edge.

Rules this must not break:

  • No new portal may be flagged is_waypoint if a creature guards it via blocks_portal_id (load-bearing rule, home-region spec §5). None of the eight is guarded today; the rule still binds whoever adds a guard later.
  • seed-map's offline navigability check must still pass — a pad outside a gate must not sever the gate from the map.
  • populateWorld's opening DELETE spares only rows with type = 'Village Guard', a blocks_portal_id, or a non-null home_x. Relevant if a portal guard is ever added here — the bug that already bit portal guards (SOMET-246) and vault chests (SOMET-244).
  • Level bands: Old Trailhead is 1-2, The Catacombs: Entry is 1-5. This does not bypass gating (Catacombs Entry is already reachable via Highlands Reach, band 1-8) but does put a level-1 character one step from level-5 creatures. If that proves brutal, the fix is the destination choice, not the mechanism.
  • home_region_db.test.js asserts live rows equal the checked-in specs; its contract must be extended to cover the migration-authored portals, or migration-only rows will either fail it or sit outside its coverage.

Tests: map-spec fixture tests for the spec-authored pair; a DB test asserting all eight live rows exist with correct coordinates and destinations; the navigability assertion; a test that the guarded-portal/is_waypoint rule still holds over live rows.

Seam risk: a future editor adding a portal to spine-descent.map.json expecting it to reach Thornbriar gets a validator error; one editing the migration expecting seed-map to converge gets a warning. The migration comment must say which route owns which row.

results.name: Slice 2 — minimap markers and World Map tab badges
results.description_html:
Spec §2 (minimap, World Map), §3. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-landmark-visibility-design.md — depends on Slice 1.

Minimap (frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/systems/minimapRenderer.js): drawMinimap at line 33 currently takes { overview, tileColors, player, creatures, doorways, villages, view } and draws a gold square for a village and a magenta diamond for a doorway. It gains waypoints and portals arrays in the same marker idiom. The overview payload gains the matching fields — generateWorldOverview at backend/src/services/mapService.js:321-322 currently ships exactly doorways and villages.

World Map tab: a pulsing badge on each world node containing a landmark the character may know about. Waypoint half from the existing GET /api/player/waypoints (listWaypointsForCharacter, services/waypoints.js:244). Portal half by extending GET /api/player/world-map's per-world rows with a portalCount — the World Map already fetches that endpoint and already scopes it by fog, so no new route. The badge shows presence, not position; this surface is per-world granularity and stays that way.

Fog of war is not weakened. Landmarks must be scoped by character_visited_worlds in the query, not in the caller — exactly as listWaypointsForCharacter already does. Revealing that an unvisited world holds a portal leaks the map structure the fog exists to hide.

Tests: a drawMinimap test pinning marker position for a known overview origin. A pulse test passing two different phases and asserting the drawn alpha differs — that is the assertion proving the pulse is wired to its input rather than hardcoded. A fog test asserting the World Map surface omits landmarks for worlds absent from character_visited_worlds.

Browser verification required. Confirm the Old Trailhead marker appears on the minimap and that the World Map tab badges the world.

results.name: Slice 1 — landmark read model, frame delivery, in-world tile rendering
results.description_html:
Spec §1, §2 (in-world), §3. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-landmark-visibility-design.md

A landmark is a read model, not a table: the union of a world's waypoints and its PORTAL source tiles.

landmark = { kind: 'waypoint' | 'portal', x, y, name, activated }

activated is per character from character_waypoints, meaningful for waypoints only; always false for a portal, since portals are not activated — walking into one uses it.

Delivery is by frame, not by chunk. The authority already holds both sides (loadWorld builds the waypoint Map the tick loop matches against; map_links drives every transition). Landmarks are static per world and single-digit in count, so they ride the existing 'joined' and 'transition' frames. A per-chunk payload would re-send the same handful of points on every chunk activation for nothing.

No second loader. If the authority needs a portal list it does not already hold, that read joins the existing loadWorld path. The two-loader inertness trap (SOMET-249) is the most expensive recurring mistake in this codebase.

In-world rendering (RenderSystem.js): pulsing iso diamond plus a soft vertical beam on the landmark tile, drawn under entities so a creature standing on it stays legible. Waypoints blue-white, portals violet. An unactivated waypoint draws as a dim outline, reusing the activated/unactivated distinction the travel popup already makes.

The pulse phase is an input, never a clock read. The draw takes a phase/nowMs parameter from the caller's animation loop. A renderer that calls Date.now() internally cannot be pinned by a test.

Tests: unit tests over the read model (waypoint only / portal only / both / neither; activated true and false for the same waypoint across two characters). A test that the 'joined' frame carries landmarks for the joined world and NOT for any other. A render test asserting a marker at the landmark tile and the outline variant for an unactivated waypoint.

Risk: this touches the join frame, which every client entry path depends on — first join, resume, transition, waypoint travel. A malformed payload breaks joining, not just marker drawing. The read model must degrade to an empty array rather than throw; 86 worlds have no landmarks.

Browser verification required. Join Old Trailhead, confirm a pulsing marker one tile east of spawn.

results.name: Landmarks — make portals and waypoints findable, and put portals in the home region
results.description_html:
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-landmark-visibility-design.md (commit 850a8ff)

Two separate defects sit behind "I can't find the portals":

  1. Waypoints and portals have no visual representation anywhere. RenderSystem.js, wallRenderer.js and minimapRenderer.js contain zero references to portal or waypoint. The minimap overview payload ships only doorways and villages.
  2. The home region contains no portals. All 14 live edge='PORTAL' links sit in deep dungeon chains.

The bug this starts from: Old Trailhead's spawn is (3150, 3250) = tile col 31.5, row 32.5. The "Old Trailhead Commons" waypoint is at (3250, 3250) = col 32.5, row 32.5. Both inside the village box (cols 30-35, rows 31-34). The player spawns one tile from a waypoint and nothing on screen says so — SOMET-292/293 shipped a working network with no visual surface.

Decisions taken: markers pulse permanently (smooth opacity oscillation, phase passed in as a renderer input so tests can pin it); all three surfaces (in-world tile, minimap, World Map tab); eight new portals in the home region.

Key constraint found during design: the home region spans two map specs — Old Trailhead and Windwatch Pass are spine-descent worlds, Thornbriar Reach is hub-vale. Spec links resolve only within one spec, so six of the eight portals must be authored by migration with literals, following 1714440201000_home_region_content.js.

Children: slices 1-3.

results.name: A guard locks onto an unreachable hostile and abandons its post indefinitely
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-13 · merged to local main as 9ffa441 (not pushed). Self-reviewed, disclosed in the closing comment. 42 permanent jams → 0; guards 95.2% on station across a 300s two-hostile run.

Observed live in the running game on 2026-08-13 while browser-verifying SOMET-291, and predicted by that slice's own review, which recorded it as a follow-up rather than fixing it in scope.

What I saw. In Old Trailhead, both Village Guards were sitting off their posts and completely motionless for the entire observation window: guard 1 at (3258, 3200) against a post at (3250, 3350) — 150 px off — and guard 2 at (3452, 3258) against a post at (3450, 3350) — 92 px off. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-13 — I was outrunning the chasers; this observation has an innocent explanation and is not evidence of a defect.

The mechanism (from SOMET-291's review, recorded at backend/src/authority/creatures.js:1096): the chase branch had no stall detection, no repath and no give-up — all of that machinery lives in the no-target return branch, which a guard holding a target never reaches. So a guard that acquired a hostile it could not walk to jammed against the inside of its own wall and stayed there. This is the part that stood, and it was far wider than reported: of the 73 walkable hostile placements around a live village's two posts, 42 jammed permanently, 99.7% of the window off station.

Why it was worth its own ticket. Pre-existing, but SOMET-291 raised the Guard leash from 300 to 600 and thereby widened the band of unreachable hostiles that can capture a guard, on the three walls that have no gate. The consequence is not cosmetic: a distracted guard is not guarding the gate, which is the entire point of SOMET-291.

Fix as shipped. The chase branch counts consecutive ticks whose step the terrain refused — measured as the fraction of the requested step actually delivered, with a target in strike range exempt — and after 2s drops the target and refuses it for five minutes, walking home through the existing stepHome. The refusal lifts early only for a hostile that starts fighting a player, which is SOMET-291's own engagingAPlayer predicate. A first version keyed on the guard's own displacement passed every test written for it and was refuted by the running game within a minute: a wall-slide after a roaming hostile moves the guard every tick while getting it nowhere.

Watch for. Any change here must not stop a guard pursuing a hostile that is reachable but currently behind a corner — the rescue depends on the guard following a chaser through the gate, and an over-eager give-up would silently undo SOMET-291. Covered by a test that trails a hostile at exactly the guard's own speed for four stall windows, and by the unchanged SOMET-291 golden trace.

The mechanism (from SOMET-291's review, recorded at backend/src/authority/creatures.js:1096): the chase branch had no stall detection, no repath and no give-up — all of that machinery lives in the no-target return branch, which a guard holding a target never reaches. So a guard that acquired a hostile it could not walk to jammed against the inside of its own wall and stayed there. This is the part that stood, and it was far wider than reported: of the 73 walkable hostile placements around a live village's two posts, 42 jammed permanently, 99.7% of the window off station.
Why it was worth its own ticket. Pre-existing, but SOMET-291 raised the Guard leash from 300 to 600 and thereby widened the band of unreachable hostiles that can capture a guard, on the three walls that have no gate. The consequence is not cosmetic: a distracted guard is not guarding the gate, which is the entire point of SOMET-291.
Fix as shipped. The chase branch counts consecutive ticks whose step the terrain refused — measured as the fraction of the requested step actually delivered, with a target in strike range exempt — and after 2s drops the target and refuses it for five minutes, walking home through the existing stepHome. The refusal lifts early only for a hostile that starts fighting a player, which is SOMET-291's own engagingAPlayer predicate. A first version keyed on the guard's own displacement passed every test written for it and was refuted by the running game within a minute: a wall-slide after a roaming hostile moves the guard every tick while getting it nowhere.
Watch for. Any change here must not stop a guard pursuing a hostile that is reachable but currently behind a corner — the rescue depends on the guard following a chaser through the gate, and an over-eager give-up would silently undo SOMET-291. Covered by a test that trails a hostile at exactly the guard's own speed for four stall windows, and by the unchanged SOMET-291 golden trace.

results.name: Home Region G — death returns you to the last village you entered
results.description_html:
Changes Requested · 2026-08-13 · dying on a doorway tile emits two transitions and strands the player

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §6. No blockers.

Today. World.resolveDeaths() snaps a dead player to player_binds or their join spawn, SAME WORLD ONLY. Nothing about villages.

Auto-bind. Entering a village footprint silently writes player_binds for that character, throttled so loitering at a gate is not a write per tick. The D2 checkpoint rule: death always returns you to the last village you ENTERED, wherever it is.

Respawn, three cases.

  • Bind in the current world → today's behaviour exactly.
  • Bind in another world → resolveDeaths() still resolves the death synchronously (heal and clears stay on the tick path); onPlayerDeath then enqueues pendingArrivals for the bound village spawn and sends transition. Nothing attempts a world change on the synchronous tick.
  • No bind → today's behaviour, unchanged.

Acceptance

  • Same-world respawn test: lands on the village spawn tile, INTERIOR (SOMET-153).
  • Cross-world respawn test: pendingArrivals set and transition sent; the rejoin authorized by the existing transition leg of mayJoin, not a new hole.
  • No-bind test asserting the old behaviour survives.
  • Double-fire test: resolveDeaths() still heals in the SAME pass, so one death cannot be reported twice. The cross-world leg defers only the relocation.
  • Auto-bind throttle test.
  • Added by review: a player who dies while standing on a doorway or portal tile must produce exactly one transition, to the bound village — the transition blocks run before resolveDeaths() in the same tick and must not act on a corpse.
  • Added by review: a failed bind upsert must leave the bind dirty and retry, matching the comment that claims deferral.
  • backend npm test, plus browser verification.

Watch for. An idle character dying to a nearby creature has previously been misread as a position/logout bug. Tag the object under test; do not idle-wait near creatures while verifying.

Constraint this slice creates for map authors (SOMET-289): death becomes a travel primitive that bypasses the visited && allows_fast_travel gate, so any world holding a bind is permanently reachable by dying. A village must therefore never be authored in a world whose only entrance is a blocks_portal_id-guarded portal.

Browser script (live data, verified 2026-08-13). Old Trailhead (entry world) holds the only relevant village — tile rows 31-34, cols 30-35, world px x 3000-3600 / y 3100-3500, respawn (3150, 3250). Windwatch Pass (East) and Thornbriar Reach (West) have no village, which is what makes the cross-world leg visible. Enter the village (silent bind) → die outside it in the same world, expecting a snap to (3150, 3250) at full hp with no reconnect → walk East and die there, expecting heal, reconnect, and arrival inside the Old Trailhead village. Exactly one transition frame on the /authority socket. Failures: respawn at world centre = bind never written; respawn in Windwatch with no reconnect = p.bind null; repeated reconnects or extra transitions = double-fire broke (stop); arriving dead or low hp = the heal was deferred with the relocation (stop).

results.name: Home Region F — waypoint travel popup, and retire world-map click-travel
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-13 · built on feat/home-region-f-waypoint-travel; 3 waypoints authored + live, waypoint-travel in / fast-travel out, popup on T, world map is a map again. Suites at baseline; browser verification outstanding.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §5. Blocked by E (the data) and by B (the waypoints must be authored and reachable BEFORE the old travel is removed, or travel gets worse before it gets better).

Travel rule (Diablo/PoE waypoints). A player may travel only while standing on a waypoint they have activated. The popup lists every waypoint the character can see: activated ones are selectable travel targets, known-but-unactivated ones render distinctly and are NOT selectable.

Authorization is server-side, as with every join. A new waypoint-travel leg in mayJoin (backend/src/services/joinPolicy.js) accepts the destination only if character_waypoints holds it AND the player is standing on an activated waypoint. The client's claim is never the input — a forged frame simply omits whatever the client would have sent, which is exactly why that file authorizes every join against facts the server owns.

Arrival reuses pendingArrivals plus the existing transition frame, so the player lands on the destination waypoint's tile exactly rather than at a world spawn.

Retirement. World-map click-to-travel (SOMET-266) is removed as a travel mechanism and the fast-travel leg of mayJoin goes with it. The World Map stays as the fog-of-war view. worlds.allows_fast_travel remains as DATA — map authors use it to decide where waypoints belong — but no longer authorizes a join on its own. The transition, resume and first-join legs are untouched.

Acceptance

  • Exhaustive mayJoin table covering the new leg AND the removed one: a visited+flagged world that the character has no activated waypoint in must now be REFUSED.
  • A test that resume still works — a character logged out deep in a dungeon must not be stranded by the retirement.
  • A test that travel is refused when the player is not standing on an activated waypoint.
  • UI test: an unactivated waypoint is rendered differently and cannot be selected.
  • backend npm test, frontend npx vitest run, plus browser verification: activate two waypoints, travel between them, confirm arrival is on the destination tile, and confirm the world map no longer offers travel.

Risk. This slice removes shipped behaviour. Merge it after B and E have landed, never before.

results.name: Home Region E — waypoint data model, activation on contact, guarded-portal exclusion
results.description_html:
In Progress · 2026-08-13 · rework: enforce the exclusion against the DB inside the applier, prove the applier write, fix waypoint moves

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §5. No blockers. F depends on this.

Data.

  • New waypoints table: id, world_id, x, y, name. Authored in the map specs — one per village, plus key junctions.
  • New opt-in boolean map_links.is_waypoint (default false) so a hand-picked SAFE staircase can also serve as one. Default false is the safety property, exactly as allows_fast_travel's is; nothing is backfilled.
  • New character_waypoints (character_id, waypoint_id, activated_at). Per character, not per account — same reason character_visited_worlds is.

The load-bearing rule. A portal referenced by any creature's blocks_portal_id may NEVER be reachable as a waypoint. Without it a guarded dungeon entrance is bypassable on the second visit, and the level-band gating services/joinPolicy.js exists to protect stops holding — that hole is documented at length in migration 1714440163000_world_fast_travel.js. Revised by review: validator enforcement is not sufficient. The runtime reads the waypoints registry, not the is_waypoint flag, and the applier never converges it — so the invariant must be enforced against the DATABASE inside the applier's transaction, after the guard pass. The live-rows DB test stays, as a detector rather than as the enforcement.

Activation is physical. Walking onto a waypoint tile writes the character_waypoints row and tells the client. There is no other way to light one — no admin grant, no side effect of visiting the world.

Read API for the client: the waypoints this character may see (those in worlds it has visited), each marked activated or not. Fog rules follow GET /api/player/world-map: an unactivated waypoint in an unvisited world is not returned at all. Reviewed and confirmed sound — slice F needs no schema change.

Acceptance

  • Validator test: a spec flagging a guarded portal as a waypoint is REJECTED with a message naming the guard.
  • DB test over live rows asserting no guarded portal carries the flag.
  • Activation test: stepping on the tile writes exactly one row; stepping again does not duplicate it.
  • A test that activation does NOT happen from merely joining the world.
  • API test that an unvisited world's waypoints are absent from the payload.
  • Added by review: the guarded-portal invariant must survive a re-seed that adds a guard after the flag, or drops a guard from the spec while its creatures remain in the DB.
  • Added by review: a behavioural test that the applier actually writes waypoint rows — positions, map_link_id, and is_waypoint converging — since the current guard is a source grep satisfied by the require line alone.
  • Added by review: moving an authored waypoint must converge cleanly or fail with a message naming the cause, without leaving a ghost row and without destroying character_waypoints.
  • backend npm test.

Merge note: 'waypoints' must be added to the WORLD_KEYS allowlist introduced by SOMET-288, or every spec authoring a standalone waypoint is rejected as an unknown key.

Open for whoever authors the home-region waypoints (F): this slice ships the mechanism, not the content. The actual waypoint rows — one per village plus key junctions — still have to be authored, and F is the slice that is broken without them.

results.name: Home Region D — gate guards actually rescue a fleeing player
results.description_html:
In Progress · 2026-08-13 · picked up: guard rescue — target priority + leash tuning

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §4. No blockers.

Rebase note (added after SOMET-285 landed on main as 4a48cd4). Guards are now a fixed level 150 and players cannot damage them at all; guardStatsForWorld has become guardStats and the worlds.level_max lookup is gone. That does NOT overlap this ticket — SOMET-285 made a guard unkillable, this one makes it actually turn up. Two consequences: the "guard prefers the player-chasing hostile" change must not reintroduce any path where a guard takes a player as a target, and the leash tuning is now purely about reach, not survivability.

Why this is small. Guards already refuse to target players and already engage faction='hostile' only (backend/src/authority/creatures.js, the guard branch). So the rescue is a targeting-priority and tuning problem, not new machinery.

  • selectGuardTarget prefers a hostile that currently holds a player target over a nearer hostile that does not. A rescue must beat a wandering slime.
  • The Guard behaviour row's leash_radius (300 today, against aggro 400) rises far enough that an interception at the gate actually completes instead of stalling mid-chase. Data change in creatureBehaviors.js + a migration for live rows.

Explicitly NOT in scope: any rule that stops a hostile entering a safe region. The design is that a chaser CAN follow the player through the gate — that is what makes the rescue a moment rather than an invisible wall. Slice A's safe region is spawn-time only.

Acceptance

  • Golden trace of the rescue: player flees → crosses the gate → guard disengages its post → hostile dies → guard walks home and re-anchors at its post.
  • A test that a guard prefers the player-chasing hostile over a nearer idle one.
  • A test that the raised leash still returns the guard home — a guard that wanders off permanently is the failure mode this tuning risks.
  • A test that guards still never target a player, and that SOMET-285's player-immunity survives the priority change.
  • backend npm test, plus browser verification: get chased, run through a village gate, watch a guard kill the pursuer and return.

results.name: Home Region C — skittish creature behaviour (flees, retaliates when cornered)
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-13 · follow-ups on fix/home-region-c-followups; awaiting review, then the browser verification SOMET-289 carries

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §3. B depends on this — the pens are populated with these creatures, and the containment guarantee comes from here.

Why it is new work. There is no non-aggressive creature in this game. Every chase_style in backend/seeds/data/creatureBehaviors.js (charge, skirmish, kite, guard, hold, ambush) acquires a target. This is the one slice with genuinely new movement code.

chase_style: 'skittish', routed in backend/src/authority/creatures.js on the resolved behaviour (NOT on faction):

  • Never acquires a player while undisturbed.
  • Retreats when a player closes inside a flee radius, moving directly away, clamped by its leash so it cannot be herded across the map.
  • Switches to normal retaliation for the rest of the engagement once it takes damage OR is cornered — a retreat step terrain refuses.
  • Loses the player and returns home at leash, like every other profile.

Three level 1–2 catalog rows adopt it (Woodland, Beast and Highland Swarm — note Highland's level band is 8–10, so only the first two belong in a starting pen).

Acceptance

  • Golden trace: idle → approach → retreat → damage → retaliate → player leaves → returns home.
  • Blocked-retreat test: a creature backed against a wall retaliates instead of jittering.
  • A player can walk straight past one and take zero damage.
  • Leash test: it cannot be pulled beyond its leash by repeated approach.
  • Added by review, now done: the leash guarantee holds for a PROVOKED creature and during roam, so a penned creature cannot be walked, roamed or knocked out of its pen.
  • Added by review, now done: a creature damaged from beyond its aggro radius still retaliates, and against the actual provoker rather than a bystander.
  • Added by review, now done: the frontend chase-style list is proven to equal the backend's rather than restating a literal.
  • backend npm test, frontend npx vitest run.

What the follow-ups changed beyond skittish. The walk-home behaviour and the leash clamp are no longer guard-only: every creature with a home anchor now walks back when outside its leash, has roam steps refused by the leash, and cannot be knocked outside it. A null home is unchanged, which is every existing wild spawn. Provocation gained a source and an expiry — _provokedBy = { by, until } — so a creature remembers who shot it from out of range and never blames a bystander.

Watch for. SOMET-249's TWO-LOADER inertness trap. Review confirmed it is closed — the DB test imports the live CREATURE_JOINED_SELECT rather than retyping it.

results.name: Home Region B — author the starting region: villages, roads, pens
results.description_html:
In Progress · 2026-08-13 · picked up: author the three home-region worlds — villages, roads, pens

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §2. Unblocked 2026-08-13 — A is merged to main and C is in main.

What. The entry world (Old Trailhead) and its two direct compass neighbours become the home region. Every other world is untouched — hostile, banded, exactly as today.

results.name: Home Region A — safe-region model and hostile spawn exclusion
results.description_html:
To Review · 2026-08-13 · merged to local main; awaiting the browser verification SOMET-289 carries

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md §1. Foundation slice — B depends on it.

What. One new pure module backend/src/services/safeRegion.js answering a single question: is this tile safe?

safe(tile) = inside a village footprint
           OR within safe_road_radius tiles of a carved path cell
           OR inside an authored safe rectangle

It MUST call collectPathCells from mapService.js rather than re-deriving roads, so the safe corridor is exactly the road the player sees drawn. Same one-source-of-truth reason VILLAGE_LIMITS is shared between src/index.js and seeds/mapSpec.js instead of copied.

Consumed at spawn time only. services/worldPopulation.js populateWorld and the map-spec creature placer skip safe tiles. The creature re-roll route inherits this for free because it goes through the same placer. Nothing on the movement or tick path may consult this module — that is the design, not an oversight: a hostile already chasing a player must still be able to follow them onto the road and through the gate, which is the whole point of slice D.

Also in scope (map spec, backend/seeds/mapSpec.js): accept villages: [...] plural, keeping singular village as a one-element alias so every existing spec still validates; accept safe_road_radius. The stamper already loops cfg.villages plural (mapService.js:319), so this is a spec/validator change, not an engine one. Every village in the array still passes villageGeometryError.

Re-scoped 2026-08-13: pens: [...] has MOVED to SOMET-289, where the pens are actually authored and populated. SOMET-289 must add pens to the new WORLD_KEYS allowlist in the same change as its reader — the validator now rejects unknown world keys, and its error message says so by name.

Non-goals. No damage suppression, no PvP rule, no projectile rule, no authoring of actual content (that is B).

Acceptance

  • Unit tests over safeRegion: village interior, both edges of the road corridor (radius r safe, r+1 not), inside an authored rectangle, and a tile that is none of them.
  • A placement test over a seeded world asserting NO hostile lands on a safe tile.
  • A multi-village spec fixture validates; an existing singular-village spec still validates unchanged.
  • A village whose box breaks villageGeometryError is still rejected when it appears in the plural array.
  • Added by review: a regression test covering the field-chest / loot-map spawn path, proving the exclusion is live through the config the authority really builds — not a config re-derived inside the test.
  • Added by review: a malformed or null safe_rects entry fails loudly rather than being silently inert.
  • Added by review: seed-map.js warns when the spec's village count and the live row count disagree.
  • backend npm test from backend/.

Watch for. The repo's recorded trap is a rule that lives on only one of two write paths (SOMET-153: the seed path bypassed the route's validator and wrote the broken production data). Spawn exclusion must sit where BOTH the seed placer and populateWorld pass through it, not in one caller.

results.name: Home Region — villages, safe roads, waypoints, and death
results.description_html:
Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-home-region-design.md

Every character begins in a village, and the whole starting region reads as settled territory: several villages joined by roads hostiles never spawn on, with pockets of low-level, non-aggressive wildlife off the road to practise on. A gate with guards is where you run when something chases you. Travel is a Diablo/PoE waypoint network — walk to a waypoint once, it lights up, then travel between the ones you have lit. Dying puts you back in the last village you entered.

Decisions taken during brainstorming:

  • Several normal-sized villages joined by safe roads — NOT one giant village box. The SOMET-282 screen budget (w+h <= 10) stands.
  • "Safe" is a SPAWN-TIME rule only: hostiles are never generated there, but one already chasing you CAN follow you in. That is what the gate guards are for. No movement-path barrier.
  • Non-aggressive means SKITTISH: flees on approach, retaliates when damaged or cornered.
  • Waypoints are BOTH a new placed object AND an opt-in flag on selected safe staircases. A portal guarded via blocks_portal_id may never be flagged.
  • Death returns you to the LAST village you entered (D2 checkpoint), which may be in another world.
  • Rollout is the starting region only: entry world + its two direct neighbours. The other 83 worlds are untouched.

Slices (children): A safe-region model → B starting-region authoring (needs A, C) · C skittish behaviour · D guard rescue · E waypoint data + activation → F waypoint travel + popup UI (needs B, E) · G death-to-last-village.

Browser verification is required for B, D, F and G — the four with a surface a player can see.

results.name: Attacking a village guard is indistinguishable from swinging at air
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-13 · merged to local main and browser-verified; the cue fires and the immunity is intact

Surfaced by the SOMET-285 fix (2026-08-12) and volunteered by the implementing agent rather than left to be found by a player.

Behaviour (before): players could no longer damage village guards. The filter lives in meleeArcTargets and projectileHitsCreature, and both hit and impacts derive from those — so a swing at a guard resolved the weapon's miss effect and emitted no impact. On screen that was exactly what swinging at empty ground looks like.

Why it mattered: a player who attacked a guard got no signal that the attack was refused rather than mistimed. The natural reading is "I missed", so they swing again, and again. The behaviour was correct; only its legibility was missing.

Shipped. A gold shield glint with two deflection sparks drawn on the guard, while the weapon's whiff still draws at the attacker's feet — so a refusal and a miss differ by position alone, and a swing at empty ground still produces neither. Purely procedural canvas strokes, because no creature in this game has a sprite (all 293 entity_types rows are render_mode = 'rect'). Implemented as a client-side built-in def rather than a vfx_effects row on purpose: addEffects silently drops events whose name is not in the effect library, so a renamed or deleted row would have restored this exact bug. Covered on both refusal paths — melee arc and projectile, including the AoE _detonate branch — with the shot deliberately not stopped by a guard, since body-blocking arrows would be a new gameplay rule rather than a legibility fix.

The pinned test was updated, not deleted: guard_player_immunity.test.js now asserts "a swing at a guard is refused, and says so" — still hit:false, still kills: [], still 7005 hp, but with a blocked impact, contrasted explicitly against a swing at empty air producing impacts: [].

A false alarm worth recording. Browser verification first appeared to show the cue was inert. It was not — the probe aimed at the guard's wire x/y, its top-left corner, while inArc tests the creature centre; with CREATURE_SIZE 48 that 24 px offset is a ~47° error against a 17.2° half-arc. But chasing it found a real hole: the existing fixture took the faction === 'guard' fallback branch while the live game takes the resolveBehavior branch, so none of the 26 green tests touched the live path. guard_block_cue_db.test.js now loads a real row through the exported CREATURE_JOINED_SELECT; dropping chase_style from either the resolver or the query leaves all 26 old tests green and fails 5 of 7 new ones — and either would make every guard in the running game killable.

results.name: Any player can kill a village guard with ~300 free, riskless knife swings
results.description_html:
Found while root-causing SOMET-283 (2026-08-12). Distinct from the displacement bug fixed there, and still open.

Two facts combine badly:

1. A guard never retaliates against a player. selectGuardTarget (backend/src/authority/creatures.js) accepts only o.faction === 'hostile', and the hostile-melee branch iterates players only. Nothing in the tick makes a guard hit a player, ever.

2. Damage has a floor of 1. MIN_DAMAGE = 1 in backend/src/authority/damage.js:16-32 means Village Guard defense = 10 never fully absorbs a hit. A starter knife (damage 6, cooldown 0.25s) therefore lands exactly 1 damage per swing rather than 0.

Consequence: 300 hp ÷ 1 damage = 300 swings ≈ 75 seconds of clicking to kill a Village Guard, at zero risk — the guard cannot fight back. There is no guard respawn path either (only an admin re-roll re-inserts them), so a village can be permanently stripped of its defenders by any player with a starting weapon.

Also note the melee arc has no faction filter — applyMeleeArc/meleeArcTargets apply to any creature, which is what makes the guard a legal target in the first place.

Interacts with SOMET-279 (level-scaling guards, in progress): scaling raises guard hp and defense, which lengthens this grind but does not change its risklessness — MIN_DAMAGE guarantees any weapon eventually wins. Scaling alone is not a fix.

Options to weigh: let guards retaliate against players who strike them (most natural, but turns a village into a PvE hazard and needs care around accidental cleave); or make guards immune to player damage (simple, but removes a legitimate player choice); or give guards a respawn so the loss is temporary. Wants a product decision.

results.name: Item-types admin form cannot edit the reserved 'gold' row (no currency category)
results.description_html:
Surfaced by the SOMET-278 fix (2026-08-12), and volunteered by the implementing agent rather than left to be discovered.

Behaviour: ItemTypesAdmin.jsx's category <select> offers only weapon / ammo / armor (see ELEMENTS/category handling in frontend/src/games/something2/itemTypeForm.js). The seeded gold row is category: 'currency'. Opening it in the admin form therefore submits some other category, and SOMET-278's new reserved guard now rejects that with a 409 — where previously it was a misleading 400.

Net effect: the gold row is safe from accidental destruction (which is the point of SOMET-278) but is also uneditable through the UI, including its harmless fields such as icon and sprite. The API accepts a correct PUT that keeps category: 'currency'; only the form cannot express one.

Fix: teach the form about the currency category — either add it to the select, or detect a reserved row and render its category read-only while leaving the safe fields editable. The second is probably better: it communicates why the field is locked instead of offering a category that will be refused.

Not urgent: nothing in normal operation requires editing the gold row, and the guard failing closed is the correct direction for a defect that could otherwise switch off the economy.

results.name: Unexplained: what displaced Vale Crossing's guards 1.7k/3.8k px off their posts?
results.description_html:
Raised during the SOMET-154 validation pass (2026-08-12). The recovery is fixed; the cause is not identified, and this ticket exists so the fix does not quietly bury the question.

What was observed: both Vale Crossing village guards were persisted far outside their leash — (2949.32, 4608.28) with home (3250, 2950), ~1685 px; and (277.34, 5345.53) with home (3250, 3050), ~3755 px. Leash radius is 300 px. updated_at 2026-08-07, so the authority wrote those positions (backend/src/authority/server.js:909).

What was ruled out: the initial hypothesis was that the return step is unbounded and lets a guard drift. That was tested and is false — greedy steering aims each axis at the post and a 2 px per-tick step cannot overshoot, so distance-to-post is monotonically non-increasing. A sweep of every walkable start in a 2200–4300 px box around the village under the pre-fix code measured a maximum outward drift of exactly 0 px. The chase step was already leash-clamped.

So something else moved them. Candidates, none confirmed: knockback (neither backend/src/authority/world.js:426-434 for player melee nor backend/src/authority/projectiles.js:160,261 faction-filters or leash-clamps its shove, so a player can freely punt a guard); a terrain regenerate/re-roll that moved the village box under stationary guards; or a spawn/respawn path writing a position without reference to home_x/home_y.

Why it still matters now that recovery works: SOMET-154's fix walks a stranded guard home, so the gate self-heals. But a guard that can be punted 3.7 km is a guard a player can deliberately pull off the gate before an attack, and the walk back is slow. Worth finding the mechanism and bounding it at the source.

Where to start: add a leash clamp plus a faction filter to the knockback sites, then check whether the live displacement is reproducible by shoving a guard repeatedly.

results.name: Entry world has no village — the entry_spawn seam from Slice A was never built
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-153 validation pass (2026-08-12). Carved out of Slice A so that slice could close on the criteria it actually delivered.

What SOMET-153 asked for: "First village's spawn point feeds Epic I entry_spawn (is_entry map)."

What exists: nothing links a village spawn to worlds.entry_spawn. Every writer of that column — backend/src/index.js:2291, backend/scripts/seed-map.js:170, backend/scripts/dungeon/gen-p5-map-content.js:355 — sets it independently of villages. The Slice A plan doc explicitly descoped this.

Live state: the only is_entry world, Old Trailhead, has no village at all. Its entry_spawn is {3250,3250}. So a brand-new player starts in a world with no safe zone, no bind point, no guards and no merchant — the entire Villages & economy epic is invisible until they walk two worlds west to Vale Crossing.

Also unresolved here — the ≤1/4-screen size limit. VILLAGE_LIMITS allows 8×6 tiles at 100 px/tile. Against the 1280×720 budget of 230,400 px²: world-pixel footprint 800×600 = 480,000 px² (208%); on-screen isometric bounding box (ISO_K 0.64, translate-only camera) 896×448 = 401,408 px² (174%); painted parallelogram area 196,608 px² (85%). So it holds only under the third reading. The plan doc asserts the limit satisfies the constraint with no computation shown. Decision needed: pick the reading that governs, and if it is either of the first two, tighten VILLAGE_LIMITS — noting that the three live 6×5 hub villages already exceed the bounding-box budget.

results.name: Admin item value edit does not reprice existing merchant stock
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-156 validation pass (2026-08-12).

Defect: merchant_stock.price is a snapshot of item_types.value taken at seed time (backend/src/services/merchantStock.js:38 and :59). PUT /api/item-types/:id (backend/src/index.js:881-916) updates value but never re-prices existing rows — unlike POST, which does call seedItemAcrossVillages (index.js:872). Meanwhile the sell price is computed live from item_types.value (backend/src/authority/trade.js:151-157).

Consequence: the two sides of the trade drift apart. An admin raising a sword's value from 10 to 1000 leaves every village still selling it at 10 while the merchant pays at least 500 for it — buy low, sell high, unbounded gold for every player, triggered by an ordinary catalog edit with no warning.

No drift today: SELECT confirms 0 rows where ms.price <> it.value. This is latent, not live.

Fix: re-price base-catalog rows on value change (buyback rows must keep their historical price — that price is the seller's contract). Simplest is to have the PUT path call the same seeding helper the POST path already uses.

results.name: Buyback stock is village-wide, not seller-scoped — snipeable, plus a CHA resale arbitrage
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-156 validation pass (2026-08-12). Needs a product decision, not just a patch.

Behaviour: fetchShop (backend/src/services/merchantStock.js:77-87) filters buyback rows on village_id and expiry only — never seller_user_id = requesting user. buyStock (backend/src/authority/trade.js:24-27) likewise never compares seller_user_id to the buyer. This appears deliberate — RenderSystem.js:1039 and :1137-1139 describe the list as other players' sold items. The Slice D plan doc states no policy either way; its goal line only says items "can be repurchased".

Tension with the AC: SOMET-156 says "the player can buy them back". Today another player can snipe your gear inside the 3-day window, and the buyback promise silently fails for the seller with no notification.

Secondary — CHA arbitrage: the row price is the seller's payout, but a resale pays out using the buyer's priceMult (backend/src/services/playerStats.js:55-58, cap SELL_FRACTION_MAX = 0.9). A high-CHA player buys a base-CHA player's row at 0.5·value and resells at 0.9·value, minting 0.4·value per item. Not an infinite loop — a repeat cycle nets 0, and catalog-buy at value then sell at ≤0.9·value always loses, so SELL_FRACTION_MAX still bounds total gold — but it makes the CHA sell bonus transferable between accounts, which it is not meant to be. Respec exists (backend/src/api/progressionRoutes.js:97), so no alt is even needed: sell at base CHA, respec into CHA, buy your own row back cheap, resell.

Decision needed: either scope buyback to the seller (matching the AC wording) and drop the shared-market framing, or keep the shared market deliberately and reword the AC — but then price resales off the row rather than the buyer's CHA.

results.name: Village guards are not level-scaled — 1 damage against high-level hostiles
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-154 validation pass (2026-08-12).

Defect: insertVillageGuards (backend/src/services/villages.js:34-45) hardcodes hp 300, and the Village Guard uses a flat damage_override: 25 with defense 10 from entity_types. Guard rows are always level 1. Hostiles, by contrast, ARE level-scaled by the per-world level bands (SOMET-241).

Consequence: The Abyss: Hub has a village whose hostiles sit at level 46-50 — e.g. Void Line, hp 251, defense 27.5. applyDamage is raw - defense floored at MIN_DAMAGE = 1 (backend/src/authority/damage.js:16-32), so the guard's 25 damage lands as 1. Simulated over 600 s: the Void Line lost 5 hp of 251 while guard hp never moved. Not a stalemate so much as a ten-minute standoff that accomplishes nothing — the guards are decorative in exactly the worlds where they would matter most.

Fix direction: scale guard hp/damage/defense with the village's world level band the same way hostiles are scaled, so a guard stays meaningfully "powerful" (SOMET-154's word) at any tier.

results.name: Reserved 'gold' item type is deletable by admin, silently killing the economy
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-155 validation pass (2026-08-12).

Defect: backend/src/index.js:917-926 deletes an item type behind adminGuard only — no reserved-name check and no reference check. Contrast the entity-types DELETE at index.js:745-757, which does return a 409 on references. world_items_item_type_id_fkey is ON DELETE CASCADE.

Repro: DELETE /api/item-types/28 (the seeded gold row, category currency) as admin → 204. Every gold pile on every map cascades away. Live worlds keep a stale entry.goldItemTypeId resolved once at world load (backend/src/authority/server.js:434), so further gold inserts fail on the FK; after a restart resolveGoldItemTypeId (backend/src/authority/items.js:88-90) returns null, loot.js:203 stops spawning gold entirely, and nothing is logged. The economy is simply off.

Rename is only accidentally blocked: validateItemType (index.js:776) rejects any category outside weapon/armor/ammo, so a PUT carrying the row's real category currency 400s with a misleading message. An admin who instead sets category:'armor' plus a slot and defense can rename it, permanently breaking resolveGoldItemTypeId's name === 'gold' match.

Fix: add a reserved-name guard plus a reference check to the item-types DELETE and PUT, mirroring the entity-types handler rather than writing a second variant.

results.name: Gold faucet: sell starting loadout, delete character, repeat
results.description_html:
Found during the SOMET-156 validation pass (2026-08-12). Unbounded gold generation.

Why the existing guard misses it: the starting_loadout_granted_at guard (added by migration 1714440035000) moved from users to characters in backend/migrations/1714440092000_characters.js:42, and is enforced per-character at backend/src/authority/items.js:169-193. It correctly closes the original sell-then-reconnect exploit. But gold is per-account (users.gold, see backend/src/authority/server.js:1063 and backend/src/authority/trade.js:161) while the loadout flag is per-character — so destroying the character resets the flag while the gold stays.

Repro: create a Warrior → join → walk to a village merchant → sell short sword (value 32) and leather-vest (16) → +24 gold → DELETE /api/characters/:id → create another Warrior → repeat. deleteCharacter (backend/src/services/characters.js:129-138) has no cooldown and createCharacter (:91-127) refills the slot immediately. MAX_CHARACTERS = 8 bounds concurrency, not rate. Ranger adds an arrow for +1.

Possible fixes (needs a product call): make the loadout grant per-account rather than per-character; or make starting-loadout items unsellable; or give them zero value; or apply a cooldown to slot reuse. Each has different consequences for legitimate re-rolls, so this wants a decision rather than a quick patch.

results.name: GET /api/worlds is unauthenticated and returns every world — defeats fog of war
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · role-scoped projection lands via PR #13 (46b3261) — unauthenticated access refused, players get an allowlist-withheld projection for unvisited worlds

Problem

backend/src/index.js — app.get('/api/worlds', ...) had no guard at all. Not adminGuard, not even requireAuth. The handler was SELECT * FROM worlds ORDER BY created_at DESC, so it returned every column of every world to anyone who asked.

Why it mattered

SOMET-263 goes to real trouble to hide this: the player world-map endpoint returns unvisited neighbours as { id, unvisited: true } with no name, specifically so the graph "shows an anonymous grey stub rather than spoiling what lies through the door". That whole design was undone by an unauthenticated endpoint that handed over every world name, seed, level band and entry spawn in one request.

Fix

Both GET /api/worlds and GET /api/worlds/:id now require auth and project the response by role — admin unchanged, player gets an explicit content-field allowlist withheld for unvisited worlds, with the two mechanically load-bearing fields (chunk_size, is_entry) always visible so doorway travel and first-login auto-join keep working.

results.name: Backend suite is flaky under parallel load (3+ tests, different subset each run)
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · all 3 named flakes root-caused and closed, merged via PR #17 (cc032cc)

Backlog · 2026-08-11 · observed across six full runs while closing SOMET-274

Problem

A full npm test against a real database fails a small, different subset of tests on nearly every run. Each one passes in isolation. Observed so far:

• authority_server.test.js — "a burst beyond the token bucket capacity is dropped, not queued for later" (2 of 6 runs)
• seed_map_db.test.js — "applying a spec twice produces identical rows" (2 of 6)
• "a guard-blocked portal refuses transfer and knocks the player back" (1 of 6)

Only seed_map_db.test.js's "every shipped spec applies cleanly" fails every run, and that one is real — SOMET-273 (now resolved and confirmed permanently expected).

Resolution

All 3 named flakes root-caused (not just retried until green) and fixed: a real production rate-limiter bug (|| vs ??), a missing advisory-lock conversion, a fixed-sleep-vs-real-latency test race, plus a structural lock-timeout fix that let the underlying mechanism actually degrade gracefully instead of the whole file dying first.

results.name: Repair the 18 progression tests stranded by the character-keyed schema
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · 45/45 progression tests; fixture leak fixed and confirmed over six full runs; commit 9044e56

Problem

SOMET-257 moved player_progression off the account and onto the character. Five progression test files were never updated, so 18 tests have been failing continuously since then. They were treated as "pre-existing failures" and filtered out of every test run during SOMET-266, which means anything new landing in progression would hide in that noise.

Failures

15 in progression_store.test.js (fixtures pass a user id to character-keyed loadProgression / awardXp / allocateStat / applyDeath, hitting player_progression_character_fk); 2 in progression_migration.test.js (query a dropped user_id column); 1 in progression_kill_xp.test.js (no live player in the world, so the XP path is skipped and the forced-failure assertion never fires).

Acceptance criteria

1. All five progression test files pass against a real database.
2. No assertion is weakened or deleted to get there; any assertion whose premise the schema change invalidated is replaced with a real invariant, not a vacuous one.
3. No test fixture leaks rows into the shared dev database.

results.name: B3 — travel from the map, and server-side join authorization
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · browser-verified end to end; the three defects that exercise found are fixed in 66b5f3e

Clicking a green world on the player World Map enters it. The map offers only worlds that are visited and flagged — and the authority now decides the same question for itself.

The security-relevant half

A join frame is {type:'join', world_id, character_id} over a socket the player already holds, and the handler asked only "is this character yours" and "does this world exist". Any of the 86 world ids succeeded, including a band 47-50 dungeon room behind a portal guard the character had never met. The map feature does not create that hole, but it is the first feature whose whole premise is that some worlds are reachable and some are not.

services/joinPolicy.js authorizes every join, deliberately not a client-supplied fast_travel: true intent — a forged frame simply omits the flag, so an intent-keyed check gates only well-behaved clients. Five legs, all from server-owned facts:

  • admin — the world picker is existing admin tooling. Role read from the DB row the token-version check already fetches, never from the JWT claim (a token minted before a demotion still carries the old role).
  • transition — pendingArrivals, set by the tick loop when it commits a portal crossing. Also what keeps a legitimate arrival working when the fire-and-forget recordVisit beside it fails.
  • resume — where you logged out, flag or no flag. Logging out deep in a dungeon must not strand a character outside it.
  • fast-travel — visited AND flagged. Either half alone is a bypass.
  • first-join — a character with no history, into an entry or flagged world. Dies the moment the character has been anywhere.

Fails closed: a DB error while gathering the facts refuses the join.

Acceptance criteria — all demonstrated

  • Clicking a visited, flagged world enters it. ✅ browser
  • A visited but unflagged world is visibly distinct and inert on click. ✅
  • An unvisited stub reveals no travel information — the flag is emitted for visited worlds only. ✅
  • Fast travel cannot place a character inside a portal-guarded dungeon it has not walked into. ✅ forged join frame, live socket
  • The map stays read-only in the editing sense. ✅

Evidence — live authority, real socket, real test account

PASS [allow]  resume into last world (Old Trailhead)  -> joined at 4617,5991
PASS [refuse] forged join into an unvisited dungeon   -> error: you cannot travel there

Browser: map renders correctly, clicking Old Trailhead enters it, character still there 14s later and persisted at 6268,3200. Backend 1688 pass / 20 fail (18 pre-existing progression fixtures, the known mire spec failure, and a token-bucket test flaky only under full-suite load — 47/47 in isolation). Frontend 761 pass.

Three defects the browser found, all green in both suites

  1. No Game instance off the game route. A direct load of /game/map left gameRef null forever, so every travel click silently did nothing.
  2. Auto-join raced travel once (1) was fixed, dragging the character back to its stale last world seconds after arriving.
  3. Travel bounced straight back. A saved position is usually the doorway the character walked out through; it fired on arrival. Never travel-only — plain login-resume (SOMET-267) had the same bug since it shipped.

Also in this item

  • Game.initChunked rejects its join promise on a server rejection received before joined, instead of sitting until the 5s timeout and reporting "authority join timeout" with the real reason already gone past in a toast.
  • GameShell.enterWorld returns whether the player actually arrived, so the map navigates to the canvas only on success.

Two test-hygiene defects found on the way

  • join_policy_db.test.js leaked its fixtures into the shared dev database: t.after hooks run in registration order, so pool.end() ran before the cleanup deletes, which threw into their own .catch(() => {}).
  • join_policy.test.js's helper spread a partial facts object over the merged defaults, so three assertions passed on the first-join leg rather than the one they name.

results.name: B2 — classify all 86 worlds: 30 surface worlds opt in to fast travel
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · all 30 live (25 seeded + hub-vale's 5 by migration)

Content work. Written into the 4 checked-in map specs (reviewable in a diff, survives a re-seed) — not applied by hand to live rows, which is how is_entry was lost.

The rule, derived rather than guessed

A dungeon room is never a travel target, discriminated by the naming convention the content already uses: ^The <Dungeon>: <Room>$. Checked against the link topology instead of trusted — compass-connected component analysis yields 9 clusters, and the pattern matches all 56 rooms across the six dungeon chains while correctly excluding "The Deep Cut".

Neither signal alone works. Components 2 and 3 mix p5 surface worlds with the Catacombs and Underdeep chains; component 1's Catacomb Threshold and Sealed Mausoleum read like dungeon interiors but are band 1-1 surface terrain with zero portal mouths.

Result

30 of 86 worlds opt in (hub-vale 5, loop-catacombs 7, p5-descent 10, spine-descent 8). Nothing becomes newly reachable: every flagged world is compass-walkable surface, so travel skips walking, not gating. Entering a dungeon still means passing its portal and its guard.

Acceptance criteria

  • map_spec_fixtures.test.js pins the invariant, not the curation: no dungeon room is a travel target, however the list is later revised — with a non-vacuity check so deleting every flag cannot make it pass trivially.
  • All 4 specs still pass validateMapSpec.
  • Diff is exactly 30 insertions with no other lines touched.

How the 30 actually reached the database

25 by seeding three specs. hub-vale cannot be applied at all and cannot be corrected — its live topology has no valid grid embedding, so validateMapSpec can never accept a truthful version (SOMET-273). Its 5 ship as migration 1714440164000, with a test pinning the migration's hardcoded names against the spec so the two cannot drift.

Still open

Whether the flag should be combined with level. A level-1 character may fast-travel to Glacier's End (band 9-12) — somewhere it could already walk, so this is a pacing question rather than a gating hole. Carried on SOMET-272.

results.name: B1 — worlds.allows_fast_travel, seedable from the map specs
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · column live, seeder verified against the dev database

The column that gates map travel, copied from how is_entry already works. default: false is the security property: a world added later is not a travel target until someone says so.

Acceptance criteria

  • NOT NULL boolean defaulting to false, asserted against the live schema rather than inferred from the migration source.
  • A newly created world is not a travel target.
  • Re-seeding a spec sets the flag to the spec's value; a world whose spec omits the key ends up false, not null.
  • The migration flags nothing — classification is B2's job and needs judgement.

Deliberately NOT copied from is_entry

seed-map.js clears is_entry on every other world before setting its own, and all 4 specs each assert an entry world — so the last seed wins. That is a bug waiting to happen for is_entry; the new flag is not mutually exclusive and has no "clear the others" step. (That is_entry hazard was separately fixed under SOMET-265.)

Half-wiring guarded

The column must appear in both halves of the upsert. Present in the INSERT but missing from the ON CONFLICT SET works on a fresh database and silently stops updating on every re-seed after that.

One test revised after seeding

world_fast_travel_db.test.js asserted zero flagged worlds, which was only correct while nothing had been seeded. It now asserts the property that has to hold forever — no dungeon room is flagged in the live rows — which is the live counterpart to the spec-level invariant and catches a hand-edited row no spec test can see.

results.name: A2 — backfill character_visited_worlds from world_players
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · applied live; pre-existing characters now have a populated World Map

SOMET-263 created character_visited_worlds empty and records visits only from that point forward, so every character predating it shows "You have not been anywhere yet" permanently. Live evidence when found: the admin account's character had 10 world_players rows and 0 visit rows.

A world_players row is evidence of a visit — only the authority's persist() writes that table, and only for a player actually in the world.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every world a character has stood in becomes a visit row.
  • Re-running the migration does not duplicate rows or move timestamps.
  • first_seen_at carries world_players.updated_at, never now().

Knowingly approximate

updated_at is when the character was last there, not first. It is the only evidence that survived, nothing currently renders the timestamp, and a wrong-but-ordered value preserves the relative order of exploration that now() would flatten to a single instant. If a "first discovered" date is ever surfaced, backfilled rows will be wrong — carried as an open question on SOMET-272.

down is deliberately empty: a rollback cannot tell a backfilled row from one earned by playing afterwards, and deleting the latter would destroy real history.

Why review missed it

Verification used a freshly-created character, for which an empty map is the correct answer. The fixture hid the bug.

results.name: A1 — resume the world you logged out of, not the entry world
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · browser-verified; the doorway-bounce defect it exposed is fixed in 66b5f3e

Auto-join called pickEntryWorld unconditionally. That answers "where does a brand-new character start", which is a different question from "where does this character resume" — so a character that left through a doorway came back with the right coordinates in the wrong world, and the authority then read world_players for the entry world.

Acceptance criteria

  • A character with a last world resumes into it at its saved position.
  • A character with no history still falls back to the entry world.
  • The last world is membership-checked against the loaded world list — a world deleted from another session must not produce a join the server refuses, because a refused join never sends joined and the client would hang rather than surface an error.

Files

frontend/src/games/something2/autoJoin.js, GameShell.jsx, backend/src/services/characters.js (exposes lastWorldId from the LATERAL join that already computed it)

Trap this hit

The guard has to be on the call site. autoJoinTarget can prefer the last world all it likes, but the pure-function test passes the value explicitly and stays green even when GameShell never supplies it — the argument arrives undefined and every player silently resumes into the entry world.

Second trap, found in the browser

"Resumes at its saved position" was true for one tick and then false: a saved position is very often the doorway the character walked out through, and it fired on arrival and threw the character into the neighbouring world. Both suites were green. Fixed by the arrival latch (suppressArrivalDoorway).

results.name: Map-based fast travel & login-resume fixes (SOMET-256 follow-on)
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · all six children (A1/A2/B1-B4 = SOMET-267…272) Done; SOMET-272's rules decided, SOMET-273's navigability defect fixed

Follow-on to SOMET-256. Raised by the user report "I have selected character but I still can't login to map", which turned out to be four compounding problems, not one.

What was actually wrong

  1. Auto-join always targeted the is_entry world and ignored where the character logged out — a defect against the agreed SOMET-256 requirement.
  2. character_visited_worlds was created empty, so every character predating SOMET-263 had a permanently blank World Map. Missed in review because verification used a fresh character, for which an empty map is correct.
  3. No world has is_entry set in the live database (SOMET-265) — a regression, not a missing feature.
  4. The World Map was read-only by design, but the user expected it to be the entry surface: click a world, go there.

Plans

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-login-resume-and-visited-backfill.md (the two defect fixes, sequenced first so the classification work could not strand them) and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-map-fast-travel.md (the travel feature).

Design decision that shapes everything below

Travel targets are opt-in per world via worlds.allows_fast_travel, default false — not "anywhere you have been". Seven creatures carry blocks_portal_id to gate dungeon entrances, and level bands run 1-1 to 47-50; letting a character teleport back into any room it once walked through would make both mechanics decorative. Default-false preserves the gating by construction rather than by a rule someone has to remember.

Resolution

All six children Done. SOMET-272 (B4) decided: no combat blocking, no cost/cooldown, no level gating change, saved-position arrival unchanged, admin access unchanged — all resolved to "keep current behavior." SOMET-273 (hub-vale unseedable / Blackfen Sinks sealed pocket) fixed via PR #11.
