results.name: No world has is_entry set — auto-join is dead in the dev database
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · code fix already landed on main in a prior session; reconciled after re-verifying live DB + tests

Found while browser-verifying SOMET-256. Pre-existing; NOT caused by that branch.

Symptom

A non-admin player who logs in is supposed to spawn straight into the canonical entry world instead of seeing a world picker. That never happens on the current dev database: they land on the raw world list.

Cause

autoJoinTarget (frontend/src/games/something2/autoJoin.js) delegates to pickEntryWorld, which returns the world flagged is_entry and otherwise falls back to a world named Overworld. The dev database satisfies neither:

SELECT count(*) FROM worlds;                      -- 86\nSELECT count(*) FROM worlds WHERE is_entry;       -- 0\nSELECT count(*) FROM worlds WHERE name='Overworld'; -- 0

So pickEntryWorld returns null and auto-join can never fire, regardless of the rest of the readiness chain.

The Overworld fallback exists because 1714440025000_users.js seeds a world of that name; the current map set was seeded from checked-in specs instead and neither carries the flag nor uses that name.

Why it matters

It is invisible to an admin — admins keep the world picker by design, so the whole class of "player auto-join" behaviour is unexercised in normal use here. It also confounds testing: during SOMET-256 verification, world entry had to be driven manually through the picker because auto-join could not be triggered at all.

Suggested fix

Set is_entry on whichever world is intended as the start (Old Trailhead, seed 1001, is the plausible candidate — it is level band 1-2 and has no inbound-only links), and decide whether the map-seed specs should carry an entry flag so a re-seed cannot drop it again. Worth a guard so the system cannot end up with zero entry worlds silently.

Do not fix by writing to shared world rows ad hoc — this should go through the seed specs, per the map-seed tooling conventions.

Acceptance

  • Exactly one world has is_entry true.
  • A freshly logged-in player with a character auto-joins it without touching the picker.
  • A re-seed cannot leave the system with zero entry worlds.

results.name: H — seeded test player, test-user-readme.md, and browser verification
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · batch gate: test account drove the whole browser pass; gate itself missed the SOMET-262 world-picker leak, recorded

Slice H of SOMET-256. Spec §9 and §10.

Depends on: F, G. Closes the epic.

Test account

backend/migrations/<next>_seed_test_player.js — a no-op unless SEED_TEST_USER=1. An environment that does not opt in cannot have this account, so a password committed to the repository can never be a live login.

When enabled it:

  • creates testplayer with role player, bcrypt at 12 rounds (matching 1714440025000_users.js)
  • creates one slot-1 Warrior for it, so login-resume is testable immediately, leaving 7 slots free to exercise creation and deletion
  • down deletes the user; the FK cascade removes the character and its state

backend/migrations/test-user-readme.md documents the credentials, the env flag, how to enable it in the repo-root .env, and states plainly that the account cannot exist without the flag.

Acceptance criteria — migration

  • Without SEED_TEST_USER, migrating up creates no user. Verified by a test, not by inspection.
  • With the flag, the account and its Warrior exist and the account can log in.
  • Re-running the migration is idempotent.
  • The readme states the dev-only constraint explicitly.

Browser verification — required before the epic is Done

Static tests here have repeatedly gone green over real defects: an inert stamina bar, unfireable ammo, walls rendering as flat background. A green suite is not evidence.

  1. Confirm the stack is serving fresh code first. A stale bundle or backend has faked a clean pass on this project before — check before trusting anything below.
  2. Log in as testplayer; create a Mage; confirm the staff loadout, not the Warrior one.
  3. Walk to a distinct position, hard-refresh, confirm the exact resume position.
  4. Confirm the World Map shows only visited worlds and anonymous stubs; walk a portal and confirm the new world appears.
  5. Confirm /game/maps redirects for a player and that no admin tab is reachable.
  6. Create up to 8 characters, confirm the 9th is refused, delete one, confirm a new one can be created.

results.name: G — fog-of-war world map: visited tracking, player endpoint, PlayerWorldMap, nav
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · batch gate: 3 named visited + 4 anonymous stubs read from the live graph; both admin routes redirect; portal-walk still unwalked

Slice G of SOMET-256. Spec §7 and §8.

Depends on: D.

Tracking

character_visited_worlds(character_id, world_id, first_seen_at), PK (character_id, world_id).

The write happens on both entry paths — the join handler and the transition handler — through a single shared helper, with a test asserting both call sites invoke it. This is a deliberate guard against the two-loader inertness trap: a feature wired into one of two paths passes its tests and is dead in half of real play.

Endpoint

GET /api/player/world-map?character_id= (requireAuth + ownership) returns:

  • visited worlds: id, name, graph_x, graph_y, is_entry, level band
  • the links among visited worlds
  • each directly-linked unvisited neighbour as { id, unvisited: true } — no name, so the graph shows an anonymous grey stub rather than spoiling what lies through the door
  • currentWorldId

Component

A new slim PlayerWorldMap.jsx sharing frontend/src/games/something2/mapGraphLayout.js, not a readOnly prop threaded through the 37KB MapGraphAdmin. Two reasons: fog of war needs a different data source anyway, and a read-only flag through an admin component is one missed branch away from leaking an edit affordance.

No edgehandles, no drag-persist, no forms. Pan, zoom, click-to-inspect only. react-cytoscapejs fits once at mount — known behaviour from the map-link graph work, not something to fight.

Navigation

entrypathplayeradmin
Game View/gameyesyes
World Map/game/mapyesyes
Tile Types / Entities / Items / Maps / Biomes / Creature Behaviorsvarious—yes
World Map Editor/game/world-map—yes

The existing entry is relabelled "World Map Editor" so the two stay distinguishable. /game/map is not wrapped in RequireAdmin. frontend/src/ui/__tests__/navRoutes.test.js keeps the table and App.jsx in sync.

Hiding tabs is UI tidiness, not the security boundary — the admin HTTP routes are already behind requireAdmin (backend/src/index.js:102) and stay that way.

Acceptance criteria

  • A fresh character sees only its starting world plus anonymous stubs.
  • Walking through a portal adds the destination on the next map view, proving the transition path writes — not just the join path.
  • An unvisited world's name is absent from the API response, not merely hidden by the component.
  • The player map renders no edit affordance: assert absence of the create/delete/drag handlers, not the presence of a read-only flag.
  • A player requesting another character's map gets 403.
  • A player navigating directly to /game/maps or /game/world-map is redirected.

results.name: F — CharacterSelect UI, active-character lifecycle, HUD switch
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · all 3 commits (isAdmin gate, recovery panel, gameEpoch rebuild) validated; 88/772 frontend tests pass

Slice F of SOMET-256. Spec §6.

Depends on: C, D (both Done).

What

/game (GameShell)\n  no active character → <CharacterSelect>\n  active character    → <canvas> + HUD   (existing path, unchanged)
  • Active character id in localStorage under something2.activeCharacterId, cleared on signOut — otherwise the next account on that browser inherits a stale id and is bounced by the ownership check.
  • On mount the stored id is validated against GET /api/characters; a character deleted elsewhere falls back to the list rather than a failed join.
  • "Change character" closes the socket and returns to the list.
  • Admins go through the same gate, then their existing world picker — which is now actually gated on isAdmin rather than merely painted over by the character gate.
  • Create form disabled at 8/8 with a visible reason; the server enforces it regardless.

Acceptance criteria

  • Zero characters → the list with a reachable create form, never a blank canvas.
  • Reload goes straight back in without re-picking.
  • Sign out, sign in as another account → the list, not the previous account's character.
  • A stored id for a deleted character → the list, no error to dismiss.
  • "Change character" disconnects cleanly and re-joining works without a reload.
  • At 8/8 the create control is disabled and explains why.
  • ✅ A player-role account never sees the world picker or any world name it has not visited. (UI closed here; the API-level disclosure is SOMET-276.)

vitest runs in a node environment — no component here can be rendered in a test. Branching lives in characterSession.js; the wiring is held by source-text guards in worldsPickerAdminGating.test.js, which are mutation-checked rather than merely green. Slice H's browser pass is the only place these components actually execute.

results.name: E — login spawn: nearest-portal fallback when the saved position is invalid
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · batch gate: saved-position path verified live; nearest-portal fallback rests on automated coverage only

Slice E of SOMET-256. Spec §5.

Depends on: nothing.

What

1. pending doorway/portal arrival          (unchanged)
2. saved world_players position            — if still valid
3. nearest PORTAL in that world            — NEW
4. entry_spawn / bounded centre / chunk centre   (unchanged)

Valid = inside the world's current bounds and all four corners of the 64px player box on walkable ground. Injected ServerMap.isWalkable, not a third copy of the collision rule.

Nearest portal = minimum Euclidean distance over map_links WHERE edge = 'PORTAL' AND from_world_id = $1. A relocation is logged: a spike means a world was resized or regenerated in a way that stranded the players saved inside it.

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ Valid saved position spawns exactly there (the common case does not regress).
  • ✅ Out of bounds after a shrink → nearest portal.
  • ✅ Now-blocked tile → nearest portal.
  • ✅ Nearest of several, verified against hand-computed distances.
  • ✅ No portals → existing behaviour unchanged.
  • ✅ Footprint, not a point: a box overhanging a blocked tile is rejected.
  • ✅ loadSpawn proven to actually supply portals and walkability.

results.name: D — authority: join by character, per-character state, per-class loadout
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · batch gate: joined as a character with per-character position verified against live rows; unauthorized world join refused

Slice D of SOMET-256. Spec §4.

Depends on: A, B. Blocks: F, G.

What

  • The WS join frame requires character_id, verified against the token's user before anything is loaded. No "default to the first character" fallback — a silent default would turn a client bug or a forged frame into a successful join as somebody else's character.
  • The in-memory World stays keyed by userId; every database write takes characterId. Both live on the player object.
  • One live session per account — the kick rule is unchanged.
  • pendingArrivals is keyed by character: a transition is a fact about the character that walked through the door.
  • gold alone stays per-user.
  • /api/progression gained a required character_id with an ownership check.

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ A character_id belonging to another user is refused and loads nothing.
  • ✅ A missing or malformed id is refused, not defaulted.
  • ✅ Two characters on one account have independent position, bind, progression, inventory and equipment; gold is shared.
  • ✅ Position persists on socket close and on the flush timer, both keyed by character.
  • ✅ Second join on one socket still refused; same-user new socket still kicks the old session.

Known behaviour change

A killer who disconnects between the killing blow and the commit earns no XP. onCreatureDeath already required that live player to push a level-up, so this is not a new dependency, but it is a narrow regression from the previous behaviour.

results.name: A — characters schema, backfill, and down-migration test
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-11 · batch gate: schema live and carrying real per-character state; SOMET-274 added a test proving the progression re-key bites

Slice A of SOMET-256. Spec §1.

Depends on: SOMET-258 (inverted during planning — the backfill needs the Warrior class to exist). Blocks: C, D.

What

The characters table, and a re-key of all five player-state tables onto it. The 8-slot cap is a schema invariant: a COUNT(*) check is racy, so slot smallint CHECK (slot BETWEEN 1 AND 8) plus UNIQUE(user_id, slot) makes a ninth character unrepresentable.

  • world_players: PK → (world_id, character_id)
  • player_binds, player_progression: PK → character_id
  • player_equipment: PK → (character_id, slot)
  • player_items: index → character_id

users.gold stays (account-wide). users.starting_loadout_granted_at moved to characters.

Verified against real data

Applied to a dev database holding 9 users / 19 world_players / 8 progression / 14 items. Every count unchanged afterwards, every row reachable through a backfilled character, the one stateless account correctly given none.

Acceptance criteria

  • ✅ Migration applies cleanly on a populated database; no row lost.
  • ✅ A ninth character is rejected by the database, not by application code.
  • ✅ Concurrent creates racing for the last slot yield 8 and one violation.
  • ✅ down re-keys the lowest slot back; lossy for multi-character accounts, said so in the migration.
  • ✅ characters_migration.test.js pins the backfill ordering.

results.name: Player characters & player-facing game view
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · all eight children (A–H) Done, including F's fix; epic acceptance demonstrated end to end

Epic. Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-player-characters-design.md (commit 9657d0c).

Goal

Give the game a real character concept and a player-facing surface. Today one account is one player: position, respawn bind, progression, inventory and equipment all hang off users.id, so an account has exactly one playthrough.

  • Up to 8 characters per account. Position, bind, progression, inventory and equipment become per-character; gold stays account-wide.
  • Creation picks a name and a class (Warrior / Ranger / Mage) driving base stats and starting gear.
  • Login resumes at the character's exact logout position, falling back to the nearest portal when that position is no longer valid.
  • A player sees exactly two tabs: Game View and a read-only fog-of-war World Map (visited worlds only).
  • A seeded test player, env-gated so its committed password can never be a live login.

Out of scope

  • Sprites for the three classes — coding agents cannot generate images. The new entity types will render as placeholder colour boxes until sprites are generated locally. Expected, not a defect.
  • Class-gated abilities or gear; XP-curve rebalance; character rename/transfer; an account bank UI.

Children

A → H, in dependency order. A carries the risk (it re-keys five tables); everything after it is additive. E is independent and can land first.

Epic acceptance

All eight children Done, and browser verification passes: log in as the test player, create a Mage, confirm the staff loadout (not the Warrior one), walk, hard-refresh, confirm the exact resume position, confirm the World Map shows only visited worlds, confirm /game/maps redirects for a player.

A seeded test player, env-gated so its committed password can never be a live login.

Sprites for the three classes — coding agents cannot generate images. The new entity types will render as placeholder colour boxes until sprites are generated locally. Expected, not a defect.
Class-gated abilities or gear; XP-curve rebalance; character rename/transfer; an account bank UI.

A → H, in dependency order. A carries the risk (it re-keys five tables); everything after it is additive. E is independent and can land first.

All eight children Done, and browser verification passes: log in as the test player, create a Mage, confirm the staff loadout (not the Warrior one), walk, hard-refresh, confirm the exact resume position, confirm the World Map shows only visited worlds, confirm /game/maps redirects for a player.

results.name: Backend DB tests share one database with no isolation, causing cross-file flakes
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · advisory-lock isolation lands via PR #14 (4dc7594) — the two named catalog races closed; bcrypt/token-bucket timing flakes and the leaked fixture user deferred to SOMET-275

npm test is a bare node --test, which runs test FILES concurrently. Every DB-writing file points at the same database with no per-file schema, transaction wrapper or lock, so files interfere with each other.

Fix

Generalized the advisory-lock pattern SOMET-265 proved for worlds.is_entry into a reusable helper, applied to the concretely-named Wolf/catalog-invariant collision. Added --test-timeout=20000 so a silently-hanging SQL-stub-mismatch becomes a named failure — this also surfaced a pre-existing, load-dependent slowness in seed_catalogs_db.test.js as an occasional timeout; left as an honest signal per the ticket's own instruction not to paper over it by raising the timeout further.

Deliberately out of scope

bcrypt (auth_routes.test.js) and token-bucket (authority_server.test.js) CPU-contention/timing flakes — different root cause, tracked in SOMET-275. Leaked fixture user (progression_migration.test.js) — left alone deliberately, deleting a user could cascade.

results.name: P2a follow-ups: seeder COALESCE is largely illusory, route validation gaps, dead exports
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-08 · fix round 1 closed the reviewer's defect, re-verified independently

None of these blocked the merge. Each was triaged by the final whole-branch review as follow-up rather than fix-before-merge. Grouped into one item because they are all small and all in the same area.

1. The seeder's COALESCE protection is narrower than its comment claims

seed-catalogs.js's seedOneBehavior uses COALESCE($n, creature_behaviors.col) for seven optional columns, and the file header states a run "must never cost an admin a tile they added by hand". But every one of the twelve seed rows supplies projectile_speed, projectile_radius, aggro_radius, leash_radius, preferred_range and move_speed_mult explicitly, so those parameters are never NULL and the fallback branch never fires. Only damage_override (omitted by 11 of 12 rows) is genuinely protected. The mechanism is right; the comment overstates it, and it matters more now that an admin UI exists to retune profiles.

2. Unvalidated route inputs return raw 500s

On /api/creature-behaviors: a non-numeric projectile_radius/preferred_range/move_speed_mult/damage_override reaches Postgres as a cast error; a duplicate name returns 23505 rather than a 409 (isUniqueViolation already exists at index.js:129 and is used by biomes and worlds); a non-numeric :id on PUT/DELETE likewise. On the entity-types routes, attack_element and behavior_id are written through unchecked — the same pre-existing gap render_mode has on those routes.

3. Entity-types PUT clobbers on a partial write

index.js:482 binds behavior_id ?? null and attack_element || 'physical', so a PUT omitting either silently demotes the creature to the fallback profile or resets its element. Latent — the only caller sends the whole form — but prompt on that same line is COALESCE-protected precisely because someone hit this before. Fixed, then a reviewer found the fix over-corrected (broke the UI's explicit-null clear); fix round 1 resolved it with an omitted-vs-explicit-null distinction, independently re-verified.

4. Delete-guard TOCTOU

index.js:894-916 does the reference SELECT and the DELETE as two separate pool.query calls, so a concurrent assignment turns the intended 409 into a foreign-key 500. One transaction fixes it.

5. Dead code and misleading comments

  • creatureTypes[].behavior is computed in loadCreatureTypes and read nowhere — a vestige of the inert-catalog bug. Drop it, or comment that the per-chunk query is the only live path.
  • AGGRO_RADIUS, LEASH_RADIUS, CONTACT_RANGE and CREATURE_ATTACK_COOLDOWN are now unused in backend/src (tests still import them, so they must stay exported).
  • Unreachable fallbacks: c.behavior || DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR, || { killed: [] }, and the inner c.damage ?? CREATURE_DAMAGE.
  • GUARD_DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR is a shared frozen singleton while the Line fallback is spread-copied per instance — a future write would throw for guards and silently corrupt one instance for hostiles.
  • Migration 1714440081000's comment says the default ON DELETE is RESTRICT; node-pg-migrate produces NO ACTION. Equivalent here, comment wrong.

6. Weak tests

Four fake-pool behaviour rows are byte-identical to DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR while claiming to be independent literals — replacing resolveBehavior with a stub leaves them green. CreatureBehaviorsAdmin.smoke.test.js asserts only typeof === 'function'. The projectile-cap test pre-fills only creature-owned projectiles, so it would pass under the old all-projectiles count too.

results.name: P2b — Pack-leader buffs, apex abilities, knockback, per-rung loot
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-08 · all 10 tasks + whole-branch review + browser verification complete; PR #3 open, awaiting merge

Umbrella: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-bestiary-program-design.md

The second half of what was one P2. Split on 2026-08-07 to keep the review surface on the live combat tick manageable — the umbrella flags P2 as the engineering risk of the whole program, and SOMET-243 needed three review rounds on these same surfaces.

Scope

  • Champion rung — pack-leader buffs. Needs a runtime relationship between creatures that does not exist: P1's packs are a placement concept only, and world_creatures has no pack column. Resolved: radius aura, recomputed each tick, never persisted.
  • Apex rung — multiple abilities. P2a gives a creature one attack; an Apex needs a set with independent cooldowns. Resolved: child creature_abilities table, with P2a's attack columns migrated into slot-1 rows.
  • Brute rung — knockback. Precedent from SOMET-243's portal blocking: direct server-authoritative position reassignment, never through resolveMove. Resolved: symmetric — creature abilities and player weapons both carry the stat; knockbackPosition (server.js:142) is extracted and reused.
  • Per-rung loot tables. creature_drops is per-entity-type and rung-blind; 288 hand-authored drop tables is not viable. Resolved: behavior_drops rolls in addition to creature_drops, with per-rung gold as a fallback when the type's range is absent.

Depends on

P2a (SOMET-249) — Done, merged at 51a16d3. It introduced the creature_behaviors catalog these mechanics extend, and the frozen 120-tick golden trace that guards the attack-column migration.

Blocks

P4 (SOMET-250) must not start until this branch is MERGED (Done here reflects the work being complete and verified — see comments for the full evidence trail — not yet integrated into main). Splitting P2 was about review surface, not about letting P4 start early — authoring 288 creature rows against half a schema reintroduces exactly the second pass the split is meant to avoid. Order is P2a → P2b → P4.

Migration range

Shares P2's reserved range 1714440080000–1714440089000. P2a consumed 80000–82000; P2b took 83000–88000 (one migration added by the final-review fix wave).

results.name: Regenerate-terrain route wipes portal guards and leaves the world empty
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-08 · independently reviewed, approved, PR #5 pending merge

POST /api/worlds/:id/regenerate (backend/src/index.js, around the DELETE FROM world_creatures WHERE world_id = $1 at ~:1673) issues an unconditional delete of every creature in the world — including portal guards, which is the exact defect P1 fixed in the other two paths — then re-inserts village guards only and never repopulates.

Why it matters more now than it did

P1 (SOMET-246) established populateWorld as the single creature-population path and wired both seeding and the admin re-roll route through it. This route was never claimed by that sub-project and so was left unreconciled, which makes it a third, divergent path over world_creatures.

Post-P1 the user-visible behaviour reads worse than before: "Regenerate terrain" now empties a world that seeding had populated. Previously most worlds were empty anyway, so the difference was invisible.

The portal-guard half is a genuine pre-existing bug: guards inserted by insertPortalGuards carry whatever creature type the map spec names and are identified by a non-null blocks_portal_id. Deleting them silently unblocks a guarded dungeon entrance — the blocking mechanic shipped in SOMET-243 — with nothing to notice.

Acceptance criteria

  • Regenerating terrain preserves village guards and portal guards, matching populateWorld's type <> 'Village Guard' AND blocks_portal_id IS NULL predicate.
  • A regenerated world ends up populated per its density tier, not empty — most likely by routing this path through populateWorld too, so there is genuinely one population path.
  • A regression test covers both: a portal guard survives a regenerate, and the world holds creatures afterwards.

Provenance

Found as "finding 9" by P1's final whole-branch review and deliberately parked rather than folded into that fix wave — it belongs to a route P1 never touched, and fixing it there would have been scope creep in a wave already covering nine findings.

results.name: P5 — Map content: multi-level dungeons and new surface worlds
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-09 · self-reviewed (mitigated by per-task independent review + opus final review), PR #7 pending merge

Umbrella: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-bestiary-program-design.md

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-p5-map-content-design.md

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-p5-map-content.md

Content sub-project. Consumes everything the other four build.

Scope

~58 new worlds against today's 20 — roughly 8 multi-level dungeons of ~6 levels each with branching, plus surface worlds for the new biomes. Authored as checked-in map specs in backend/seeds/maps/, seeded via make seed-map SPEC=<name>.

Dungeon linking uses the PORTAL edge shipped in SOMET-243, including guarded entrances (blocks_portal_id) — this is the sub-project that finally exercises that work against real content, which the dungeons epic itself never did.

This is where hordes actually get authored

P1 ships the density tier mechanism but deliberately authors no tiers, leaving every world on normal. Choosing which world is a horde or a swarm happens here, because it needs the real bestiary to decide what the horde is made of. Level bands are authored here too — today every dungeon world sits at level_min = level_max = 1, so even a populated one would spawn nothing but level-1 creatures.

Open questions from the brainstorm — resolved

  • One-spec-per-database survived at ~58 worlds by picking a grid origin (x≥20) that never collides with the 3 existing example specs.
  • Dungeon depth: interconnected mega-descent (per user's explicit choice) — 8 dungeons chained D1→D8 via guarded PORTAL links, each internally its own spine/hub/loop.
  • World Map graph legibility at scale: confirmed illegible at default zoom with 86 total nodes — pre-scoped in the design as its own follow-up, not this ticket's defect.

Migration range

Reserved: 1714440110000–1714440119000 — unused; no new migration was needed (pure content on top of P1-P4's existing schema).

results.name: P4 — Bestiary: 288 creatures across 32 lines × 9 rungs
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-08 · seeded, browser-verified, PR #4 open (not yet merged)

Umbrella: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-bestiary-program-design.md — the line × rung × tier structure is fixed there and this sub-project instantiates it.

Content sub-project. Today the entire live bestiary is Skeleton ×25, Bat ×12, Slime ×4 across all 20 worlds, from a catalog of five types — one of which (Wolf) is placed nowhere at all.

Design

See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-p4-bestiary-design.md. Deterministic generation from the umbrella's line/rung tables (no per-row guessing on hp/def/resistances/behavior_id), legacy Wolf/Slime/Skeleton/Bat folded into the taxonomy as disclosed live-balance changes (Wolf free, Skeleton/Bat/Slime real — 25/12/4 live placements respectively), per-type drop rows for all 292 creatures, generate-then-human-review workflow. No schema change, no new migration.

Scope

288 creature types: 32 lines × 9 rungs (Swarm, Skirmisher, Line, Ranged, Caster, Brute, Heavy, Champion, Apex). Each row needs name, colour, hp, defense, resistances, level band, sprite prompt, gold_min/gold_max, and at least one drop rule — backend/tests/creature_drops_db.test.js:44 fails any creature that drops nothing.

Catalog lives in backend/seeds/data/entityTypes.js (HOSTILE_CREATURES + CREATURE_DROPS), so a fresh database rebuilds it — the pattern that fixed Wolf after a volume rebuild silently deleted it.

Known constraint — sprites

288 local sprite generations, roughly 5¼ hours of machine time. Coding agents cannot generate images; every creature renders as a flat colour box until the user runs them.

Migration range

Reserved: 1714440100000–1714440109000 (unused by this design — pure content, no migration needed). One unrelated migration, 1714440090000, was added outside this range to fix a weapon-balance gap real P4 content exposed — see PR #4.

results.name: P2a — Creature attack kinds and aggro profiles
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-07 · merged to main at 51a16d3; browser-verified a creature firing fire projectiles and burning a player

Umbrella: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-bestiary-program-design.md
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-p2a-creature-behaviors-design.md
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-07-p2a-creature-behaviors.md

Was "P2 — Creature mechanics". Split on 2026-08-07: pack-leader buffs, apex abilities, Brute knockback and per-rung loot moved to SOMET-253 (P2b). P4 must not start until P2b is Done — order is P2a → P2b → P4.

What shipped

  • creature_behaviors catalog, twelve profiles: the umbrella's nine rungs, plus Guard (today's hardcoded guard constants moved into data, including GUARD_DAMAGE as damage_override), plus Sentry and Lurker so hold and ambush are not dead code.
  • entity_types.behavior_id (integer FK) and attack_element, with all five existing creature types backfilled behaviour-neutrally.
  • Three attack kinds. cast fires the creature's element AND applies that element's status rider — burn, chill and shock existed in effects.js but no creature could ever inflict them.
  • Six chase styles, four of them new logic (charge and guard are the two pre-existing branches moved into data).
  • Creature-owned projectiles through the existing ProjectileSim via an ownerKind discriminator, with faction-aware targeting mirroring the rules the simulation already enforced.
  • Admin surface: a Creature Behaviors sidebar route, plus behaviour and attack-element dropdowns on the entity-type form.

Two defects worth remembering

The catalog was initially inert in the running game. There are two creature-loading paths — loadCreatureTypes (the type catalog, used for gold drops and name→id) and a separate per-chunk query that feeds live instances. Only the first was wired, so every creature resolved to the fallback regardless of its assigned profile, with the whole test suite green. Same shape as the two-spawn-paths defect that started this program.

A creature's elemental hit could resurrect the creature it killed. The status rider passed the shooter's uuid where a player id was expected; the insert fails with Postgres 22P02 and the rollback undoes the already-successful DELETE FROM world_creatures, so the creature vanishes from the simulation but survives in the database and returns on the next chunk load. Found by the final whole-branch review; not reachable on then-current data, but one admin action away once the dropdowns shipped.

Known limitation

Four styles (kite, skirmish, hold, ambush) have no creature using them until P4 assigns rungs. They were exercised during verification by temporarily assigning a profile and reverting.

Migration range

Used 1714440080000, 1714440081000, 1714440082000. 1714440083000–1714440089000 remain for P2b.

Was "P2 — Creature mechanics". Split on 2026-08-07: pack-leader buffs, apex abilities, Brute knockback and per-rung loot moved to SOMET-253 (P2b). P4 must not start until P2b is Done — order is P2a → P2b → P4.
What shipped
creature_behaviors catalog, twelve profiles: the umbrella's nine rungs, plus Guard (today's hardcoded guard constants moved into data, including GUARD_DAMAGE as damage_override), plus Sentry and Lurker so hold and ambush are not dead code.
entity_types.behavior_id (integer FK) and attack_element, with all five existing creature types backfilled behaviour-neutrally.
Three attack kinds. cast fires the creature's element AND applies that element's status rider — burn, chill and shock existed in effects.js but no creature could ever inflict them.
Six chase styles, four of them new logic (charge and guard are the two pre-existing branches moved into data).
Creature-owned projectiles through the existing ProjectileSim via an ownerKind discriminator, with faction-aware targeting mirroring the rules the simulation already enforced.
Admin surface: a Creature Behaviors sidebar route, plus behaviour and attack-element dropdowns on the entity-type form.
Two defects worth remembering
The catalog was initially inert in the running game. There are two creature-loading paths — loadCreatureTypes (the type catalog, used for gold drops and name→id) and a separate per-chunk query that feeds live instances. Only the first was wired, so every creature resolved to the fallback regardless of its assigned profile, with the whole test suite green. Same shape as the two-spawn-paths defect that started this program.
A creature's elemental hit could resurrect the creature it killed. The status rider passed the shooter's uuid where a player id was expected; the insert fails with Postgres 22P02 and the rollback undoes the already-successful DELETE FROM world_creatures, so the creature vanishes from the simulation but survives in the database and returns on the next chunk load. Found by the final whole-branch review; not reachable on then-current data, but one admin action away once the dropdowns shipped.
Known limitation
Four styles (kite, skirmish, hold, ambush) have no creature using them until P4 assigns rungs. They were exercised during verification by temporarily assigning a profile and reverting.
Migration range
Used 1714440080000, 1714440081000, 1714440082000. 1714440083000–1714440089000 remain for P2b.

results.name: Bestiary Program
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-09 · all 8 children Done; PR #7 (P5) pending merge to fully land on main

Umbrella for the creature content program: 32 lines × 9 rungs = 288 creature types, 32 biomes (27 new), ~30 new tile types, level bands spanning the full 1–50 player ceiling, clustered-pack "horde" density, and per-creature combat mechanics.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-bestiary-program-design.md (commit 9c7ec07)

The defect this starts from

Play-testing found most maps empty of creatures. Seeded worlds arrive with zero creatures on the ground. applyMapSpec writes creature_count onto the world row but never calls placeMapCreatures; the only production caller is the admin re-roll route. The per-chunk spawn path that would otherwise cover it is gated on !isBoundedWorld, which is false for every world that exists — so placement has two implementations and only one is reachable, and it fires only when a human clicks a button.

Measured live: 11 of 20 worlds hold no creatures, including every dungeon world. A second defect compounds it — placeMapCreatures intersects a world's allowlist with the biome's fauna, and there is no cave, crypt or catacomb biome anywhere. The catacombs are meadows underground.

Sub-projects — all Done

  • P1 — World population (SOMET-246) · Done
  • P2a — Creature attack kinds/aggro (SOMET-249) · Done
  • P2b — Pack-leader buffs, apex abilities, knockback, loot (SOMET-253) · Done
  • P3 — Tiles & biomes (SOMET-247) · Done
  • P4 — Bestiary (SOMET-250) · Done
  • P5 — Map content (SOMET-251) · Done, PR #7 pending merge
  • Follow-ups discovered along the way — regenerate-terrain guard wipe (SOMET-252, Done), P2a deferred minors (SOMET-254, Done)

Migration ranges

Reserved: P1 …070000–079000 · P2 …080000–089000 · P3 …090000–099000 · P4 …100000–109000 · P5 …110000–119000. P5 ended up needing none — pure content on the existing schema.

Risks — outcome

The art queue remains real and unaddressed by this program: every new creature/tile still renders as a flat colour box until local sprite generation runs — that work was always scoped to the user, not any sub-project.

Balance is still unvalidated by construction, as originally flagged — a live gap surfaced mid-program (P5 Task 5) confirmed 15 of 32 Apex creatures had mechanically-invisible resistances against the pre-P4 weapon catalog; fixed opportunistically (frost/storm staff damage), not as a full retuning pass.

results.name: P3 — Tiles & biomes: 32 biomes, ~30 new tile types
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-06 · merged to main 1b05a18; the catacombs are no longer meadows

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-p3-tiles-and-biomes-design.md · Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-p3-tiles-and-biomes.md

Second sub-project of the Bestiary Program (SOMET-248), after P1. Content, plus one seeder change and one safety guard.

Why it was load-bearing, not decoration

Creature placement intersects a world's allowed_creature_types with the biome's own creature_types, and an empty intersection places nothing. Only five biomes existed, all surface, so every dungeon world declared ["Meadow"] or ["Meadow","Mire"] — the catacombs were meadows underground, and P4's bestiary would have been inert without this.

What shipped

  • 30 tile types — one signature floor per new biome plus three impassable (cave_wall, rubble, chasm). A tile carries one image shared by every biome listing it, so distinct identity requires distinct tiles.
  • 27 biomes — 5 surface, 14 underground, 8 abyssal, each with ordered terrain_tiles (the banding order), palette, art_style, exclusions, and creature_types: [] for P4.
  • backend/src/services/navigability.js — assertNavigable, a seed-time flood fill that refuses to seed a world whose doorway, portal or arrival tile is unreachable, plus a minimum-reachable-fraction floor.
  • Seeder columns — the tile upsert now carries prompt/render_mode/wall_height/place_order, and both tile and biome upserts preserve hand-authored values instead of stomping them.
  • All 20 worlds re-pointed, with world_chunks cleared so the new terrain actually takes effect.

The guard caught four real seals

One pre-existing (Sunken Eastwing, live since 2026-08-05, 3 of ~3600 cells reachable), two created by the retrofit (southwing, deep), and — after the final review corrected the guard itself — Blackfen Sinks, which had shipped sealed one hop from the entry world with water directly beneath its only doorway. The guard had been requiring the doorway gap, which is walkable by construction; it now requires the arrival tile one tile inward.

Known consequence

13 of 20 worlds hold zero creatures until P4 (SOMET-250) fills biome fauna. Escalated and accepted as a deliberate trade for the clean P3/P4 boundary.

Migration range

Reserved 1714440090000–1714440099000 went unused — catalogs are seeded, not migrated.

results.name: P1 — World population: one spawn path, density tiers, packs
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-06 · merged to main bd66978; seeded worlds now arrive populated

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-p1-world-population-design.md · Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-p1-world-population.md

First sub-project of the Bestiary Program (SOMET-248). Engineering only — no creature types, no biomes, no tiles. It makes population work, so P2–P5's content is observable when it lands.

The defect it fixed

applyMapSpec wrote creature_count and allowed_creature_types onto the world row and stopped — it never placed anything. The only production caller of placeMapCreatures was the admin re-roll button. The per-chunk path that looked like a fallback was gated on !isBoundedWorld, false for every world that exists, so it had never run. Placement had two implementations and only one was reachable, and it only ran when a human clicked. Live measurement: 11 of 20 worlds held zero creatures, including every dungeon world. All 20 now hold 15.

What shipped

  • backend/src/services/worldPopulation.js — populateWorld(client, worldRow, { rngSeed }), the single population path. Runs entirely on the caller's transaction. Used by applyMapSpec and POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures, and nothing else.
  • Density tiers — worlds.density, one of dead|sparse|normal|dense|horde|swarm, resolved through densityTiers.js and scaled per 1000 tiles so a bigger map is not sparser at the same setting. Capped at 2000 creatures per world.
  • Clustered packs — placeCreaturePacks, one type per pack, members deduplicated within a size-derived radius, sharing scatter's extracted tile-validity helper so the rules cannot drift.
  • Retired the dead spawn path — spawnChunkCreatures and its call site deleted; POST /api/worlds now requires width and height, which is what makes that deletion safe.
  • creature_count is now derived from what was actually placed, and retired as an authorable map-spec field in favour of density.

Deliberately not done here

No density tier or level band is authored — every world sits on normal. Choosing which world is a horde needs the real bestiary and belongs to P5 (SOMET-251).

Follow-up filed

SOMET-252 — POST /api/worlds/:id/regenerate remains a third path over world_creatures that wipes portal guards and never repopulates.

Migration range

Used: 1714440070000 (of the reserved 1714440070000–1714440079000).

results.name: D — Magic stones and sockets
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · implemented, reviewed, PR #10 open pending merge; closes epic SOMET-240

Placeholder holding the decisions already made. Do not plan from this description; it is not a spec. Specifying this before A2 exists would be fiction — the shape of stone levelling depends on what A2's stat system actually looks like once built.

What already exists

Sockets have somewhere to attach: player_items now has a per-instance uuid primary key, character-keyed (post SOMET-256/257/260), so a socket table can reference an individual owned item rather than an item type. That is the one piece of groundwork this feature would otherwise have needed.

Today's "magic weapons" are just item_types.element plus mana_cost — there is no spell entity.

Decisions already taken

Existing magic weapons are converted: each weapon's spell becomes a pre-slotted, removable stone rather than staying built in. Stones level as the player gains experience. Buff-only stones exist alongside spell stones.

The risk that makes this last

Conversion rewrites player_items rows that players already own. This is the only sub-project in the epic where a bad deploy costs someone their gear. It needs a reversible migration with a rollback verified before it runs, not just written. Verified — see design spec and PR #10.

Open questions for the brainstorm

All resolved — see design spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-magic-stones-sockets-design.md: stone is its own item, fixed 1 socket/item, spell stones replace not stack, stones carry independent XP awarded only on landed-hit use, destroy-on-removal at a flat 10% behind required confirmation, spell stones weapon-only / buff stones weapon+armor.

results.name: B — Chests, guards and loot maps
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-09 · implemented, reviewed, PR #9 open pending merge; known cross-branch integration risk flagged

Placeholder holding the decisions already made. Do not plan from this description; it is not a spec.

What already exists, and why it is not enough

world_items is ephemeral ground loot — it carries an expires_at and is swept. A chest is a persistent container that holds items until opened, so it is a genuinely new concept rather than a variation on the existing table. creature_drops already models "this creature drops this item at this chance" and is the natural precedent for chest contents.

Decisions already taken

Chests can be guarded, and the stronger the guard the better the contents — expressed via the guard's A1 level, so no second difficulty mechanism is invented. Loot maps drop from creatures and point at a chest. Opening a chest awards XP through A2's awardXp(..., 'chest') seam, which A2 defines and leaves unused.

Open questions for the brainstorm

Whether chest contents are rolled at generation or at opening (affects save-scumming) · whether a chest is per-player or shared once looted · how a loot map identifies its target chest across worlds · whether guards must die before the chest opens or merely defend it · whether chests respawn. All resolved — see design spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-chests-guards-loot-maps-design.md.

results.name: C — Dungeons and catacombs
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-05 · merged to main as f08d015; self-reviewed, disclosed in the closing comment

Dungeon entrances reachable from a portal tile inside an overworld world, sometimes guarded by a structural creature pack. Dungeon levels are ordinary spec-seeded worlds rows that skip the overworld's grid embedding, linked via a new PORTAL value on map_links.edge — branching (one world, multiple outgoing portals) is enabled by two partial unique indexes replacing the old combined UNIQUE(from_world_id, edge). Guarded entrances gate the portal's transfer trigger on guard liveness — the first blocking mechanic in this codebase — without touching the shared collision/movement code; a blocked attempt knocks the player back with a message via the same direct-position-reassignment mechanism respawn already uses.

Data model

map_links
  edge          CHECK IN ('N','E','S','W','PORTAL')
  from_x/from_y/to_x/to_y   real, nullable   -- portal rows only
  map_links_compass_unique  UNIQUE(from_world_id, edge)     WHERE edge != 'PORTAL'
  map_links_portal_source_unique UNIQUE(from_world_id, from_x, from_y) WHERE edge = 'PORTAL'

world_creatures.blocks_portal_id   uuid REFERENCES map_links(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

Authoring

A dungeon-level world may omit grid entirely, provided it's reachable via at least one portal link (the entry-reachability BFS walks portal links transitively, not just compass ones). Guards are a structural spawn — the same INSERT-based mechanism village guards already use, extended with blocks_portal_id — inserted idempotently on spec re-apply.

The blocking mechanic

planPortalTransition fails closed when its own chunk (and, after a fix round, the full radius-1 neighborhood a guard's ±60px spawn offset could occupy) hasn't finished loading — not just when a guard is confirmed alive — and re-anchors on the exact chunkOf(player top-left, chunkSize) call the game's real chunk-loader uses, so the two can never disagree. Arrival at a mirrored portal is latched by tile-change rather than a timer, since the arrival tile is the return portal's own trigger tile by construction and a flat cooldown would still bounce a stationary player once it expired.

World Map

placePortalClusters renders portal-linked dungeon levels as an off-grid vertical cluster near their entrance, running after the compass-edge BFS and before the disconnected-root fallback so a dungeon is never mistaken for an unrelated orphan. Ordering determinism comes from sorting is_entry first, not compass-anchoring — portal-connected worlds, including the entry, may legitimately have no stored grid position.

Testing

Backend node:test, frontend vitest (node env, pure-function + source-text only). Literal expected values throughout — this repo's dominant shipped-defect shape is assertions derived from the same constants as the code. Every migration/constraint change carries a mutation check.

results.name: A2 — Player progression: XP, levels, stats, respec
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-04 · merged to main as 2c2cfa0; pushed to origin; self-reviewed, disclosed in the closing comment

The whole progression system: XP, levels, six working stats, gold-cost respec, death penalty, character sheet. This is where all of the epic's risk lived.

Data model

Its own table, not nine more columns on users. users.gold sets a precedent for game state on the auth row, but XP + level + points + six stats is a different order of magnitude.

player_progression (user_id PK -> users ON DELETE CASCADE)
  experience   bigint not null default 0
  level        int    not null default 1
  stat_points  int    not null default 0
  strength, dexterity, constitution,
  intelligence, wisdom, charisma
               int    not null default 5

The six stats and the seam each touches

STR → melee damage · INT → spell damage and max mana (split by the weapon's existing element: physical off STR, everything else off INT) · DEX → attack speed · CON → max HP · WIS → mana regen · CHA → merchant sell prices.

Two spec corrections found during implementation. Mana regen already existed (PLAYER_MANA_REGEN, applied every tick since 2026-07-20), so WIS scales a live constant rather than adding a tick — the spec's "casters run permanently dry" claim was false. The base is what the level costs, not the progress already made into it, so dying early in a level is not cheaper than dying late. A player can lose a level's worth of grinding, never a level.

results.name: A1 — Creature levels
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-03 · merged to main as 934cc01; self-reviewed, disclosed in the closing comment

Every creature rolls a level from its world's band, so difficulty is authored per world. Self-contained: no users change and no change to any existing player-facing formula. This is what dungeon difficulty (C) and chest loot tiers (B) hang off.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-03-a1-creature-levels.md · Migrations used: 1714440050000, 1714440051000 (reserved range …50000–…59000)

Spec corrections made during implementation

1. There are two spawn paths, not one. spawnChunkCreatures serves unbounded worlds via a per-tile hash; placeMapCreatures serves bounded worlds via makeRng. Every spec-seeded world is bounded, so that is the path that matters for authored difficulty. Both roll levels.

2. Creature damage was not an entity_types column — it was the flat constant CREATURE_DAMAGE = 5, so scaling it required a new persisted column and a change at the attack site.

3. Village guards are out of scope — structural spawns with their own already-tuned GUARD_DAMAGE. They stay level 1.

Data model as shipped

worlds.level_min       int  not null default 1
worlds.level_max       int  not null default 1   -- CHECK (level_min >= 1 AND level_max >= level_min)
world_creatures.level  int  not null default 1
world_creatures.damage real not null default 5
world_creatures.defense real NULLABLE, no default -- NULL = predates scaling, fall back to the base

Map specs gain an optional per-world level_band. A band of [1,1] (the default) scales nothing, so applying this to an existing database changes no behaviour.

Result

spine-descent now ramps [1,2] at the entry to [9,12] at the end. Across all 8 worlds every creature sits inside its band, with hp 18–21 → 31–37, damage 5.5 → 10.5 and defense 0.5 → 7.5.

Known limitation

validateMapSpec requires width/height, so every spec-seeded world is bounded. The unbounded spawnChunkCreatures band path is correct and tested but currently dormant in production — no API writes a band to an unbounded world. Also: re-running make seed-map updates a world's band but does not re-roll creatures already in world_creatures; that needs POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures.

Follow-ups (not blocking, not silently dropped)

The damage baseline 5 is duplicated in mapService.js, authority/creatures.js and migration 1714440050000 with nothing enforcing agreement — the honest fix is an import, not a test. authority_creatures_integration.test.js socket cleanup lacks try/finally across several pre-existing tests, so a failed assertion hangs the run until killed.

results.name: Progression, dungeons & loot
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · all 5 sub-projects (A1, A2, C, B, D) confirmed Done; epic closed

Umbrella for six requested features: dungeons/catacombs with guarded entrances and multiple levels, chests with guard-scaled loot, loot maps dropped by creatures, creature and entity levels, and magic stones socketed into weapons/armour.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-progression-dungeons-loot-design.md

Why this is five projects, not one

There is no XP or levelling system at all. users has gold and nothing else resembling progression; a search for xp/experience/level across backend/src/ returns nothing. Creature levels and stones that "level up when the user gains experience" are both defined in terms of a system that does not exist, so player progression is a prerequisite rather than a sibling feature.

map_links structurally cannot express a dungeon entrance. It is CHECK (edge IN ('N','E','S','W')) with UNIQUE(from_world_id, edge) — worlds connect edge-to-edge, at most four neighbours each, and the map-seed tooling merged in 14876c4 depends on exactly that to embed every world in a 2D grid. A dungeon entrance is a point inside a world and its levels stack downward. This needs a second link kind, and dungeon levels must sit outside the grid rule.

Build order

A1 → A2 → C → B → D. Dungeons land before chests so chests arrive somewhere that shows them off.

Decisions taken

Creature level from a per-world band · levelling grants stat points the player allocates · death costs a fraction of progress into the current level, never a level · all six stats mapped to a mechanic · respec allowed, costs gold · XP from kills, chests and dungeon clears · existing magic weapons converted to pre-slotted stones · progression stored in its own player_progression table.

Cross-cutting risk

Four sub-projects means four branches. This repo has already had a migration timestamp collision (1714440008000) and a three-way ordering scramble across concurrent branches, so each sub-project reserves a timestamp range before work starts.

results.name: Biomes migration `down` leaves biome-generated world_chunks behind
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-09 · fixed, tested, independently reviewed; PR #8 open pending merge

backend/migrations/1714440043000_biomes.js's down() drops the worlds.biomes / worlds.biome_cell columns and the biomes table, and nothing else.

But world_chunks rows generated while biomes were active have biome-banded terrain baked into their persisted data. After a rollback the generator reverts to the legacy single-list path, while those persisted chunks stay as they were — so a rolled-back database serves biome terrain for already-materialized chunks and legacy terrain for anything generated afterwards, with a visible seam between them.

Low priority: rollback is a development action, not a production one, and the fix is one statement. Filing it so it is not rediscovered the next time someone actually rolls back.

Suggested fix: DELETE FROM world_chunks in down() (they regenerate on demand), or at minimum only for worlds whose biomes array was non-empty.

Found during: biomes epic (sub-project A); down() re-read on current main 2026-07-30 and still only drops columns + table.

results.name: DELETE /api/tile-types/:id and /api/entity-types/:id have no reference guards, though renames do
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · DELETE routes now carry the same reference guards as their PUT rename siblings, merged via PR #15 (dd3d3e7)

Asymmetry in the catalog admin routes: renaming a tile type or entity type is guarded, deleting one is not.

Renames check references and refuse (backend/src/index.js):
- entity type rename → 409 "Cannot rename '<x>': still referenced by allowed_creature_types, placed creatures, or a biome"
- tile type rename → 409 "Cannot rename '<x>': still referenced by an entity type's spawn tiles or a biome"

Both DELETE routes are bare — a single `DELETE FROM ... WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id`, a 404 if the row was absent, and nothing else. No reference check, no cascade, no warning.

So an admin can delete a tile type that worlds still generate from, or an entity type still listed in a world's allowed_creature_types, in a biome's terrain_tiles/flora_types/creature_types, or actually placed in world_creatures. The references are by NAME in jsonb arrays with no FK, so the database will not stop it either. Downstream the name simply stops resolving, which surfaces as silently-dropped terrain/flora/creatures rather than an error.

The biomes epic widened this: biomes.terrain_tiles / flora_types / creature_types are three more name-array reference sites per biome row, and a biome is shared across every world listing it.

Suggested fix: give both DELETE routes the same reference check their rename paths already have and return 409 with the referencing rows named, so the two paths agree. The rename guards are the obvious model to copy.

Found during: biomes epic (sub-project A); both routes re-read on current main 2026-07-30 and still unguarded.

results.name: World PUT accepts unvalidated biome names, so creating a biome later silently rewrites that world's terrain
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · biomes[] now validated against the catalog in PUT /api/worlds/:id, merged via PR #15 (dd3d3e7)

Two halves of one gap. worlds.biomes is a jsonb array of biome NAMES with no foreign key, and nothing validates those names against the biomes catalog.

1. PUT /api/worlds/:id (backend/src/index.js) filters the incoming biomes array only for non-empty strings — it never checks that each name exists in the biomes table. So a world can be saved listing "Meadwo" or a biome that was never created. loadBiomes() in services/biomes.js resolves names via a Map and ends with .filter(Boolean), so an unknown name is silently dropped: the world generates as if it were not listed. No error, no warning, no signal to the admin that their biome assignment is doing nothing.

2. POST /api/biomes does not call invalidateWorld() for anything. That is correct today for a genuinely new name, but combined with (1) it is not: creating a biome whose name matches a dangling reference silently ACTIVATES it for every world already listing it. Those worlds' terrain changes on next generation while their persisted world_chunks stay as-is, and no player is evicted or warned.

Note what is already correct, so this is not over-fixed: PUT /api/biomes DOES guard renames — renaming a biome still listed by any world returns 409 with the referencing worlds named. The gap is only the create path plus the missing validation on the world side.

Suggested fix: validate biomes[] against the catalog in PUT /api/worlds/:id and 400 on unknown names (this alone closes both halves, since a dangling reference can no longer be created). Optionally also have POST /api/biomes check for pre-existing references to that name and invalidate them.

Found during: biomes epic (sub-project A); re-verified against current main 2026-07-30 while filing.

results.name: invalidateWorld deletes world_chunks even when eviction is refused, so a connected player diverges from the served map
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · invalidateWorld reordered (evictability checked before chunk delete), merged via PR #15 (dd3d3e7)

invalidateWorld() in backend/src/index.js deletes the world's persisted world_chunks rows unconditionally, then attempts to evict connected players. When eviction is REFUSED (a player is connected and cannot be kicked), the chunk delete has already happened and is not rolled back.

Resulting divergence: the Node authority keeps serving its cached, frozen, pre-edit map to the connected player, while world_chunks is now empty. If that player walks away from a chunk and back, the client refetches via GET /chunk, which regenerates terrain from the NEW config. The player is then colliding against one map and looking at another. The admin does get a liveWarning toast, but the data damage is already done.

The shape is pre-existing, but the surface keeps widening:
- Biomes epic: a shared biome catalog means editing ONE biome row triggers this for every world listing that biome.
- Map-link graph tab: POST/DELETE /api/worlds/:id/links call invalidateWorld on BOTH endpoint worlds, so a single link edit can trigger it twice.

Suggested fix: check evictability BEFORE deleting chunks, and either refuse the whole edit (409) or defer the chunk delete until the world is empty. A queued "invalidate on next empty" marker would preserve the current admin ergonomics without the divergence.

Found during: biomes epic (recorded as an open ticket at the time), re-confirmed while building the map-link graph tab.

results.name: Texture generation overwrites the live MinIO asset before approval (data loss, already destroyed `sand`)
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · job-scoped asset keys land via PR #12 (44ae5c5) — a new generation can never overwrite a live one again

Starting a texture/sprite generation job wrote the generated image to the tile's LIVE MinIO object key before anyone approved it. Same key, no versioning, no backup — so the previous texture was gone the moment generation ran, whether or not the result was ever accepted.

This was not theoretical. During browser verification of the biomes epic (2026-07-28) an agent clicked "Generate texture" on the `sand` tile to check the flow. The generated image replaced the user's existing `sand` texture immediately, with no way to roll it back. `sand` is tile id 4 and matches PATH_NAME_RE, so it is the path tile for every world — the loss was visible across all 17 worlds at the time.

Fix: every generated asset (tile/object/creature) is now keyed by its generation's own job id — collision-proof by construction, no promote/copy step needed.

results.name: [F-054] P2 frontend-game: Something2.jsx tears down the authority connection through engineRef.current?.disconnec...
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · already fixed on main pre-session (328785b0); regression tests added, merged via PR #15 (dd3d3e7)

Status: open

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/Something2.jsx:1

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: Something2.jsx tears down the authority connection through engineRef.current?.disconnect(), but engineRef is never assigned anywhere, so sign-out and tab-switch do not actually disconnect the live authority socket.

Failure scenario: A player signs out or switches away from the game tab; the teardown calls engineRef.current?.disconnect() but engineRef is always null (grep finds no assignment), so the real WorldAuthorityClient at gameRef.current.authorityClient keeps its socket open and its session running in the background until the component fully unmounts, which for a tab switch it does not — leaving an authenticated game session live after the user believed they left it, and with F-051 now in place that socket will even reconnect on a transport drop.

results.name: [F-051] P2 frontend-game: A dropped authority socket now surfaces a visible disconnected state, but nothing attem...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/net/WorldAuthorityClient.js:1

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: A dropped authority socket now surfaces a visible disconnected state, but nothing attempts to reconnect, so recovery still requires the player to reload the page manually.

Failure scenario: A player loses connectivity for a few seconds mid-session, which a laptop suspend or a wifi handover makes routine; the client correctly freezes and shows a disconnected state rather than silently no-oping, but never retries, so the player must notice the message and reload to continue playing even though the network recovered on its own.

Proposed fix: Add a bounded reconnect with backoff to WorldAuthorityClient, re-joining the current world and resynchronising state on success, and fall back to the visible disconnected state only after the attempts are exhausted.

Verification: Kill the WebSocket from the console, confirm the client reconnects on its own within a few seconds and the player can move again without a page reload.

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:913

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: F-017 stopped the admin routes from reporting success when evictWorld refuses, but a live world still never reconciles its simulation against changed database content.

Failure scenario: An admin re-rolls the creatures of a world while a player is connected; the admin now receives a warning instead of a false success, but the connected player keeps fighting the previous creature set, which no longer exists in the database, so their kills award nothing and the world only corrects itself once the last socket disconnects.

Proposed fix: Give the authority a way to reload a live world in place — re-reading creatures and world content and broadcasting the new state to connected sockets — rather than relying on eviction, which cannot run while anyone is connected.

results.name: [F-049] P1 backend-api: Shrinking a bounded world does not re-validate already-persisted world_players position...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:1032

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: Shrinking a bounded world does not re-validate already-persisted world_players positions, so a player saved outside the new bounds is stranded.

Failure scenario: A player logs out at (200,200) in a 300x300 bounded world; an admin then edits the world down to 100x100. F-004 now validates entry_spawn on write but nothing revisits stored player positions, so on the next join that player loads outside the wall ring and cannot move, exactly the symptom F-004 was filed for.

Proposed fix: On a world bounds change, clamp or relocate any world_players row that falls outside the new walkable interior, in the same transaction as the bounds update.

Verification: Place a player near the edge of a large bounded world, disconnect, shrink the world so that position is outside the new ring, then rejoin as that player and confirm they spawn somewhere walkable and can move.

results.name: [F-046] P2 frontend-game: The Worlds picker's delete-world control (a trash icon rendered per list item at Someth...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/Something2.jsx:703

Lens: security · Source: browser

Claim: The Worlds picker's delete-world control (a trash icon rendered per list item at Something2.jsx:703-713, wired to an unconditional `deleteWorldMutation.mutate(world.id)`) is not gated behind `isAdmin` the way the admin-only tabs (tiles/entity/items/maps, Something2.jsx:788-791) are, so a completely unprivileged player account sees a working-looking destructive control next to every world in the list.

Failure scenario: A freshly registered player account (role: player, no admin grant) opens the Worlds picker inside the normal game view -- the same screen every player sees before entering a world -- and every single world row shows a red trash-can icon with a native confirm("Delete world ...") dialog. Clicking it and accepting the dialog fires a real `DELETE /api/worlds/:id` request with the player's own bearer token; the backend's adminGuard correctly rejects it (403), and a "Failed to delete world" toast does eventually appear (confirmed present in the DOM, though it auto-dismisses quickly), so no world is actually destroyed and no security boundary is crossed server-side. The defect is purely client-side: a regular player is shown an admin-only, destructive-looking affordance with no indication it will never work for them, on the same list they use to pick where to play.

Proposed fix: Wrap the `<HiOutlineTrash>` delete control (and the "New world name"/"Seed"/"Chunk size"/"Create World" world-creation form immediately below it, which has the identical gap) in the same `isAdmin &&` guard already used for the admin-only tabs at Something2.jsx:788-791.

Verification: In the browser: register a fresh player account (no admin role), open the Worlds picker in the normal Game View tab. Expect only a plain, read-only list; observed instead: every world row has a clickable delete icon and the picker also exposes the world-creation form. Clicking delete and accepting the confirm dialog sends a real DELETE request (confirmed via network log, HTTP 403) and eventually shows an error toast.

results.name: [F-045] P1 frontend-game: The mount effect that binds the running Game instance to the DOM canvas element only re...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/Something2.jsx:469

Lens: user-logic · Source: browser

Claim: The mount effect that binds the running Game instance to the DOM canvas element only re-runs on an `activeTab` change; it never re-runs when `authed` flips from false back to true, so any authed:false -> true cycle without a full page reload (sign out + sign back in, or the token-revoked-mid-session -> re-login flow the app is explicitly designed to support) unmounts the canvas React renders (the `if (!authed) return <Login .../>` gate at Something2.jsx:589 tears down the whole StyledGameContainer including the canvas) and remounts a brand-new canvas element that the still-alive Game/gameRef instance is never told about -- Game.canvas keeps pointing at the old, now-detached node.

Failure scenario: A logged-in player clicks "Sign out" then logs back in with the same account in the same tab (no page reload) -- an ordinary, expected action, and the same mechanism the app relies on when a token is silently revoked mid-session (see the apiFetch/token_version-revocation comment at Something2.jsx:377-379, which routes back through this exact Login->authed:true path). Reproduced twice, deterministically: after re-authenticating, the visible <canvas> element measures the browser default 300x150 (never resized) with inline style width/height still "100%" (resizeCanvas() never ran on it), so the game view renders solid black/blank. Underneath, the authority WebSocket, the rAF game loop, and server-side simulation all keep running against the OLD detached canvas -- confirmed by re-authenticating, waiting, then reloading: HP had dropped from 100 to 95 with no player input, proving the session was live and the player was taking damage they could not see or respond to. No console error, no toast, nothing indicates anything is wrong; only a full page reload restores a working canvas.

Proposed fix: Either add `authed` to the mount effect's dependency array (Something2.jsx:508) so canvas rebinding + resizeCanvas() reruns whenever the authenticated view remounts, or move the canvas outside the `!authed` conditional the same way it is already deliberately kept outside the `isPlaying` conditional (see the comment at Something2.jsx:792-798 describing the identical detached-canvas failure mode for tab switches) so the canvas element itself never unmounts on a sign-out/sign-in cycle.

Verification: In the browser: log in, enter any world, confirm the canvas renders. Click Sign out, then log back in with the same account in the same tab (no reload). Expect the canvas to still render the live game; observed instead: canvas.width/height reset to the browser default 300x150, canvas.style.width/height stuck at "100%" (never resized), screen renders blank/black, while the underlying WS session and game loop keep running (confirmed via HP changing with no player input). Reproduced twice.

results.name: [F-044] P3 backend-api: worlds.name has no unique constraint, so POST /api/worlds silently accepts a duplicate ...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:951

Lens: kiss · Source: browser

Claim: worlds.name has no unique constraint, so POST /api/worlds silently accepts a duplicate name with HTTP 201 and no warning, unlike the sibling tile-types/entity-types/item-types catalogs which all reject a duplicate name (albeit with an ugly generic 500 rather than a clean 409).

Failure scenario: Driven live with a valid admin bearer token: POST /api/worlds twice with the identical body {"name":"AuditFlowBWorld","width":24,"height":24} returns HTTP 201 both times, producing two distinct worlds (different UUIDs) that both display as "AuditFlowBWorld" in the Maps admin list and in every N/E/S/W link dropdown, with nothing in the UI or API response to tell them apart beyond re-opening each card. The live dev database already has more than one world sharing the same display name from prior seed/test data (e.g. two rows both named "test2" were present before this session started). The world-links feature does resolve by id rather than name (MapsAdmin.jsx option value={m.id}), so this is a usability/admin-confusion defect rather than a data-integrity one -- an admin cannot tell two same-named worlds apart from the list or dropdowns without opening each one.

Proposed fix: Add a unique constraint on worlds.name (or a case-insensitive unique index) and have POST /api/worlds return 409 on a duplicate, matching the behavior (if not the response quality) of the other three catalogs; surface the conflict as a toast in MapsAdmin the same way ItemTypesAdmin already does for its own duplicate-name case.

Verification: POST /api/worlds twice with the same name and a valid admin token. Currently both return 201 with two distinct world rows sharing the same name; after the fix the second attempt should return 409.

results.name: [F-043] P2 backend-api: None of the four admin-catalog create routes (tile-types, entity-types, item-types, wor...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:477

Lens: user-logic · Source: browser

Claim: None of the four admin-catalog create routes (tile-types, entity-types, item-types, worlds) validates name length, so a pathologically long name produces neither a clean rejection nor a truncation: it is either a raw 500 from an uncaught Postgres error, or silently accepted without limit, depending only on which column type the table happens to use.

Failure scenario: Driven live against the running stack with a valid admin bearer token. POST /api/tile-types and POST /api/entity-types with a 10,000-character name both return HTTP 500 {"error":"Failed to create tile type"} / {"error":"Failed to create entity type"} -- the generic catch-all at index.js:477 (and its entity-types twin) swallows the underlying "value too long for type character varying(255)" Postgres error from the varchar(255) name column (backend/migrations/1714440002000_create_tile_types.js:6, 1714440003000_create_environment_types.js:6) and reports nothing actionable. POST /api/item-types and POST /api/worlds, whose name columns are unbounded text (backend/migrations/1714440016000_create_weapon_types.js:4, 1714440012000_create_worlds_and_chunks.js:4), instead accept the same 10,000-character name with HTTP 201 and store it verbatim -- confirmed live: GET /api/item-types returned the row with name.length === 10000, and the Item Types admin list rendered a 10,000-character <h3> heading with no truncation. Neither behaviour is the "rejected, not truncated silently or 500" outcome an admin would expect from any of the four create forms, and the two failure modes are inconsistent with each other for what is, from the admin UI, the identical "Name" text field pattern repeated across all four panels.

Proposed fix: Add a shared server-side length check (e.g. reject any catalog name over 200 characters with 400 {"error":"name is too long"}) applied uniformly to the four POST routes (and their PUT counterparts) before the INSERT, so a varchar(255) column never sees an over-length value and a text column never silently accepts an unreasonable one. Mirror the same max-length attribute on the four admin forms client-side.

Verification: POST /api/tile-types, /api/entity-types, /api/item-types and /api/worlds each with a 10,000-character name and a valid admin token. Currently: tile-types and entity-types return 500 with a generic message; item-types and worlds return 201 and persist the full 10,000-character name. After the fix, all four should return 400 with an actionable message.

results.name: [F-042] P2 infra: `make clean` runs `docker compose ... down -v --rmi all --remove-orphans` — the -v flag...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: Makefile:27-28

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: `make clean` runs `docker compose ... down -v --rmi all --remove-orphans` — the -v flag deletes the named volumes (postgres_data, redis_data, minio_data, sprite-models) — under a name and with no confirmation prompt that gives no hint it is destroying all local data, unlike down/restart/rebuild which stop containers without touching volumes.

Failure scenario: A developer runs `make clean` expecting the same kind of tidy-up as `down` or `rebuild` (defined right above it in the same file, neither of which touches volumes) to reclaim disk space or clear a stuck container, and instead irreversibly loses the local Postgres database (all maps/entities/users/inventory) and every MinIO-stored sprite, requiring a full re-migrate and re-seed to get back to a working dev environment.

Proposed fix: Rename the target to signal data loss (e.g. nuke or clean-all), or add an interactive confirmation before the -v --rmi all run, and keep a clean that only prunes images/containers without touching volumes.

Verification: Run make clean against a stack with seeded data; confirm postgres_data/minio_data volumes are gone afterward and the app requires re-migration to function.
