results.name: [F-041] P2 infra: Unlike JWT_SECRET, which docker-compose.yml requires via ${JWT_SECRET:?...} sourced fro...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: compose/docker-compose.yml:87-88

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: Unlike JWT_SECRET, which docker-compose.yml requires via ${JWT_SECRET:?...} sourced from the gitignored .env, the Postgres and MinIO credentials are literal values hardcoded directly in the tracked compose file (POSTGRES_PASSWORD here, MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD/MINIO_SECRET_KEY at lines 33, 77, 110), so there is no .env-gated path to change them.

Failure scenario: A developer who decides to stop using the shared default and rotates the Postgres or MinIO password can only do so by editing docker-compose.yml directly, which is tracked in git — the new credential value is committed to the repository in cleartext the moment it's saved, reproducing exactly the kind of secret-in-history exposure the .env/.gitignore split exists to prevent for JWT_SECRET.

Proposed fix: Move POSTGRES_PASSWORD/POSTGRES_USER and the MinIO credential pair into .env-sourced ${VAR:?...} references, matching the pattern already used for JWT_SECRET, so a real rotation never touches a tracked file.

Verification: Change POSTGRES_PASSWORD in docker-compose.yml and run git diff; confirm the new value appears in the diff of a tracked file. After the fix, confirm rotating the password only touches .env.

results.name: [F-040] P2 infra: MinIO's S3 API and admin console are both published with bare port mappings (0.0.0.0:19...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: compose/docker-compose.yml:109-110

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: MinIO's S3 API and admin console are both published with bare port mappings (0.0.0.0:19000, 0.0.0.0:19001 per live docker ps) and MINIO_ROOT_USER/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD are the vendor's shipped default value, hardcoded in the tracked compose file and duplicated identically into the backend and sprite-gen service environments (3 copies total).

Failure scenario: A device on the developer's LAN opens the MinIO console on the host's :19001, logs in with the well-known vendor-default root credentials (never changed since this file was written), and gets full read/write/delete access to every bucket — including overwriting or deleting the sprite assets the client loads and that sprite-gen (F-033) writes to unauthenticated.

Proposed fix: Require MINIO_ROOT_USER/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD via .env with the same ${VAR:?...} pattern already used for JWT_SECRET, generate a non-default value, and bind 19000/19001 to 127.0.0.1 unless LAN access is actually needed.

Verification: From a second LAN machine, load the MinIO console on the host's :19001 and log in with the default credentials; after the fix, confirm the port no longer accepts a connection from off-host. Confirmed in browser/network test (Flow D arbitration sweep), mechanism-level: `ss -tlnp` confirms MinIO's S3 API (19000) and console (19001) both bound to 0.0.0.0/[::], and the console root (`curl http://127.0.0.1:19001/`) returns HTTP 200 (reachable, unauthenticated at the transport level). MINIO_ROOT_USER/PASSWORD confirmed as the literal vendor-default `minioadmin`/`minioadmin` in the tracked compose file. Did not additionally drive a full browser login through the third-party MinIO console UI itself; the reachability + default-credential mechanism is directly confirmed, matching how Flow B settled F-009 on mechanism rather than the full stress variant.

results.name: [F-039] P1 infra: Postgres (db) and Redis are published with bare HOST:CONTAINER port mappings (no bind I...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: compose/docker-compose.yml:90-91

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: Postgres (db) and Redis are published with bare HOST:CONTAINER port mappings (no bind IP), which Docker Compose binds to 0.0.0.0 by default, and Postgres's credentials are the hardcoded literal user/password pair visible in the same file — live `docker ps` confirms both are reachable as 0.0.0.0:15432 and 0.0.0.0:16379, not 127.0.0.1.

Failure scenario: A device on the same LAN/WiFi as the developer's machine connects directly to <host-ip>:15432 using the credentials visible in the tracked compose file and gets full read/write access to the game database — including the users table with password hashes and token_versions — with no other secret needed; Redis on :16379 has no auth configured at all and accepts the same reachability from any LAN peer.

Proposed fix: Bind these ports to 127.0.0.1 in compose/docker-compose.yml (e.g. "127.0.0.1:15432:5432") so they stay reachable from the host and other containers but not the LAN, and set a Redis requirepass.

Verification: From a second machine on the same network, attempt psql against <host-ip>:15432 and redis-cli -h <host-ip> -p 16379 ping; both should time out after rebinding to 127.0.0.1. Confirmed in browser/network test (Flow D arbitration sweep): `ss -tlnp` on the Docker host shows Postgres (15432) and Redis (16379) both listening on 0.0.0.0 and [::] (not 127.0.0.1). Connected with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 15432 -U user -d game_db` using the literal credentials from the tracked compose file and successfully read the users table (16 rows) -- full read access confirmed using nothing but what a LAN-adjacent device could reach and a docker-compose.yml grep.

results.name: [F-038] P0 infra: The live .env's JWT_SECRET has never been changed from the instructional placeholder va...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: .env:4

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: The live .env's JWT_SECRET has never been changed from the instructional placeholder value shipped in the project's own .env.example template, so the running stack signs and verifies session JWTs — including admin-capable ones — with a low-entropy, guessable secret rather than a real random one.

Failure scenario: Any party who reaches the backend (bound 0.0.0.0:13101) or the realtime authority (bound 0.0.0.0:18080) — e.g. another device on the developer's LAN — can sign an HS256 JWT with this exact known secret. Neither authenticate() (backend/src/auth/middleware.js) nor the WS authority's upgrade handler (backend/src/authority/server.js) checks the token's username against the DB; both only require the payload's user_id and tv to match a real row, and both are small sequential integers with no rate limit on this path, so a handful of guesses yields a working, DB-role-backed session — including the seeded admin account — without ever touching the real password.

Proposed fix: Rotate JWT_SECRET in .env to a random 32+ byte value (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`) immediately, and add a boot-time check alongside the existing `:?` requiredness in docker-compose.yml that refuses to start if JWT_SECRET equals any known example/placeholder text.

Verification: Sign a JWT locally with the placeholder secret and a small guessed user_id/tv pair; present it as a Bearer token to an admin-guarded route and as the WS authority's ?token= param; confirm both accept it. After rotating the secret, confirm the same token is rejected.

results.name: [F-037] P2 sprite-gen: The /generate response reports recipe.controlnet/steps/frames from recipe_for(tier) usi...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: sprite-gen/app/main.py:45

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: The /generate response reports recipe.controlnet/steps/frames from recipe_for(tier) using the requested/detected tier, independent of the backend_name actually resolved for the job, so it can describe a pipeline that never runs.

Failure scenario: SPRITE_BACKEND=sd-turbo is permanently set in compose/docker-compose.yml for this deployment. A caller POSTs {tier: 'gpu', creature: 'goblin', base_prompt: 'x'} with no explicit backend, expecting the gpu-tier sdxl/ControlNet pipeline; backend_name resolves to 'sd-turbo' via the SPRITE_BACKEND override instead (confirmed live: test_generate_fills_defaults_from_tier_recipe now gets backend 'sd-turbo' back instead of the expected 'sdxl'), yet the response's recipe.controlnet is still True and steps is still 30, because those fields come from recipe_for('gpu') rather than from what sd-turbo actually does — SDTurboBackend has no ControlNet pipeline at all and internally clamps steps to 4 — so a caller relying on the response to know whether pose-guided ControlNet generation ran is misled.

Proposed fix: Derive controlnet/steps/frames for the response from the resolved backend_name (e.g. a small per-backend capability table) instead of purely from recipe_for(tier), so the reported recipe always matches what actually executes.

Verification: POST /generate with tier: 'gpu' and no backend while SPRITE_BACKEND=sd-turbo is set; confirm the response's controlnet field reads False, matching the backend that will actually run.

results.name: [F-034] P2 sprite-gen: GenerateRequest.kind is an unconstrained string, so any value other than exactly 'tile'...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: sprite-gen/app/main.py:58

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: GenerateRequest.kind is an unconstrained string, so any value other than exactly 'tile' or 'object' silently falls through to the full 8-direction creature pipeline with a different response shape, instead of being rejected.

Failure scenario: A caller sends kind: 'Tile' (capitalized) or any other typo'd/unrecognized value; work()'s `if req.kind == 'tile': ...` and `if req.kind == 'object': ...` both fail to match, so it silently falls through to generate_creature — 8 directions x n_frames instead of the one flat image the caller asked for, roughly 8x the generation time — and the result is stored/returned in put_creature's shape (atlas_key, frame_keys) instead of put_tile/put_object's shape (image_key, frames), so a caller written against the flat shape gets undefined/KeyError reading result['image_key'].

Proposed fix: Change GenerateRequest.kind to Literal['creature', 'tile', 'object'] so FastAPI/Pydantic rejects an unrecognized kind with 422 at the request boundary instead of silently mis-routing it.

Verification: POST /generate with kind: 'Tile' and confirm it now returns 422 instead of 202 with a creature-shaped result.

results.name: [F-033] P1 sprite-gen: POST /generate has no authentication and no upper bound on frames/steps/size, and JobMa...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: sprite-gen/app/main.py:13

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: POST /generate has no authentication and no upper bound on frames/steps/size, and JobManager runs jobs on one synchronous worker thread with no timeout or cancellation, so a single call can monopolize the service for hours with no recovery short of restarting the container.

Failure scenario: Any caller able to reach the sprite-gen container's HTTP port — which by default includes every other container on the compose network, since main.py has no auth middleware at all, and compose/docker-compose.yml publishes it as "18100:8100" with no source-IP restriction (Docker binds 0.0.0.0 by default) — POSTs {creature:'x', base_prompt:'y', kind:'creature', frames:500} with no explicit backend. backend_name resolves to sd-turbo (the deployment default, ~66s/frame observed), so 500 frames x 8 directions = 4000 sequential generations queue on the sole JobManager worker (tens of hours); every other /generate call, including the ones the Node backend's own adminGuard-protected routes submit for real admins, sits queued behind it with no cancel path (jobs.py exposes no kill/cancel) until the container is restarted.

Proposed fix: Clamp frames/steps/size to explicit maxima in the GenerateRequest Pydantic model and reject requests over the max with 422 instead of queueing them; add a bounded job queue and a way to cancel/expire a running job; consider a shared-secret header so only the backend container can reach /generate.

Verification: POST /generate with frames: 500 and confirm it is rejected with 422 rather than accepted with 202; separately confirm (with the infra audit) whether port 18100 is reachable from outside the compose network.

results.name: [F-032] P0 sprite-gen: SPRITE_STORE_ENABLED is a container-wide env flag with no test-mode override, so runnin...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: sprite-gen/app/main.py:108

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: SPRITE_STORE_ENABLED is a container-wide env flag with no test-mode override, so running the sprite-gen pytest suite inside the deployed container performs real writes to the production MinIO 'sprites' bucket.

Failure scenario: docker exec something2-sprite-gen-1 pytest -q (the project's own baseline command) runs test_object_storage_api.py::test_generate_kind_object_manifest_keys_are_flat, which POSTs creature: 'Tree', kind: 'object' to /generate; because SPRITE_STORE_ENABLED=true is set in this container, main.py's work() calls default_store().put_object('Tree', out) for real and overwrites sprites/objects/Tree/{static.png,atlas.png,atlas.json} in the live MinIO bucket with an 8x8 stub placeholder image — 'Tree' is a real row in entity_types (confirmed via the game_db). The same run's test_tile_storage_api.py::test_generate_kind_tile_runs_tile_branch_no_store POSTs creature: 'grass', kind: 'tile', silently overwriting sprites/tiles/grass/static.png — 'grass' is a real row in tile_types — and this second overwrite causes no test failure at all, because put_tile's returned dict happens to still contain a 'frames' key that satisfies the test's assertion.

Proposed fix: Add a pytest-only guard (e.g. an autouse conftest.py fixture that monkeypatches app.main._STORE_ENABLED to False, or a dedicated test-runner entrypoint that unsets SPRITE_STORE_ENABLED / points MINIO_BUCKET at a disposable test bucket) so the suite can never reach default_store() regardless of the container it runs in.

Verification: Note the object timestamp for sprites/tiles/grass/static.png in MinIO, run docker exec something2-sprite-gen-1 pytest -q tests/test_tile_storage_api.py, then confirm the timestamp is unchanged; also confirm app.main._STORE_ENABLED is False inside the pytest process after the fix.

results.name: [F-031] P3 frontend-game: The 't' (toggle tile textures, Game.js:786-789) and 'm' (cycle render-mode override, Ga...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/core/Game.js:780

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: The 't' (toggle tile textures, Game.js:786-789) and 'm' (cycle render-mode override, Game.js:780-783) dev keydown handlers are missing the `!e.repeat` guard that every other one-shot hotkey in the same setupInput() method already uses ('i' at 739, 'e' at 761, 'g' at 773), so they re-fire on every OS auto-repeat tick while the key is held rather than once per physical key press.

Failure scenario: A developer holds 't' down instead of tapping it (even the OS default key-repeat window, typically starting after ~500ms and repeating every ~30-50ms, is enough): toggleTileTextures() flips on/off many times before keyup, each flip also replacing the on-screen toast via _showToast, and the final rendered state on release is whichever parity the repeat count happened to land on — effectively unpredictable from the user's point of view — unlike every other panel/mode hotkey in this same handler, which fires exactly once per press.

Proposed fix: Add `&& !e.repeat` to both the 't' and 'm' conditions, matching the guard already used for 'i', 'e', and 'g' a few lines above each.

Verification: In the browser, press and hold 't' (or 'm') for about a second and release; observe the tile-texture (or render-mode) toggle state after release does not reliably correspond to a single press, and the toast/console log fires repeatedly during the hold.

results.name: [F-030] P2 frontend-game: Game.js's entire non-chunked code path — init() (210-250), setMap() (252-254), the non-...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/core/Game.js:210

Lens: yagni · Source: static

Claim: Game.js's entire non-chunked code path — init() (210-250), setMap() (252-254), the non-chunked branches of update()/render() (462-472, 651-653), _onServerState()/_reconcileSelf() (479-579, including the RECONCILE_SOFT_PX/HARD_PX/LERP tuning constants at 44-46) — plus net/EngineClient.js's WebSocket-wrapper class (lines 19-131 only, not the auth helper functions below it which ARE used elsewhere), core/Map.js (264 lines), entities/MapEntity.js, and the 'legacy single-Map path' branch of Player.update (entities/Player.js:56-125) are never reached by the shipped app: Something2.jsx never calls Game.prototype.init, never calls setEngineClient with a real client (only the teardown call `setEngineClient?.(null, null)` at Something2.jsx:461), and never does `new EngineClient(...)` anywhere in frontend/src (confirmed by repo-wide grep). No test file calls Game.prototype.init, setEngineClient, or instantiates the EngineClient WS-wrapper class either.

Failure scenario: A developer, reading Game.js's own inline comments describing dual chunked/non-chunked support, spends time tuning RECONCILE_SOFT_PX/RECONCILE_HARD_PX/RECONCILE_LERP (Game.js:44-46) or fixing a suspected bug in _reconcileSelf (Game.js:562-579) to smooth out perceived player rubber-banding in production — but that code path only executes via _onServerState, which only fires from an EngineClient instance that Something2.jsx never creates, so the change has zero effect on any real session; the actual live reconciliation path is net/reconcile.js via _onWorldState, an entirely separate implementation with its own tuning. The same trap applies to anyone patching core/Map.js's collision/tile logic or Player.js's non-ChunkedMap branch believing it still backs some reachable in-game mode: the fix ships, the tests (if any are added against the dead path) pass, and no real player is ever affected because the code never runs.

Proposed fix: Delete the unreachable branches: Game.init/setMap/_onServerState/_reconcileSelf and their RECONCILE_* constants, the EngineClient WS-wrapper class (relocate the still-used auth helper functions below it into their own module first), core/Map.js, entities/MapEntity.js, and Player.update's legacy branch. This removes roughly 500 lines split across Game.js/Player.js/Map.js/EngineClient.js, directly shrinking Game.js and Player.js without touching any code that actually executes, and removes the risk of a future change being made against a path with no effect.

Verification: Repo-wide grep confirms no reachable call site: `grep -rn "new EngineClient(" frontend/src` returns nothing; `grep -rn "setEngineClient" frontend/src/games/something2/Something2.jsx` shows only the `(null, null)` teardown call; `grep -rln "\.init(\|setEngineClient\|new EngineClient" frontend/src/games/something2/src/js` returns only core/Game.js itself (the definition site, not a caller).

results.name: [F-029] P2 frontend-game: renderChunked's tile-draw loop iterates every cell chunkTileCells (core/chunkTiles.js:3...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/systems/RenderSystem.js:119

Lens: kiss · Source: static

Claim: renderChunked's tile-draw loop iterates every cell chunkTileCells (core/chunkTiles.js:38-60) returns — which culls only at whole-CHUNK granularity via chunkVisible — and calls worldToScreen plus allocates a cell object for EVERY tile of every chunk-visible chunk, before RenderSystem.js:123's per-tile relX/relY bounds check throws most of them away. With the backend's default chunkSize of 64 (backend/src/authority/world.js:81) and ChunkStreamer's radius of 1 (core/Game.js:290 -> 9 loaded chunks), that is up to 9*64*64 = 36864 worldToScreen calls and object allocations rebuilt from scratch every single animation frame.

Failure scenario: On the fixed 1280x720 canvas (GAME_WIDTH/HEIGHT) with 128x64 iso diamonds (ISO_TILE_W/H), well under a thousand tiles are ever actually on screen, but chunkTileCells enumerates and projects all ~36864 loaded-and-chunk-visible cells every frame at 60fps before the bulk are discarded by the per-tile cull at RenderSystem.js:123 — over an order of magnitude more worldToScreen calls and array pushes than the frame needs, with the array itself reallocated fresh every frame. This is the dominant avoidable per-frame cost in the render path and gets strictly worse the moment chunkSize or the streamer radius is increased, or on lower-end/mobile hardware, directly lowering frame rate during ordinary movement rather than during any one heavy action.

Proposed fix: Push the existing per-tile relX/relY visibility check (RenderSystem.js:123) down into chunkTileCells itself (or compute a cheap local row/col range per visible chunk from the camera bounds) so off-screen cells are never constructed or projected in the first place — chunkVisible already proves this exact pattern one granularity up (chunk-level) and it just needs to be repeated at tile-level.

Verification: In the browser with devtools Performance recording, join a chunked world and walk continuously; compare the cell count chunkTileCells produces for a frame against the count that survives the RenderSystem.js:123 per-tile cull for that same frame, and measure time spent inside renderChunked's tile loop.

Failure scenario: The backend authority process restarts (deploy, crash, or a transient network blip) while a player is mid-session. The WebSocket 'close' event fires WorldAuthorityClient.onClose, which only flips the unused `authorityJoined` flag; Game.state stays 'playing' and the rAF loop keeps calling update()/render() every frame, so the player's sprite keeps moving under local prediction (Player.update against the already-loaded chunkedMap) and the screen looks fully live. Verification: In the browser: join a chunked world, then force-close the authority WebSocket (devtools Network tab, or kill/restart the authority server process). Confirm the player sprite keeps responding to WASD with no on-screen indication anything is wrong, and that pressing 'g'/'e' or left-clicking to attack produces no toast and no visible error — only a manual reload restores play. confirmed in browser: joined MerchantVerify (bounded, creature-free world) as an admin session, captured a reference to the live authority WebSocket via an injected constructor wrapper, and called ws.close() directly on it (readyState went OPEN -> CLOSING -> CLOSED=3). Over the following 10+ seconds: zero new WebSocket connections appeared (no reconnect attempt), zero console output of any kind referencing the disconnect, and no toast/visual state change. Pressing 'd' afterward still moved the on-screen sprite (local prediction against the already-loaded chunkedMap continued rendering), giving no on-screen indication the session was dead -- an exact match for the finding's claimed defect. Only a full page reload restored a live connection.

results.name: [F-027] P2 frontend-admin: TileTypesAdmin's delete has no check for whether an entity type's spawn_tiles reference...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/EntityTypesAdmin.jsx:1064

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: TileTypesAdmin's delete has no check for whether an entity type's spawn_tiles references the tile being deleted, and EntityTypesAdmin's Spawn Tiles multi-select (line 1064-1075) only renders checkboxes for tiles currently in tileTypes, so a dangling spawn_tiles entry left behind by a tile deletion becomes permanently invisible and un-removable through the admin UI.

Failure scenario: An admin creates entity type "Cactus" with spawn_tiles ["sand"], then later deletes the "sand" tile type from the Tile Types tab (TileTypesAdmin.jsx:432-436, a bare window.confirm with no reference check; DELETE /api/tile-types/:id has no FK/consistency guard either, index.js:503-517). entity_types.spawn_tiles is untouched jsonb, so the "Cactus" row still contains ["sand"]. Reopening Cactus in EntityTypesAdmin, the Spawn Tiles MultiSelect only iterates the live tileTypes list (line 1065), so the checkbox for "sand" no longer exists — the admin cannot see or uncheck it. Any Save Changes on that entity re-sends the untouched formData.spawn_tiles array, so the dead reference persists indefinitely, invisible in the UI that is supposed to be its source of truth.

Proposed fix: Before deleting a tile type, query which entity types reference it in spawn_tiles (and vice versa for valid_neighbors) and either block the delete with a 409 listing the referencing rows, or cascade-strip the name from those arrays in the same request; at minimum, have EntityTypesAdmin render orphaned spawn_tiles entries (e.g. greyed out with a "tile no longer exists" note and a way to remove them) instead of silently dropping them from the visible list.

Verification: Create an entity type with a spawn tile checked, delete that tile type from the Tile Types tab, then reopen the entity type's edit modal. Expect either a warning about the dangling reference or a way to clear it; currently expect the Spawn Tiles list to simply omit it with no indication anything is wrong. confirmed in browser: created an entity type with spawn_tiles:["auditfixturetile"] referencing a fresh tile type, then deleted that tile type. After a fresh page load, the entity type's edit modal Spawn Tiles list simply omitted the checkbox for the deleted tile with no warning, while GET /api/entity-types confirmed the row's spawn_tiles array still contained the dangling "auditfixturetile" string. Same defect class as F-005 (name-keyed reference, zero integrity check) but a distinct trigger (tile delete vs entity rename) and a different, non-crashing consequence (silent object-density loss vs. zero-creature-placement) -- not merging these myself per the audit brief.

results.name: [F-026] P2 frontend-admin: MapPreview.jsx and the legacy flat-map hooks it depends on (useMaps, fetchMap, fetchMap...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/MapPreview.jsx:39

Lens: yagni · Source: static

Claim: MapPreview.jsx and the legacy flat-map hooks it depends on (useMaps, fetchMap, fetchMapEntities, useGenerateMap, useDeleteMap, useSaveEntities, useGenerateEntities — all in useMaps.js) have zero call sites anywhere in the frontend; the whole "maps" subsystem was superseded by the worlds/chunked system (useWorlds.js, MapsAdmin.jsx) but was never removed.

Failure scenario: A developer greps for "map preview" or "generate map" while extending the admin UI, finds MapPreview.jsx and useGenerateMap looking like a complete, working feature (styled, commented, animated), and wires a new screen to them assuming they are the supported path. It would call the legacy /api/maps/generate and /api/maps/:id endpoints (index.js:158,520,535,560,579,624,651), producing a map that lives in the old `maps` table and never appears in MapsAdmin.jsx's boundedMaps list or the world picker in Something2.jsx, because both only read from /api/worlds. The map looks like it silently vanished.

Proposed fix: Delete MapPreview.jsx and the unused legacy exports from useMaps.js (useMaps, fetchMap, fetchMapEntities, useGenerateMap, useDeleteMap, useSaveEntities, useGenerateEntities) together with their backend routes, or if the flat-map system is still needed for some path this audit did not find, wire at least one admin entry point to it so it is not silently unreachable.

Verification: grep -rn "MapPreview\|useGenerateMap\|useDeleteMap\b\|useSaveEntities\|fetchMap(\|fetchMapEntities" frontend/src --include=*.jsx --include=*.js, excluding the defining files themselves; expect zero matches, confirming nothing renders or calls these today.

results.name: [F-025] P2 frontend-admin: EntityTypesAdmin and TileTypesAdmin only validate that name is non-empty before submitt...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/EntityTypesAdmin.jsx:819

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: EntityTypesAdmin and TileTypesAdmin only validate that name is non-empty before submitting, while the sibling ItemTypesAdmin mirrors the backend's category-aware validateItemType() (validateClient(), ItemTypesAdmin.jsx:372-396) — and the backend for entity-types/tile-types has no equivalent bounds check either (index.js:208-237, 457-475 only check `!name || !color`), so stats like hp, max_hp, mana, strength and chance can be saved negative or nonsensical with no error anywhere.

Failure scenario: An admin editing a creature entity type mistypes Max HP as -50 (EntityTypesAdmin.jsx:1049-1050, a bare <input type="number"> with no min/max and no client check). handleSubmit (line 819) only checks formData.name.trim(); it saves. PUT /api/entity-types/:id (index.js:239-270) writes max_hp=-50 verbatim with no server-side validation either. The row now persists a negative max HP with no error ever shown to the admin, unlike the Item Types form, which would have rejected an equally invalid weapon/armor/ammo combination client-side before the request was even sent.

Proposed fix: Add a validateClient()-style check to EntityTypesAdmin and TileTypesAdmin (at minimum: numeric stats >= 0, chance in [0,1], speed in [0,2]) mirroring the pattern ItemTypesAdmin already established, and add the matching server-side check in index.js so the gap is closed on both sides rather than just the one panel that happens to have it.

Verification: In the Entity Types admin, edit an entity and set Max HP to -50, click Save Changes. Expect a client-side validation error naming the field; currently expect the save to succeed silently. confirmed in browser: edited the existing Wolf entity type, set Max HP to -50, clicked Save Changes. No client-side validation error appeared; PUT /api/entity-types/:id returned 200 and GET afterward confirmed max_hp:-50 persisted with no error anywhere. Reverted Wolf to its original max_hp:12 immediately after to avoid leaving a shared fixture broken for later flows.

results.name: [F-024] P2 frontend-admin: useCreateEntityType/useUpdateEntityType/useDeleteEntityType and useCreateTileType/useUp...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/useMaps.js:238

Lens: dry · Source: static

Claim: useCreateEntityType/useUpdateEntityType/useDeleteEntityType and useCreateTileType/useUpdateTileType/useDeleteTileType throw a hardcoded generic Error string on a non-ok response, discarding the backend's {error: "..."} body, while the otherwise-identical useCreateItemType/useUpdateItemType/useDeleteItemType (useMaps.js:291-349) parse that same body and surface the real message.

Failure scenario: Two admins have the Entity Types tab open. Admin A opens Edit on "Goblin". Admin B deletes "Goblin" in their own tab. Admin A edits a stat and clicks Save Changes: PUT /api/entity-types/:id returns 404 {"error":"Entity type not found"} (index.js:264), but useUpdateEntityType (useMaps.js:230-248) ignores the body and throws the fixed string "Failed to update entity type", so the toast reads "Update failed: Failed to update entity type" — it never tells Admin A the row is gone and a refresh is needed. Running the identical race in the Item Types tab shows "Update failed: Item type not found" (useUpdateItemType parses error.error at useMaps.js:315-319), which is actually actionable.

Proposed fix: Give useCreateEntityType/useUpdateEntityType/useDeleteEntityType and the three tile-type mutations the same res.json().catch(()=>({})) parse-and-throw pattern already used by the item-type mutations, or extract one shared apiMutationError(res) helper so the four catalogs cannot drift again.

Verification: With two browser tabs signed in as admin: in tab 1 open Edit on an entity type, in tab 2 delete that same entity type, then in tab 1 click Save Changes. Expect the toast to name the real reason ("Entity type not found"); currently expect the generic "Failed to update entity type". confirmed in browser: opened Edit on a fresh entity type, deleted that same row via a background request (simulating a second admin tab), then clicked Save Changes in the still-open modal. The backend correctly returned 404 {"error":"Entity type not found"}, but the toast shown was the generic hardcoded "Update failed: Failed to update entity type" -- the specific backend reason was discarded exactly as claimed.

results.name: [F-023] P1 frontend-admin: MapsAdmin destructures only {worlds, isLoadingWorlds} from useWorlds() and never reads ...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: frontend/src/games/something2/MapsAdmin.jsx:153

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: MapsAdmin destructures only {worlds, isLoadingWorlds} from useWorlds() and never reads worldsError, so a failed /api/worlds fetch renders the same "no maps yet" empty state as a genuinely empty catalog.

Failure scenario: An admin's session token has been revoked (password rotated, logout-everywhere) or the network blips while the Maps tab is open. useWorlds() (useWorlds.js:10-18) sets worldsError from the query, and its own comment says "errors are surfaced via the returned error and toasted by the caller" — Something2.jsx honors that contract (Something2.jsx:396-402, toasts worldsError), but MapsAdmin.jsx:153 does not. isLoadingWorlds flips to false, worlds stays undefined, boundedMaps becomes [], and MapsAdmin renders "No bounded maps yet. Generate one above." with zero indication anything failed. The admin, seeing an apparently-empty catalog, may click "Generate map" and create a duplicate of a map that still exists server-side but simply failed to load.

Proposed fix: Destructure worldsError from useWorlds() in MapsAdmin.jsx and toast it in a useEffect, mirroring the pattern already used in Something2.jsx (lines 400-402), or better, lift that effect into useWorlds() itself so every caller gets it for free instead of each one having to remember to opt in.

Verification: In the browser, open the Maps admin tab, then force /api/worlds to fail (revoke the token via `make admin-password` in another tab, or block the request in devtools) and reload the tab. Expect an error toast and a visibly-different state from "no maps yet"; currently expect the empty-state message with no toast. confirmed in browser: patched fetch to reject only /api/worlds while leaving every other endpoint (including auth) working, then opened the Maps admin tab. After the query settled, MapsAdmin rendered "No bounded maps yet. Generate one above." with no toast, no error banner, and nothing in the console -- indistinguishable from a genuinely empty catalog.

results.name: [F-022] P3 backend-authority: player_items.quantity is read and preserved by four code paths but written above 1 by n...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/trade.js:82

Lens: yagni · Source: static

Claim: player_items.quantity is read and preserved by four code paths but written above 1 by none, and sellItem silently destroys any surplus if a stack ever appears.

Failure scenario: consumeAmmo and ammoCount (ammo.js:37 and 67) are built entirely around multi-unit stacks, claimItem copies world_items.quantity into the inventory row (loot.js:120) and dropItem carries it back out (loot.js:229) — but every INSERT into player_items in the tree writes quantity 1 or the column default: trade.js:40, items.js:100, index.js:424, and spawnDrops, which deliberately inserts one ground item per unit rolled (loot.js:72-82). SELECT count(*) FROM player_items WHERE quantity > 1 on the live game_db returns 0. So the ammo module's central design decision — the pick CTE and its long comment about stacks never being merged — is defending a state that nothing produces. The trap it leaves is in sellItem (trade.js:81-101): it DELETEs the whole row regardless of quantity, pays sellPriceFor(value) for a single unit, and lists exactly one buyback item, so the first write path that ever creates a stack turns selling it into a silent loss of every unit but one.

Proposed fix: Decide the question once. results.name: [F-021] P3 backend-authority: The token-revocation check — SELECT token_version, compare against the JWT's tv — exist...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:134

Lens: dry · Source: static

Claim: The token-revocation check — SELECT token_version, compare against the JWT's tv — exists in two independent copies, one in the HTTP middleware and one in the WS upgrade handler, with no test asserting they agree.

Failure scenario: Both copies read token_version and reject when it differs from payload.tv (auth/middleware.js:37-46 and authority/server.js:134-136). They agree today and nothing is currently broken, which is why this is recorded at P3 rather than higher. The cost is prospective and specific: any second revocation condition has to be added in both places. Adding a ban or disabled flag, an issued-at floor, or a move to a session table means editing two files whose SELECT lists have already diverged (the middleware also selects role; the WS query does not), and a change applied only to the HTTP copy would leave a banned account's live game socket running until it disconnects — which is precisely the failure the WS copy exists to prevent.

Proposed fix: Extract the check into one exported helper in backend/src/auth (for example assertTokenCurrent(pool, payload) returning the user row or null) and have both callers use it, keeping their transport-specific responses — 401 JSON versus socket.destroy() — at the call sites.

Verification: Not statically checkable. After extraction, one test that bumps a user's token_version and asserts both an HTTP request and a live WS upgrade are rejected covers both call sites, which no current test does. confirmed in browser: registered a fresh player account, called POST /api/auth/logout-all to bump token_version, then reused the pre-bump JWT against both GET /api/auth/me (401 'token revoked') and a live WebSocket upgrade to ws://localhost:13101/authority?token=... (connection rejected before handshake) — the two independent checks currently agree with no divergence observed; the underlying duplication and missing regression test remain as described.

results.name: [F-020] P2 backend-authority: The socket message handler is a 320-line if-chain in which every branch invents its own...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:376

Lens: solid · Source: static

Claim: The socket message handler is a 320-line if-chain in which every branch invents its own guards, so input validation is applied inconsistently and the gaps are where this surface's two worst defects live.

Failure scenario: server.js:376-698 dispatches eleven message types with no shared envelope validation and no per-type argument spec. The inconsistency is already in the tree: drop, buy and sell type-check their id (typeof msg.itemId !== "string" at 614, 651, 676), while equip and unequip pass msg.itemId and msg.slot straight through, pickup and interact check nothing, and join neither validates nor normalises msg.world_id. No branch checks that the frame is an object at all. Those last two gaps are not hypothetical: they are the process-killing `null` frame and the duplicate-world-shard exploit filed separately against this same handler, and one validated dispatch point would have closed both. The ongoing cost is that any cross-cutting concern — per-type rate limiting, a protocol version, an audit log of client commands, a per-type auth check — currently means eleven independent edits with eleven chances to miss one, which is exactly how the present inconsistency arose. Six of the branches also repeat the identical ws._opChain serialisation-plus-try/catch boilerplate verbatim.

Proposed fix: Replace the if-chain with a dispatch table keyed on msg.type, each entry declaring its handler plus a small argument spec (types, and an id format where applicable), and validate the envelope once before dispatch — msg is a plain object and msg.type is a known string. Handlers then receive already-validated values, and the ws._opChain wrapper repeated in six branches becomes one shared decorator rather than six copies.

Verification: Structural. After the change, assert that for each message type a frame with a wrong-typed field is rejected uniformly, and that the frames null, [], 1 and "x" are all ignored without reaching any handler.

results.name: [F-019] P2 backend-authority: buyStock looks the stock row up by id alone — it never checks that the row belongs to t...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/trade.js:16

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: buyStock looks the stock row up by id alone — it never checks that the row belongs to the village the player is standing at, to the world they are in, or that it has not expired — so the "no merchant nearby" gate does not constrain what can actually be bought.

Failure scenario: The buy handler (server.js:657) only asserts that SOME merchant is within INTERACT_RADIUS and then discards the village it found, passing only msg.stockId to buyStock, which selects WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE (trade.js:17) and reads village_id into a variable it never compares against anything. A player who has once opened village A's shop — the shop frame at server.js:639 hands them every row id — can then walk to village B, or travel through a doorway into a different world entirely, and buy A's unique player-buyback listings from B's merchant, taking an item out of a village they are not in and cannot currently reach. The same missing predicate makes expired listings purchasable: expires_at is only swept lazily per village by fetchShop (merchantStock.js:37-40) and buyStock has no expires_at predicate at all, so a buyback row whose 3-day window has lapsed still sells as long as nobody has opened that village's shop since it expired. Stock ids are UUIDs so this is not blind guessing, but it makes the physical-merchant model advisory rather than enforced, which is the entire premise of villages. The sell handler at server.js:684 already passes village.id through; buy is the one that does not.

Proposed fix: Pass the village resolved by nearestMerchantVillage into buyStock the way the sell handler already does, and add AND village_id = $2 AND world_id = $3 AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) to the FOR UPDATE select, so the row's location and validity are decided inside the same locked read that decides the sale.

Verification: With two villages that both have merchants, open village A's shop and record a buyback row's stockId, then stand at village B's merchant and send {"type":"buy","stockId":"<A's id>"}. Currently expect a bought frame and the row to vanish from A's catalog; after the fix expect {"type":"error","message":"that item is no longer for sale"} and the row still listed in A. Confirmed in browser (Flow D arbitration sweep): sold an item at village A's merchant (test4) to create a buyback row, recorded its stockId, then walked to village B's merchant in the SAME world and sent {"type":"buy","stockId":"<village A's buyback id>"}. Server replied {"type":"bought",...}, gold decreased by the buyback price (100->87), and the row vanished from merchant_stock -- confirmed bought from a different village's merchant than the one it belonged to, exactly as claimed. The "no merchant nearby" gate only checked that SOME merchant was in range, never that the specific stockId belonged to it.

results.name: [F-018] P2 backend-authority: activateChunk uses the world_chunks INSERT as its once-only spawn flag but commits it b...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:247

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: activateChunk uses the world_chunks INSERT as its once-only spawn flag but commits it before the rest of the activation, so a transient failure afterwards leaves that chunk permanently free of wild creatures — and the empty catch means nothing is logged.

Failure scenario: activateChunk (server.js:247-300) runs INSERT INTO world_chunks ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id and uses ins.rowCount > 0 as the guard for spawnChunkCreatures (server.js:262). Every statement in the function is its own transaction. If any later statement throws — a per-creature INSERT, the creature SELECT, the world_items SELECT — control reaches the bare catch at server.js:295, which logs nothing, and the chunk is deliberately left out of loadedChunks so recomputeActive (server.js:315, every 4 ticks, roughly 200 ms) retries it. But on every retry the world_chunks row now exists, ins.rowCount is 0, and the creature-spawn block is skipped. The chunk is therefore permanently empty of wild creatures in any unbounded world, and no amount of retrying, rejoining or restarting the server recovers it — the only remedy is deleting the world_chunks row by hand. Because the catch is silent, the operator sees neither the original error nor the 5 Hz retry loop it starts, and a player standing in that chunk simply sees a world with nothing in it.

Proposed fix: Make materialisation and spawning one unit of work: take a client and wrap the world_chunks INSERT together with the creature INSERTs in a single BEGIN/COMMIT, so a failure rolls the world_chunks row back and the retry genuinely retries. Independently, log the swallowed error at server.js:295 (console.error("chunk activation failed:", chunkKey, err)) so the condition is visible at all, and add a backoff so a persistently failing chunk is not re-attempted five times a second.

Verification: Inject a pool whose INSERT INTO world_creatures rejects exactly once, activate a fresh chunk in an unbounded world, let the next retry succeed, then run SELECT count(*) FROM world_creatures WHERE world_id = '<id>' AND x >= <chunk x0> AND x < <chunk x1>. Currently expect 0 permanently; after the fix expect the retry to spawn that chunk's creatures.

results.name: [F-017] P1 backend-authority: evictWorld refuses to evict a world that has live sockets and returns false, and every ...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:913

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: evictWorld refuses to evict a world that has live sockets and returns false, and every admin caller discards that boolean, so world-content edits silently fail to reach exactly the worlds people are playing in.

Failure scenario: A loaded world entry snapshots row, tileTypes, creatureTypes, itemTypes, links and villages once in loadWorld (server.js:150-194) and is only ever dropped when the last player leaves (server.js:715) or by evictWorld. evictWorld returns false without doing anything when entry.sockets.size > 0 (server.js:916), and all four callers — index.js:1064, 1089, 1146 and invalidateWorld at index.js:1172 — ignore the return value. So POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures on a world with even one player online DELETEs and re-INSERTs world_creatures (index.js:1110, 1133) while the live sim keeps its old in-memory creature objects: those players keep fighting creatures that no longer exist in the database, and each kill calls commitCreatureDeath, whose DELETE ... RETURNING matches nothing (loot.js:48-51, rowCount 0), so it returns early and awards no drops and no gold at all. The route replies 200 {"placed": N} and the admin sees success. The same staleness applies to villages and links: creating a village with a merchant via POST /api/worlds/:id/villages leaves entry.villages empty, so interact at the new merchant answers "no merchant nearby" indefinitely and planBind never binds a respawn point, with nothing anywhere reporting why. activateChunk does not rescue this, because it skips any chunk already in loadedChunks.

Proposed fix: Give the authority a refresh path that re-reads row, links and villages and reconciles the creature set in place, and call it from the same admin mutations instead of relying on eviction; keep evictWorld for the idle case. At minimum, propagate the refusal: have the admin routes read the boolean and report to the caller that the change will not take effect until the world empties, so a re-roll that did nothing does not present as a success.

Verification: With one player connected to a bounded world, re-roll that world's creatures from the admin UI, then have the player kill a creature it can still see. Currently expect no drop and no gold, and SELECT count(*), min(x) FROM world_creatures WHERE world_id = '<id>' to disagree with what the player is looking at; after the fix expect the player's creature set to match the database. Confirmed in browser (Flow D arbitration sweep), via the actual admin endpoint (not a synthetic reproduction): with a player connected to BoundedArena, called POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures (re-roll) via the real admin route after the DB already showed 0 wild creatures for that world. The connected player's live session kept receiving 'creatures' broadcast frames listing ~1600-1700 stale creature entries (the pre-re-roll swarm) for the remainder of the session -- contact damage from those DB-nonexistent creatures repeatedly dropped the player's hp to 0 and respawned them in a loop (hp series oscillating 100->5->100 across dozens of ticks), and melee kills against them registered hit:true client-side but spawned zero loot/gold (commitCreatureDeath's DELETE...RETURNING matched 0 rows, confirmed via world_items staying empty after several confirmed hits) -- exactly the "no drop, no gold, sim disagrees with DB" failure the finding describes, reproduced with a stronger real-world consequence (sustained player death-loop) than the finding's own minimal repro. Root-causing why this specific world entry never later self-healed even after every socket cleanly disconnected was not fully isolated (repeated attempts at a minimal single-account reconnect repro on two untouched virgin worlds, including 6x rapid-fire reconnects, did not reproduce a stuck entry) -- but the core claim (evictWorld silently no-ops while any player is connected, so admin edits never reach a live world) is directly and unambiguously confirmed via the real API.

results.name: [F-016] P1 backend-authority: dropItem DELETEs the inventory row and INSERTs the ground item as two independent pool....
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/loot.js:218

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: dropItem DELETEs the inventory row and INSERTs the ground item as two independent pool.query calls with no transaction, so a failure between them destroys the item permanently.

results.name: [F-015] P1 backend-authority: The WebSocketServer is constructed with no maxPayload and no handler applies any rate l...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:103

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: The WebSocketServer is constructed with no maxPayload and no handler applies any rate limit or queue bound, so a single authenticated socket can force 100 MiB allocations per frame and queue unbounded database work.

Failure scenario: new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true }) at server.js:103 inherits ws 8.21.1's default maxPayload of 104857600 bytes (backend/node_modules/ws/lib/websocket-server.js:74). One authenticated player can therefore send repeated ~100 MiB text frames; ws buffers each one, converts it to a string, and hands it to JSON.parse at server.js:378, so a handful of concurrent frames exhausts the container heap and the process is OOM-killed, dropping every player and the co-hosted HTTP API with it. A cheaper variant needs no large frames at all: every mutating handler appends to ws._opChain (server.js:495, 564, 583, 615, 652, 677) with no depth bound, and each link performs at least one database round trip — interact performs two, one of them a DELETE against merchant_stock (merchantStock.js:37). A client that streams {"type":"interact"} frames faster than the chain drains (tens of thousands per second arriving against roughly a thousand round trips per second completing) grows an ever-deeper promise chain of retained closures while monopolising a pool connection, so resident memory climbs monotonically and other players' merchant reads contend on the same table indefinitely. Nothing anywhere in the authority counts, sizes or throttles inbound frames.

Proposed fix: Pass an explicit maxPayload to the WebSocketServer sized to the largest legitimate frame (a join frame is well under 1 KB; 4096 is generous), so an oversized frame closes the socket with code 1009 before it is buffered. Add a per-socket token bucket checked before dispatch, and bound ws._opChain by tracking its depth and refusing new work above a small limit instead of queueing it.

Verification: With a valid player JWT, send one 100 MiB frame while watching docker stats something2-backend-1, then send 50000 {"type":"interact"} frames in a burst while watching RSS and SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity. Currently expect RSS to climb by roughly the frame size and to keep climbing under the burst; after the fix expect the oversized frame to close the socket with 1009 and the burst to be dropped at a fixed rate.

results.name: [F-014] P1 backend-authority: join passes the client's raw world_id straight into the in-memory worlds Map key, and P...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:388

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: join passes the client's raw world_id straight into the in-memory worlds Map key, and Postgres accepts several spellings of the same UUID, so a client can conjure a second private simulation of a world and become invisible and untargetable to everyone in the real one.

Failure scenario: worlds.id is a uuid column (migration 1714440012000_create_worlds_and_chunks.js:3). loadWorld(msg.world_id) at server.js:388/150 looks the client string up in the worlds Map by JavaScript identity and, on a miss, runs SELECT ... FROM worlds WHERE id = $1. Postgres uuid input is case-insensitive and also accepts braced and hyphenless forms — verified against something2-db-1: 'A0EEBC99-9C0B-4EF8-BB6D-6BB9BD380A11'::uuid, '{a0eebc99-...}'::uuid and 'a0eebc999c0b4ef8bb6d6bb9bd380a11'::uuid all compare equal to the canonical form. So a client that sends its world id upper-cased gets a Map miss, a successful row fetch, and a SECOND worlds entry backed by the same database world. entry.sockets and world.players are per-entry, so the tick loop's state broadcast (server.js:832) never lists that player for anyone in the canonical entry and never lists anyone else for them: they are invisible and cannot be hit by melee or projectiles, while still killing the same world_creatures rows and looting the same world_items. Both entries also simulate and flushAndPrune-persist the same creature rows independently, so a creature killed in one shard keeps chasing and damaging players in the other and yields no loot when killed there (commitCreatureDeath's DELETE returns rowCount 0). Nothing normalises the value on any path: ws.worldId, persist(), pendingArrivals and evictWorld all key on the same client-supplied string.

Proposed fix: Key the worlds Map on the id RETURNED by loadWorld's SELECT rather than on the client's string, and set ws.worldId from that canonical value — this is the smallest change and also fixes every other worlds.get(ws.worldId) call site. Alternatively reject a world_id that is not the canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID form with a { type: "error" } reply, as part of the envelope validation this handler lacks.

Verification: With two player accounts and one real world id: have account A send {"type":"join","world_id":"<id>"} and account B send {"type":"join","world_id":"<the same id upper-cased>"}, then walk both onto the same tile. Currently expect neither state frame to list the other player and melee swings to connect with nothing; after the fix expect both to appear in each other's state frames. confirmed in browser: opened two raw authority WebSockets from the page context with two different real player accounts (admin user_id=1, audit_flowC_user2 user_id=456), both sending {"type":"join","world_id":<MerchantVerify id>} -- one with the id lower-cased, one upper-cased. Both got a `joined` frame (HTTP-equivalent success), but each connection's subsequent `state` frames listed only its own player id (["1"] and ["456"] respectively) -- neither ever saw the other. Control test with both connections using the identical lower-case id showed each `state` frame correctly listing both ["1","456"], isolating the case difference as the specific cause and ruling out any other confound (e.g. distinct accounts alone do not cause this).

results.name: [F-013] P0 backend-authority: grantStartingLoadout is gated on "this account owns zero items", which is a state the p...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:415

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: grantStartingLoadout is gated on "this account owns zero items", which is a state the player can re-enter at will, so reconnecting after emptying the inventory mints a fresh dagger and leather-vest every time.

Failure scenario: A player joins, unequips both starting items and sends two `drop` frames. dropItem (loot.js:218) DELETEs both player_items rows, so the account now owns nothing while both items lie on the ground with a 10-minute TTL. The player closes the socket and reconnects: server.js:415 sees inv.items.length === 0 and calls grantStartingLoadout, whose only guard is `SELECT id FROM player_items WHERE user_id = $1 LIMIT 1` (items.js:92), so it inserts a fresh dagger and leather-vest. The player walks back and picks up the originals: net +2 items per reconnect, unbounded, needing nothing but a page reload. The same loop pays cash without the ground-item step: the live catalog has dagger value 26 and leather-vest value 16 (confirmed via GET /api/item-types on localhost:13101), so selling both to a village merchant credits floor(26/2) + floor(16/2) = 21 gold via sellItem (trade.js:95) and leaves the account at zero items, ready for the next join to re-grant. Gold buys anything in the village base catalog (merchantStock.js:29), so this is unbounded item and currency generation available to every account.

Proposed fix: Make the grant once-per-account rather than once-per-empty-inventory: record it on the account (a users.starting_loadout_granted_at column, or a player_grants row) and gate on that, inside a single statement so two concurrent joins cannot both grant. If a genuine "re-kit a destitute player" behaviour is wanted, make it an explicit and rate-limited action rather than a side effect of join.

Verification: In the browser: note the gold total, unequip and sell the starting dagger and leather-vest to a village merchant, reload the page to reconnect, and open the inventory. Currently expect a fresh dagger and leather-vest plus gold up by 21; repeat once to confirm it is unbounded. After the fix expect an empty inventory on the second join. CONFIRMED in browser, definitively, twice in a row. Using a clean account (never before touched) that still held its original starting dagger+leather-vest: sold both to a village merchant while standing at its merchant tile (sellPriceFor: floor(26/2)+floor(16/2)=21), then did a clean close+reconnect (confirmed close event, 800ms settle) and rejoined the same world. The new join granted a FRESH dagger and leather-vest (different player_items instance ids from the ones just sold, e.g. dagger 725c1afb... replacing sold 35f2cf45...) and gold was up by exactly 21 (0 -> 21). Repeated the whole cycle a second time on the same account: sold the fresh loadout again, reconnected again, got ANOTHER fresh dagger+vest (yet another new instance-id pair) and gold now at 42 (21+21) -- unbounded item and currency generation confirmed exactly as the finding predicts, with the gold delta matching the predicted arithmetic exactly on both cycles.

results.name: [F-012] P0 backend-authority: The WebSocket message handler dereferences msg.type without checking that the parsed fr...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/authority/server.js:378

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: The WebSocket message handler dereferences msg.type without checking that the parsed frame is an object, so a frame whose body is the four bytes `null` throws inside an async listener and terminates the whole Node process.

Failure scenario: Any registered account opens ws://localhost:13101/authority?token=<its own valid JWT> and sends the literal frame `null`. JSON.parse("null") returns null without throwing, so the try/catch at server.js:378 does not fire; the very next expression evaluates msg.type and throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')". The listener is declared async, so the throw becomes a rejected promise that the ws EventEmitter discards, and Node 22 (the runtime in something2-backend-1) defaults to --unhandled-rejections=throw, turning it into an uncaught exception that exits the process. Reproduced locally on Node v22.19.0 with the identical listener shape: exit code 1 with that exact TypeError. No process-level unhandledRejection or uncaughtException handler exists anywhere in backend/src (grep finds only comments referring to the hazard), and ws.on("error") at server.js:374 does not catch it because this is not a transport error. The Express API is attached to the same http server (index.js:1394), so one 4-byte frame from any player drops every connected player and every in-flight HTTP request.

Proposed fix: Guard the envelope before dispatch: immediately after the JSON.parse try/catch at server.js:378 add `if (!msg || typeof msg !== "object" || Array.isArray(msg)) return;`. Additionally wrap the whole message body in a try/catch, mirroring the upgrade handler's `(async () => { ... })().catch(...)` pattern at server.js:114-147, so no future handler branch can escape as an unhandled rejection, and register a process-level unhandledRejection logger as a backstop.

Verification: With a valid player JWT: node -e "const W=require('ws');const s=new W('ws://localhost:13101/authority?token=<TOKEN>');s.on('open',()=>s.send('null'))". Currently expect docker logs something2-backend-1 to show the TypeError and the container to exit/restart, dropping every other socket; after the fix expect the frame to be ignored and the socket to stay open. confirmed in browser: from an admin session with a valid joined WS (world MerchantVerify), sent the literal 4-byte frame `null` via a raw WebSocket.send('null') (not JSON.stringify(null), the literal string). The socket closed immediately with code 1006 (abnormal closure). docker ps still reported something2-backend-1 as "Up" (its CMD is `tail -f /dev/null`, decoupled from the app), but `docker exec something2-backend-1 ps aux` showed only that tail process -- the nodemon/node src/index.js process that had been serving all prior requests was gone, and `ss -tlnp` inside the container showed nothing listening on the app port. GET /api/health failed with a connection error. The exact TypeError trace was not visible (docker logs returned empty for this container, consistent with the dev process being exec'd outside the container's own logging stream), but the process-death signature (open WS -> null frame -> 1006 close -> app process gone, container shell still alive) is exactly what the finding predicts. Backend was restarted via `docker compose exec -d backend npm run dev` and confirmed healthy again before continuing.

results.name: [F-011] P3 backend-api: The three generation-job routes and the four approve routes are near-verbatim copies th...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:718

Lens: dry · Source: static

Claim: The three generation-job routes and the four approve routes are near-verbatim copies that differ only in a kind string and a default frame count, and one copy has already drifted.

Failure scenario: POST /api/sprite-jobs (718), /api/entity-jobs (808) and /api/tile-jobs (869) are identical 20-line blocks apart from kind and the chosenFrames default (4 vs 1 vs 1), including the tier auto-select fallback and the sprite_sets INSERT — so the jobId validation the security finding calls for, or any concurrency cap on this CPU-bound work, must be written three times to be correct. The four approve routes have already drifted: POST /api/entity-types/:id/image clears sprite = NULL with a comment explaining that the atlas path otherwise keeps winning, while POST /api/tile-types/:id/image (904) leaves sprite populated; that is harmless only because resolveTileVisual gates on render_mode === animated rather than on sprite presence, so it is a trap waiting for the tile renderer to adopt the entity precedence rule. job_id handling also differs: three routes treat it as optional, /api/entity-types/:id/sprite (774) 404s without it.

Proposed fix: Extract one startGenerationJob({ subject, kind, defaultFrames, req, res }) helper for the three job routes and one approveGenerated({ table, mode, ... }) helper for the approve routes, so validation, tier fallback and the sprite/image precedence rule exist once. Make the tile image approval clear sprite the way the entity one does, so the two agree.

Verification: After extraction, POST each of the three job routes with a jobless payload and confirm identical validation behaviour; approve a tile image over an existing animated tile and confirm tile_types.sprite is NULL.

results.name: [F-010] P2 backend-api: generateWFC() has no caller anywhere outside its own unit tests, yet the tile_types.val...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/services/mapService.js:1-72

Lens: yagni · Source: static

Claim: generateWFC() has no caller anywhere outside its own unit tests, yet the tile_types.valid_neighbors column it is the sole consumer of is still a curated, required field in the Tile Types admin UI.

Failure scenario: generateWFC (mapService.js:1-72) and densityAt (mapService.js:337) have zero non-test references in backend/src or frontend/src; world generation goes through generateWorld/generateRegion instead. mapService.js:47 is the only read of validNeighbors in the codebase. TileTypesAdmin.jsx:583 still renders a full checkbox grid for valid_neighbors, POST/PUT /api/tile-types (index.js:467, 488) still persist it, and getTileTypesMap (index.js:91) still ships it to the client. So an admin who spends time curating adjacency rules for every tile type changes nothing about any generated map, and the UI gives no hint of that. The dead generator also keeps its own test suite green, so a change to hash2/globalValueNoise/worldConfig must keep code no product flow reaches passing.

Proposed fix: Decide the product question, then act on it: either delete generateWFC, densityAt, the valid_neighbors editor and (via migration) the column; or wire generateWorld to honour valid_neighbors so the admin input has an effect. Do not leave the field editable while nothing reads it.

Verification: Set valid_neighbors on two tile types so they are mutually exclusive, then POST /api/maps/generate and inspect the returned grid for adjacent occurrences of the two. Currently expect them adjacent (the rule is ignored).

results.name: [F-009] P2 backend-api: A 50 MB JSON/urlencoded body limit is installed globally, so it applies to every unauth...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:18

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: A 50 MB JSON/urlencoded body limit is installed globally, so it applies to every unauthenticated route, and no global rate limit exists — only /api/auth has one.

Failure scenario: express.json({ limit: "50mb" }) at index.js:18 runs as app-level middleware, before routing and before any auth guard, so it parses bodies for unauthenticated paths too. An unauthenticated client POSTs 50 MB of JSON to /api/health (or any path, including ones with no route); the body is buffered and parsed before the 404 is produced. The only rate limiter in the surface is authRateLimiter() inside auth/routes.js:13, scoped to register/login, and cors() is installed with no origin restriction (index.js:17), so this is reachable from any origin without credentials. A modest number of concurrent such requests drives backend heap growth; because the WS authority shares the process (index.js:1394), a heap exhaustion drops every connected player. No route in this surface needs 50 MB: the largest legitimate body is the map entity array in POST /api/maps/:id/entities.

Proposed fix: Drop the global limit to something small (e.g. 256kb) and apply a larger per-route limit only where it is needed, e.g. app.post("/api/maps/:id/entities", adminGuard, express.json({ limit: "10mb" }), handler). Add a modest global rate limiter in front of the router.

Verification: head -c 52000000 /dev/zero | tr "\0" "a" into a JSON string file, then run 20 concurrent unauthenticated `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @big.json http://localhost:13101/api/health` and watch the backend container RSS. Currently expect large RSS growth per in-flight request; after the fix expect HTTP 413 immediately. confirmed in browser (partial, by design -- the full 20-concurrent stress test was skipped to avoid destabilising the host per the audit brief): a single unauthenticated ~44MB JSON POST to /api/health (a route accepting no body) was fully buffered and parsed before the 404 was produced, and backend RSS jumped from ~37MiB to ~181MiB for that one request and did not settle within a few seconds. This proves the global pre-auth, pre-routing 50mb body limit and its per-request memory cost; the container stayed healthy throughout (no restart).

results.name: [F-008] P2 backend-api: creature_count has no server-side upper bound and the re-roll loop issues one round-tri...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:1118-1141

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: creature_count has no server-side upper bound and the re-roll loop issues one round-trip INSERT per creature and a full generateRegion() per placement attempt, so a large count ties the request and a DB connection up indefinitely.

Failure scenario: The Creatures field in MapsAdmin is <Input type="number" min="0"> with no max (MapsAdmin.jsx:79) and PUT /api/worlds/:id only clamps with Math.max(0, Math.floor(creature_count)) (index.js:1027). An admin typing 500000 and clicking Re-roll creatures makes index.js:1118 loop 500k times, each iteration calling generateRegion() for a 1x1 window up to 40 times (each of those rebuilds worldConfig and recomputes the whole coarse path lattice via collectPathCells), then issuing one individual INSERT per placed creature. The request has no timeout and never returns, holds a pool client for its duration, and grows world_creatures without limit — which the authority then loads into the world sim. POST /api/maps/generate (index.js:537) has the same class of gap: rows/cols default to 100 but are unvalidated, so {"rows":100000,"cols":100000} allocates a 10^10-cell grid and exhausts the heap.

Proposed fix: Clamp creature_count server-side in PUT /api/worlds/:id (e.g. 0..2000, 400 above it) and add a max to the MapsAdmin input; batch the placement INSERTs into a single multi-row statement; hoist worldConfig()/collectPathCells() out of the per-attempt path by sampling a pre-generated region instead of calling generateRegion() per candidate tile. Apply the same numeric clamp to rows/cols in POST /api/maps/generate.

Verification: PUT /api/worlds/:id with creature_count 200000 (expect 400 after the fix; currently 200), then POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures and time it. Currently expect no response; after the fix expect a 400 at the PUT. Confirmed in browser (Flow D arbitration sweep), PUT half only: PUT /api/worlds/:id with {"creature_count":200000} returned HTTP 200 and persisted creature_count=200000 with no validation. Did not additionally trigger POST .../creatures at that count -- per the finding's own text the re-roll loop would not return, and reproducing an indefinite hang was judged too costly for a verification check (same reasoning Flow B used for F-009's stress variant). Reset creature_count back to 0 immediately after to avoid leaving a live landmine for later test runs.

results.name: [F-007] P2 backend-api: Village create, village delete and creature re-roll each perform several dependent writ...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:1229-1258

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: Village create, village delete and creature re-roll each perform several dependent writes with no transaction, so a failure part-way leaves the world in a state the API cannot be asked to repair.

Failure scenario: POST /api/worlds/:id/villages runs INSERT villages, then insertVillageGuards, then seedBaseCatalog, then invalidateWorld as four independent statements on the shared pool. If seedBaseCatalog throws (constraint error, transient DB fault), the village row and its guards are already committed but the shop is empty; the client gets HTTP 500 "Failed to create village" and the admin retries — and the retry is rejected with 400 "village overlaps an existing village" from the phantom village they were never told exists. DELETE /api/worlds/:id/villages/:villageId (index.js:1265) and POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures (index.js:1097) have the same shape around the guard wipe: they DELETE every world_creatures row of type Village Guard and then re-insert them, so a failure between the two leaves the world with zero guards and no endpoint that re-derives them except another creature re-roll.

Proposed fix: Check out a client and wrap each of the three routes in BEGIN/COMMIT with ROLLBACK in catch and release in finally, exactly as POST /api/maps/:id/entities (index.js:579) already does — and move the connect() inside the try (see the P0 finding on the same pattern).

Verification: Point the backend at a pool whose merchant_stock INSERT fails, POST a village, then GET /api/worlds/:id/villages. Currently the village is listed despite the 500; after the fix the list should be unchanged.

results.name: [F-006] P2 backend-api: seedBaseCatalog() is called only at village creation, so item types added later never e...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:1256

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: seedBaseCatalog() is called only at village creation, so item types added later never enter any existing village merchant catalog and there is no re-seed endpoint.

Failure scenario: An admin creates village V in world W; seedBaseCatalog (index.js:1256) copies the item types that exist at that moment into merchant_stock. The admin then adds a new armour type. services/merchantStock.js fetchShop() reads merchant_stock only, and nothing ever re-runs the seed, so players trading at V never see the new armour — and every village created before the item existed is permanently missing it, while villages created afterwards have it. The only recovery is deleting and recreating the village (which cascades away its buyback rows) or a manual SQL insert.

Proposed fix: Add an idempotent re-seed: an admin route (or a call on item-type create) that inserts the missing base-catalog rows for every village, e.g. the existing SELECT-INSERT plus `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM merchant_stock ms WHERE ms.village_id = $2 AND ms.item_type_id = item_types.id)`, and a matching delete/price-refresh when an item type is removed or repriced.

Verification: Create a village, then create a new weapon item type with value > 0, then read the shop for that village and confirm the new weapon is absent. After the fix it should appear without recreating the village. Confirmed in browser (Flow D arbitration sweep): created village on world test4 (base catalog seeded from the item_types existing at that moment), then created a new weapon item type (id 76, value backfilled to 40 directly to isolate this claim from the separately-confirmed F-003 value-not-persisted bug) and confirmed SELECT count(*) FROM merchant_stock WHERE item_type_id=76 AND village_id=<village A> returns 0 -- the new weapon never reached the existing village's shop.

results.name: [F-005] P1 backend-api: Entity types are referenced by NAME (not id) in worlds.allowed_creature_types and world...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:239

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: Entity types are referenced by NAME (not id) in worlds.allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type, but PUT /api/entity-types/:id renames freely with no check on those references, silently orphaning them.

Failure scenario: A world has allowed_creature_types ["Goblin"] and creature_count 40. An admin renames the Goblin entity type to "Goblin Scout" in the Entity Types panel. PUT /api/entity-types/:id (index.js:239) updates the row with no referential check. The next POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures runs `SELECT ... FROM entity_types WHERE is_creature = true AND name = ANY($1::text[])` (index.js:1120) with the stale ["Goblin"], matches zero rows, skips the placement block, and returns HTTP 200 {"placed": 0}. The admin sees a success toast and a world with no creatures, with no error surfaced anywhere. The same name coupling applies to the hardcoded GUARD_TYPE = "Village Guard" literal (index.js:1177) used by three DELETE statements: renaming that entity type makes the re-roll `WHERE type <> $2` guard-sparing clause stop matching, so a re-roll wipes every village guard.

Proposed fix: Either block a rename that is referenced (check worlds.allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type, return 409 with the referencing worlds) or cascade it inside one transaction (UPDATE worlds SET allowed_creature_types, UPDATE world_creatures SET type). Longer term, key allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type on entity_types.id instead of name, and resolve GUARD_TYPE via faction = guard, which is how the authority already identifies guards (authority/creatures.js:66).

Verification: With a bounded world configured for one creature type: rename that entity type in the admin UI, then click Re-roll creatures and observe the response. Currently expect HTTP 200 with placed 0 and an empty map; after the fix expect a 409 on the rename or a re-roll that still places creatures. confirmed in browser: configured a bounded world with allowed_creature_types ["AuditFixtureBeast"] and creature_count 5; POST .../creatures placed 5 (baseline). Renamed the entity type to AuditFixtureBeastRenamed via PUT /api/entity-types/:id (200, no reference check). Re-rolling creatures on the same world then returned HTTP 200 {"placed":0} -- the exact silent-failure reproduced live.
