results.name: [F-004] P1 backend-api: PUT /api/worlds/:id stores entry_spawn as any object without checking it lands inside t...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:1032

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: PUT /api/worlds/:id stores entry_spawn as any object without checking it lands inside the world bounds, and chooseSpawn() only checks Number.isFinite, so an out-of-range spawn puts every first-time joiner inside the solid wall ring.

Failure scenario: A world is 24x24 tiles (valid coordinates 0..2400 px). In MapsAdmin the entry-spawn inputs (MapsAdmin.jsx:96-98) are plain number fields with no min/max, so an admin typing 99999 saves entry_spawn {x:99999,y:99999}. index.js:1032 accepts any object and writes it to jsonb unvalidated. On join, mapService.chooseSpawn() (line 588) only tests Number.isFinite and returns it verbatim; authority/server.js:206 uses it with no clamp. stampBounds() marks every tile outside the rectangle as map_wall, so every player joining that entry world for the first time materialises deep inside impassable wall with no in-game way out. The same gap lets a bounds shrink via PUT strand already-persisted world_players positions outside the new ring.

Proposed fix: In PUT /api/worlds/:id validate entry_spawn.x/entry_spawn.y are finite numbers inside (0, width*100) x (0, height*100) and return 400 otherwise; when nextW/nextH shrink, also clamp or clear entry_spawn and any world_players rows now outside the ring. Mirror the min/max on the MapsAdmin inputs.

Verification: In the browser: set a bounded world as entry, type 99999 into both entry-spawn fields, Save (expect 400 after the fix; currently 200). Then join that world as a fresh player and confirm whether the avatar appears inside the wall and cannot move in any direction. confirmed in browser: set entry_spawn to {x:99999,y:99999} on a 24x24 bounded world via PUT /api/worlds/:id (200, no validation error), then joined that world over a live WebSocket as a fresh player account and sent 41 movement input frames over ~2s. The player spawned at (99999,99999) and never moved by even 1px across 50 subsequent state frames -- confirmed stuck, not merely theoretical.

results.name: [F-003] P1 backend-api: item_types.value (an item gold worth) is never written by POST or PUT /api/item-types a...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:360-370

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: item_types.value (an item gold worth) is never written by POST or PUT /api/item-types and has no admin UI field, so every item type created after the merchant migration is permanently worth 0 gold.

Failure scenario: An admin creates a new sword via the Item Types panel. The INSERT at index.js:360 omits the `value` column, so it takes the migration default 0 (backend/migrations/1714440032000_merchant_stock.js:6, notNull default 0). services/merchantStock.js:30 seeds a village base catalog with `WHERE category IN (weapon,armor) AND value > 0`, so the new sword can never appear in any merchant catalog; authority/trade.js:91 reads the same column for the sell price, so a player who loots it sells it for sellPriceFor(0) = 0 gold. There is no API route and no form field that can set `value` — the only remedy is a manual SQL UPDATE. Every item type shipped through the admin UI since that migration is affected.

Proposed fix: Add `value` to the INSERT and UPDATE column lists in POST/PUT /api/item-types, validate it in validateItemType() as a non-negative finite integer (the same shape as the existing stamina_cost check at index.js:318), and add the field to ItemTypesAdmin.jsx. Backfill existing zero-value rows using the same expressions the migration used.

Verification: curl -s http://localhost:13101/api/item-types | jq '[.[] | {name, value}]' and confirm every row created through the admin UI has value 0; then create an item type via POST /api/item-types with {"value": 25} and confirm the returned row still reports value 0. confirmed in browser: POST /api/item-types with {"value":25} (admin bearer token, live stack) returned 201 with the stored row reporting value:0; the Item Types create/edit form (ItemTypesAdmin.jsx) has no value field to set it either.

results.name: [F-002] P1 backend-api: The three unauthenticated job-status proxies interpolate the raw :jobId path param into...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:745

Lens: security · Source: static

Claim: The three unauthenticated job-status proxies interpolate the raw :jobId path param into a URL path, so an encoded ../ traverses out of /jobs/ and reaches arbitrary GET endpoints on the internal sprite-gen service.

Failure scenario: An unauthenticated caller requests GET /api/entity-jobs/..%2F..%2Fopenapi.json. Express decodes the param to "../../openapi.json"; spriteGen.getJob() builds fetch("http://sprite-gen:8100/jobs/../../openapi.json"); the URL parser normalises it to http://sprite-gen:8100/openapi.json. Confirmed live against localhost:13101 on 2026-07-24: the response was sprite-gen full OpenAPI schema (HTTP 200), and GET /api/tile-jobs/..%2Fcapability returned the host hardware profile. sprite-gen is not otherwise reachable from outside the compose network, and none of these three routes requires a token, so the public API is acting as an open unauthenticated GET proxy into the private service segment. Impact today is internal-API and host-capability disclosure; it becomes remote-trigger the moment sprite-gen gains any GET endpoint with a side effect.

Proposed fix: Validate :jobId against the job-id format before use (e.g. reject anything not matching /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ with 400) in all three proxies — /api/sprite-jobs/:jobId (745), /api/entity-jobs/:jobId (833), /api/tile-jobs/:jobId (894) — and encodeURIComponent it inside services/spriteGen.js:24 so the escape is closed at both layers. Decide separately whether these three routes should require auth at all.

Verification: curl -s "http://localhost:13101/api/tile-jobs/..%2Fcapability" with no Authorization header. Currently returns sprite-gen capability JSON with HTTP 200; after the fix expect HTTP 400 and no proxied body. Confirmed in browser (Flow D arbitration sweep): curl -s "http://localhost:13101/api/tile-jobs/..%2Fcapability" with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 with the sprite-gen host capability JSON, exactly as claimed.

results.name: [F-001] P0 backend-api: POST /api/maps/:id/entities and POST /api/maps/:id/generate-entities call `await pool.c...
results.description_html:
Status: fixed

Location: backend/src/index.js:580

Lens: user-logic · Source: static

Claim: POST /api/maps/:id/entities and POST /api/maps/:id/generate-entities call `await pool.connect()` OUTSIDE their try block, so a connection-acquisition failure escapes the async handler as an unhandledRejection and kills the whole Node process.

Failure scenario: The Postgres container restarts (or max_connections is briefly exhausted) while an admin saves map entities. `pool.connect()` at index.js:580 rejects before the try block is entered; Express 4.18 does not catch async handler rejections, so the rejection reaches the process. Proven locally on Node 22.19 by injecting a pool whose connect() rejects: the HTTP request never gets a response (client aborts) and, with no unhandledRejection listener installed, the process terminates with a fatal uncaught-rejection trace pointing at index.js:580. Because attachAuthority() binds the WS authority to this same server (index.js:1394), the exit drops every connected player mid-session. index.js:653 has the identical shape.

Proposed fix: Move `const client = await pool.connect()` inside the try block in both routes (initialise `let client = null` outside, and guard `client?.release()` in finally), matching the hardening already applied to backend/src/auth/middleware.js:35-43 for the same failure class. Consider also adding a process-level unhandledRejection handler that logs and responds rather than exiting.

Verification: Run the repo-local probe: require backend/src/index.js, __setPool({ query: async () => ({rows:[{token_version:1,role:"admin"}]}), connect: async () => { throw new Error("boom"); } }), then POST /api/maps/1/entities with a valid admin bearer token. Expect (current) process exit with an uncaught rejection at index.js:580; after the fix, expect HTTP 500 and the process still alive.

results.name: Attack VFX Slice E — admin CRUD for vfx_effects and binding dropdowns
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · admin CRUD + live preview + binding dropdowns + orphan guard on rename AND delete; commit 2f1c097

Deliver the 'fully data-driven, tunable without a deploy' half of decision 2.

DEPENDS ON: Slice C (the schema is only complete once particle columns exist).

Sequenced LAST deliberately — and it paid off: the columns this screen edits needed no changes, because drawing had already validated them across B, C and D.

SCOPE
- ✅ Backend CRUD for vfx_effects behind requireAdmin, following the tile-types / entity-types route patterns.
- ✅ Admin registry screen (list + create/edit/delete), following the existing admin pattern.
- ✅ Live preview in the editor, delegating to the SAME pure particle function the renderer uses.
- ✅ Binding dropdowns in the Items admin, reading the live library, with an explicit "(kind default)" option so a binding can be removed.
- ✅ Guard against orphaning: renaming or deleting a bound effect is refused with the bindings named.

TESTS
- ✅ CRUD routes reject a missing/non-admin token.
- ✅ Enum and particle_count validation rejected on write, before the statement.
- ✅ Delete/rename of a bound effect surfaces the warning, across both binding tables.

DONE WHEN
An effect can be retuned live in the admin and the change shows in game without a deploy. — the wiring is proven (the admin invalidates the very cache key the running game reads, asserted against both files); the end-to-end claim itself is UNVERIFIED, no browser pass.

results.name: Attack VFX Slice C — impacts event, particle system, element tinting
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · particle columns + cap enforced on write, impacts event, deterministic particles, element tinting; commit 2d51f88

Make a hit read as a hit. This is where particles pay off.

DEPENDS ON: Slice B. (Built first — see SOMET-159.)

SCOPE
- ✅ Migration: particle_* columns on vfx_effects (count, spread, speed, gravity, lifetime_ms, size).
- ✅ Authority: frame.impacts = [{ t:'c:88', x, y, v:'spark_fire', el:'fire' }], omitted entirely from frames with nothing to report, as detonations already are.
- ✅ Client: particle rendering. particlesAt(fx, progress) is a PURE function of progress and a per-effect seed.
- ✅ Element tinting — off the effective element, not the catalog's static one. A bare magic weapon converts to physical (Magic Stones replace semantics), and a socketed stone decides the element per swing, so a static per-element binding would have been wrong in both directions.

PERFORMANCE
- ✅ Hard cap on total live particles with oldest-first eviction.
- ✅ particle_count validated on write (CHECK ≤ 64), verified rejected against the live database.

TESTS
- ✅ Particle determinism: same seed → same positions.
- ✅ Cap enforcement under a burst of simultaneous impacts.
- ✅ Authority: impacts lists exactly the damaged targets, and is absent when nothing was hit.

DONE WHEN
A hit sparks in the element's colour, and a crowded fight holds framerate. — cap and determinism proven by test; the in-world look and framerate are still unviewed (browser pass outstanding).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-attack-vfx-design.md

results.name: Attack VFX Slice B — full shape vocabulary, all 22 weapons bound, miss feedback
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · 4 shapes, 12 effect rows, 22/22 weapons bound, miss feedback; commit 7b0b5a3

Widen the proven spine from slice A until every weapon reads as itself.

DEPENDS ON: Slice A.

SCOPE
- Renderer: implement the remaining shapes — line, ring, burst, bolt (arc already done in A).
- Author and seed effect rows covering the 12 melee and 10 projectile weapons. Weapons differ by real geometry: reach 70..200, arc_width 0.5..2.0, so follows_weapon effects read differently per weapon without one row each.
- Bind all 22 weapons via item_types.vfx.
- Miss feedback: the server already knows whether an attack connected; frame.attacks carries hit:false. Client plays the weapon's 'miss' binding instead of 'attack'.
- Kind-level fallback resolution: binding -> kind default (melee -> generic slash, projectile -> generic bolt) -> nothing. This exists so a weapon added later in the Items admin with no binding renders plain-but-visible rather than invisible, which would look exactly like the bug this epic fixes.

TESTS
- ✅ Fallback resolution order (bound / unbound / unresolvable name).
- ✅ Authority: hit:false on a whiff, and the paired case — a swing that connects carries the attack effect.
- ✅ Each shape renders without throwing on degenerate input (zero reach, zero arc, zero width, NaN direction).

DONE WHEN
Every weapon looks distinct in a real world, and a whiff reads as a whiff rather than as a dropped input. — data and rendering verified by test and by query; the in-world look is still unviewed (browser pass outstanding).

results.name: Attack VFX Slice A — vfx_effects table + attacks event + melee arc renderer
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · shipped in 58c769c…fb81100; 14 backend + 19 client VFX tests pass

Thinnest end-to-end path: proves the protocol shape, schema expressiveness and render timing together, while they are still cheap to change. Melee only, one seeded effect, no admin screen, no particles.

SCOPE
- Migration: vfx_effects table, GEOMETRY columns only (name unique, shape, color, width, duration_ms, ease, fade, follows_weapon). CHECK constraints on shape and ease, in the style of item_types.element.
- Migration: item_types.vfx jsonb (bindings: moment -> effect name). Seed one effect ('sweep_heavy') and bind it to one melee weapon.
- Authority: world.attack() exposes the attack descriptor it already computes. Stash + clear per tick exactly like pendingDetonations, and ride the existing state frame as frame.attacks — no new message type.
frame.attacks = [{ a:'p:1', v:'sweep_heavy', x, y, nx, ny, reach, arc, hit }]
Effect names are resolved SERVER-side; the client never needs the weapon catalog.
- API: GET /api/vfx-effects returning the library.
- Client: new pure core/vfx.js following the blasts.js precedent (canvas-free, unit-testable under vitest node env): addEffects / pruneEffects / effectProgress. pruneEffects returns a NEW array.
- Client: RenderSystem.drawVfx() pass after the depth-sorted entity pass, before the HUD. Draws the 'arc' shape only.
- Effect defs handed to Game the same way tileTypes/entityTypes already are.

TESTS
- vfx.js: lifetime, pruning, eased progress.
- Migration test in the style of migration_tile_prompts.test.js.
- Authority: attacks carries correct geometry for a melee arc.

DONE WHEN
A halberd swing is visible in a real world (browser-verified, not just green tests).

results.name: Redis state layer for the Node authority
results.description_html:
Deferred out of slice 3b-3b (2026-07-19). Ammo consumption was proposed as the first Redis consumer and rejected: it would have added a third copy of the state (memory to Redis to Postgres) rather than removing one, and the write volume it would relieve does not exist (a sling at 0.50s cooldown is 2 writes/sec per shooting player).

What would actually justify Redis — the questions this epic must answer:

  • Sharding the authority across multiple Node processes: today one process owns all world state in memory, so Redis buys nothing over that map. Multi-process authority is what makes shared state necessary.
  • Restart recovery without replaying Postgres.
  • What lives in Redis vs Postgres, and which is authoritative on disagreement.
  • Behaviour when Redis is unavailable — degrade to Postgres, or refuse writes?
  • Flush semantics: any write-behind cache can refund or lose player-visible resources on a crash. This is the same class of bug as the mirrored autoLoot flag fixed in the 3b-2b fast-follows.

Current state: Redis is already provisioned in compose/docker-compose.yml (redis:7-alpine, appendonly on) but wired only to the frozen game-engine service. The Node authority has no client and no REDIS_URL.

Related: the connected-chunked-world epic (SOMET-53), which is what most plausibly forces multi-process authority.

results.name: DEV-AUTH: reloading the page mints a brand-new anonymous user
results.description_html: <p><b>Found during Slice 3b-2b browser verification.</b> Pre-existing, unrelated to loot, but it silently invalidates a whole class of testing.</p><p>`fetchDevToken` is called WITHOUT a `user_id` (Game.js:227 / Something2.jsx:329), so every page reload issues a token for a fresh anonymous user. The player loses their identity — and therefore their entire account-wide inventory and equipment — on every refresh.</p><p><b>Why it matters beyond the obvious:</b> any "does X persist across reload?" check is meaningless, because the reloaded session is a different account. The 3b-2b verification had to work around this by explicitly reconnecting as the same user_id to confirm server-side persistence. Anyone testing persistence through the UI will get a false negative and may "fix" a bug that does not exist.</p><p>Fix: persist the dev user id (localStorage or similar) and pass it to `fetchDevToken` on reconnect. Related: <b>SOMET-78</b> (admin API endpoints unauthenticated) — both are dev-auth gaps that must be closed before anything ships beyond dev.</p>
results.description_stripped:
Found during Slice 3b-2b browser verification. Pre-existing, unrelated to loot, but it silently invalidates a whole class of testing.

`fetchDevToken` is called WITHOUT a `user_id` (Game.js:227 / Something2.jsx:329), so every page reload issues a token for a fresh anonymous user. The player loses their identity — and therefore their entire account-wide inventory and equipment — on every refresh.

Why it matters beyond the obvious: any "does X persist across reload?" check is meaningless, because the reloaded session is a different account. The 3b-2b verification had to work around this by explicitly reconnecting as the same user_id to confirm server-side persistence. Anyone testing persistence through the UI will get a false negative and may "fix" a bug that does not exist.

Fix: persist the dev user id (localStorage or similar) and pass it to `fetchDevToken` on reconnect. Related: SOMET-78 (admin API endpoints unauthenticated) — both are dev-auth gaps that must be closed before anything ships beyond dev.

results.name: SECURITY: admin API endpoints are unauthenticated
results.description_html:
Surfaced by the Slice 3b-2a final review. Pre-existing and project-wide — backend/src/index.js registers only cors() + body parsers; there is no auth middleware anywhere. So /api/entity-types, /api/tile-types and now /api/item-types + POST /api/players/:userId/items are open to anyone.

Why it matters more now: this is the first slice where an open admin endpoint has direct combat consequences — anyone can author a weapon with arbitrary damage/cooldown, or grant any item to any account. It defeats the 'server owns all item state' guarantee at the HTTP layer even though the WebSocket layer is airtight (ids-only, ownership validated).

Not caused by this slice and the spec never mentioned admin auth, so it was left out of scope — but it should not ship beyond dev unaddressed.

results.name: Fast-follow: equip->attack race (equip is now async write-through)
results.description_html:
Done · 2026-08-12 · optimistic mutation + whole-map rollback; 6 ordering tests, mutation-checked; commit 12fe50f

Found by the Slice 3b-2a Task 9 review. Newly introduced by 3b-2a (3b-1's equip{weaponId} was synchronous in-memory and therefore atomic; the new equip{itemId,slot} awaits DB write-through).

Race: ws.on('message', async ...) does not await the previous handler, and items.js equip() mutates inv.equipment only AFTER its DB round-trips. A client firing equip then attack back-to-back can have the attack resolve with the PREVIOUS weapon. A narrower window also exists mid-equip during the toClear loop (partially-cleared paper-doll visible to a concurrent read).

Confirmed mechanism (2026-08-12): the ammo-free attack path is fully synchronous and is NOT placed on ws._opChain, while equip/unequip are — so an attack frame arriving mid-equip ran immediately against stale equipment.

Impact: UX inconsistency only — NOT an exploit. Verified by review: no path to stats for an unowned/fabricated item (all stats resolve from server-held p.inv + the item_types catalog), and no cooldown bypass (_attackCd gating is weapon-identity independent).

Fix: in items.js equip()/unequip(), mutate inv.equipment optimistically BEFORE awaiting the DB write, rolling back on failure. (Out of Task 9's file scope, hence deferred.)

Minor sibling: server.js unequip doesn't check r.ok/reply with an error on rejection, unlike equip. — Already resolved by the equipOrUnequip unification (F-020 / SOMET-200); verified, no change needed.

results.name: Map preview on world select (iso minimap + animation)
results.description_html:
When a world is selected in the World Browser (/game-something2) but not yet entered, the blank game area shows an isometric minimap PREVIEW of that world: terrain diamonds colored by tile type + small dots for placed objects. Diamonds reveal (stagger/fade) on selection change, then the camera gently drifts. Entering the world swaps the preview for the real game canvas.

Design (brainstorm 2026-07-15):
- Projection: isometric diamonds, reusing the game's iso projection (frontend/src/games/something2/src/js/core/iso.js) scaled to fit the map in the preview box.
- Animation: reveal (per-diamond alpha, staggered by distance from center) then gentle idle drift (slow sinusoidal camera pan).
- Content: terrain tiles + object/entity dots (two fetches: map data + entities).
- Perf: bake the fully-revealed map to an offscreen canvas; idle drift blits the offscreen with a translated camera instead of redrawing ~10k diamonds/frame. Reveal phase redraws for its short duration only.

Integration: in Something2.jsx game-view area, selectedMapId && !isPlaying -> MapPreview; isPlaying -> existing game canvas; nothing selected -> hint.

Subtasks: (1) mapPreviewRenderer pure module + iso-fit; (2) MapPreview.jsx component (canvas + rAF reveal/drift + data hooks); (3) integrate into Something2 + tile-color plumbing. Verify in browser.

results.name: Dynamic entity sprite generation (hardware-aware)
results.description_html:
Foundation for on-demand, per-entity pixelart sprite generation whose quality/speed tier is chosen automatically from detected hardware. Generation is ALWAYS available; a CUDA GPU is a TIER switch, not an on/off gate.

Principles (from brainstorm 2026-07-15):
- Rectangles are the DEFAULT render mode -> maps generate fast; images/sprites are opt-in PER ENTITY TYPE.
- Real diffusion runs on CPU too (slow; user will wait). GPU auto-accelerates AND raises fidelity.
- Trigger surface = the entity editor (frontend/src/games/something2/EntityTypesAdmin.jsx + useSprites.js).

Current gap: sprite-gen app/config.py reads DEVICE from env (default 'cpu') with NO auto-detection; /health exposes device but nothing selects a recipe by hardware.

Tier behavior:
- GPU tier: device=cuda, ControlNet pose-guided directional frames, higher step count, SDXL/SD-Turbo -> consistent pixelart set.
- CPU tier: lighter backend + low steps + reduced/single frame -> real diffusion, just slow.

Data flow: entity editor -> POST /api/sprite-jobs (tier auto from capability) -> Node bridge -> sprite-gen /generate (recipe by tier) -> async job (fast GPU / slow CPU) -> poll /api/sprite-jobs/:id -> approve -> /api/entity-types/:id/sprite links atlas -> game loads image -> renders per entity renderMode (default rect).

Tasks: (1) auto device+capability detection; (2) tiered generation recipe; (3) Node bridge surfaces capability + tolerates long CPU jobs; (4) entity-editor capability banner + per-entity generate + renderMode control.

Relationship to SOMET-38: this is the generation FOUNDATION that SOMET-42/43 consume. Those two are no longer 'GPU-blocked' (generation works on CPU too), re-scoped to depend on this epic.

results.name: Map generator v2: structured layout + per-object render modes
results.description_html:
Goal: generate maps that read like a hand-authored top-down overworld (reference: pixel-art forest with winding trails, forest clumps, clearings), and let each object type render as a colored rectangle, a static image, or an animated moving sprite.

Two threads:

THREAD 1 — Structured generation (CPU-friendly, land now)
Replace the single WFC pass (backend/src/services/mapService.js generateWFC) which only produces per-tile adjacency noise, with a layered generateWorld pipeline:
1. Biome field — low-frequency value/simplex noise -> contiguous regions (deep forest / field / dirt) mapped to tile types. Fixes the speckle problem.
2. Path carving — pick clearing anchors, connect with a cost-weighted walk/A* over the biome grid, stamp dirt -> winding trails.
3. Object density field — trees/rocks placed by a density map (biome x noise) so forests clump and clearings stay open. Replaces the flat per-tile chance roll in Map.generateEntities and backend /generate-entities.
4. Clearings & landmarks — N deliberate low-density spots; optional POI markers.
Output contract unchanged: still a rows x cols tile-type grid + entity list, so DB schema / API / frontend loader are untouched. generateWFC kept as optional texture option or retired.
Rejected alternatives: keep WFC + bolt-on structure passes (WFC fights large-scale structure); overlapping-model/pattern WFC (overkill, hard to control).

THREAD 2 — Per-object render modes (code lands now, sprite assets later)
